new_roles.title: Director, Continuous Improvement
new_roles.description:
Join Reynolds Consumer Products…and Drive Your Career across a world of opportunities!
 
 
We currently have an opportunity for a
**Continuous Improvement Director**
at our
**Lake Forest Corporate Headquarters**
plant in
**Lake Forest, IL**
. This position will support our Malvern, AK, Louisville, KY, Bellwood, VA, and Wheeling plants with up to 75% travel. This position could also be located at our Malvern, AK, or Louisville, KY locations.
 
 
**Responsibilities**
The
**Continuous Improvement Director**
will be responsible for driving continuous improvement and demonstrating maximum efficiency and delivery productivity for the entire Business Unit (BU) with disciplined process and world class measures. The Continuous Improvement Director will be a key creator of the Continuous Improvement and Digital Factory strategy for the BU, leveraging best practices across our manufacturing sites as we continue to develop our Boundless operating system across Reynolds Consumer Products (RCP). We embrace and accept individual experiences and backgrounds to achieve a diverse and inclusive workplace.
 
 
**You Will Have the Opportunity to Make Great Things Happen!**
**Strategy & Business Transformation**

* Develop plans, schedules, and budgets for tactical projects to improve existing processes; ensure cost-benefit evaluation for all assigned projects are completed to define potential financial, business and industry impacts of initiatives.
* Support the business leaders in the development of intermediate and long-term CI strategies to assure delivery of the projected CI Saving Budget.
* Create the digital manufacturing (IoT) strategy and coach plant teams on implementation and sustained performance enhancement as a result.
* Advise and influence senior leadership on business transformation topics that include organizational effectiveness, performance results, and change management in the terms of complexity and impact on the business.

**Continuous Improvement & Operational Excellence**

* Manage a CI Savings Budget across the Business Unit that represents an achievable value to deliver back to the business.
* Act as the subject matter expert for the core pillars of the Boundless operating system to assure sustained results, including assisting in training and plant acclimation to the new PEPS process.
* Drive the improvement of processes and systems in the plants and implement programs that will have continuing long-term benefits.
* Continuously evaluate and measure program or initiative performance and progress against goals and serve as a change agent within the organization.
* Monitor existing processes to make sure they continue to perform at optimal levels of efficiency achieving lowered conversion costs year-over-year.
* Direct all CI activities to include Kaizen events in 5S, SMED, TPM, VSM, PDCA or equivalent, A3 Problem Solving.
* Ensure adherence to Lean Methodology, including Kaizen, 5S, Standard Work, Daily Management, Layered Audit Process and Business Plan development to eliminate waste.
* Confer with management, engineering, and other staff regarding manufacturing capabilities, production schedules, and other considerations to facilitate production process improvements.

**Leadership & Talent Development**

* Effectively lead, manage, develop, coach, and evaluate team members and associates at various levels of experience.
* Develop and deliver Lean Training at all levels of the organization while driving Operational Excellence standards.

**You Will Love It Here If…**

* You listen, learn, and evolve
* You thrive in a fast-paced environment
* You put safety first, always
* You are passionate about collaboration, teamwork, and achieving shared goals
* You believe in treating all people with respect, operating ethically, and growing a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace
* You are committed to improving our impact on local communities and creating positive experiences

**Qualifications**
**Education/Experience**
**Required**

* BA/BS degree in Business, Supply Chain or related field.
* 10+ years of related professional Manufacturing with experience in Continuous Improvement and Operations.
* 3+ years in a leadership role focused on continuous improvement or operational excellence.

**Preferred**

* MBA or other advanced degree a plus.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt strongly preferred.
* Previous experience with Automation and SAP strongly preferred.

**Knowledge/Skills/Abilities**

* Proficient in MS Office with advanced Excel Skills.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including presentation skills and the ability to communicate and influence at all levels within the organization.
* Self-directed with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment with multiple accountabilities and multiple internal customers.
* Strong analytical skills as well as organizational skills with high attention to detail.
* Solid project management capabilities with the ability to organize and manage multiple projects simultaneously from origin through execution.
* Ability to work a flexible schedule during key business deadlines.
* Must be team oriented with the ability to work on high collaboration and performance teams.

**Competencies**

* Results Driven – Ability to focus on organizational growth, financial performance and achieving results.
* Critical Decision Maker – Clear, critical thinker that engages in thoughtful, data-driven decisions and has the ability to summarize and draw appropriate conclusions from complex data.
* Strategic Orientation – Ability to balance short-term goals with long-term organizational and functional strategic priorities.
* Innovative Thinking – A forward thinker who offers new, creative and often unconventional thoughts, opinions and methods for solution generation and problem solving.
* People Leadership – Ability to develop employees through coaching and feedback and holds team members accountable through modeling appropriate behavior.
* Compelling Communication – Effective written and verbal communicator that clearly and succinctly conveys information across all levels.

Want to know more? Check out our website or connect with us on LinkedIn!
 
 
**Apply today to join a fast-growing innovative company!**
Not a good fit but know someone who is? Please refer them!
 
 
**No unsolicited recruiter or agency inquiries, please.**
RCP affords equal employment opportunities to applicants without regard to race, color, religion, age, disability status, sex, marital status, protected veteran status, pregnancy, national origin, genetics, genetic information, parental status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local law. RCP conforms to the spirit as well as to the letter of all applicable laws and regulations.
 
 
**Posted Salary Range**
USD $144,100.00 - USD $214,350.00 /A
 
 
**Bonus Eligibility**
Role is eligible for 25% annual incentive provided the business meets financial goals and the individual meets their performance goals, subject to plan administration guidelines.

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
**Job Title**
Director, Operational Excellence
 
 
**Agency**
Texas A&M University
 
 
**Department**
Strategy and Business Services
 
 
**Proposed Minimum Salary**
Commensurate
 
 
**Job Location**
College Station, Texas
 
 
**Job Type**
Staff
 
 
**Job Description**
**A Glimpse of the Job**
The Director, Operational Excellence provides strategic leadership and oversight for the Operational Excellence program. Directs the development and implementation of division-wide process improvement strategies, methodologies, governance frameworks, and performance measures that enhance operational effectiveness and service delivery. Leads a centralized Operational Excellence function while providing strategic guidance and oversight to embedded Operational Excellence resources across multiple divisions. Partners with senior leaders to identify opportunities for process optimization, organizational effectiveness, service improvements, and change initiatives that advance the university's mission and strategic priorities.
 
 
**Essential Duties**
**Operational Excellence Strategy, Governance & Leadership**

* Develops and executes the strategic vision, goals, and operating model for the Operational Excellence function
* Establishes governance structures, methodologies, standards, tools, and performance metrics for operational excellence initiatives
* Provides leadership and direction for division-wide continuous improvement efforts and organizational effectiveness programs
* Ensures alignment of priorities with institutional strategic objectives and administrative service goals
* Evaluates organizational performance and identifies opportunities to improve effectiveness, efficiency, service quality, and resource utilization

**Leadership of Operational Excellence Workforce**

* Provides oversight, coaching, and professional development for Operational Excellence staff, including analysts and embedded resources
* Establishes workforce strategies, competency models, career pathways, and development programs for staff
* Promotes consistent application of process improvement methodologies, analytical approaches, and change management practices across all teams
* Fosters collaboration and knowledge sharing among central and embedded Operational Excellence resources
* Monitors workload distribution, resource allocation, and organizational capacity to support strategic initiatives

**Consulting & Organizational Effectiveness**

* Serves as a trusted advisor to executive and administrative leadership on process improvement, organizational effectiveness, change management, and service enhancement strategies
* Leads the assessment of complex operational challenges and facilitates the development of sustainable solutions
* Oversees high-impact improvement initiatives across administrative and operational functions
* Facilitates executive-level discussions and cross-functional collaboration to remove barriers and improve organizational performance
* Recommends strategic operational changes supported by data, analysis, and stakeholder engagement

**Project Intake, Prioritization & Portfolio Management**

* Establishes and manages project intake and prioritization processes for Operational Excellence initiatives
* Evaluates requests for support and aligns resources based on organizational priorities, risks, and anticipated impact
* Monitors the progress, outcomes, and performance of projects and initiatives
* Provides executive reporting regarding project portfolios, organizational improvements, and return-on-investment measures
* Ensures appropriate coordination among stakeholders, project teams, and embedded Operational Excellence resources

**Stakeholder Engagement, Change Leadership & Communication**

new_roles.title: Director of Operational Excellence $25K Sign On and $10K Relocation
new_roles.description:
Pay Range:$65.73 - $92.22 $25K Sign On and $10K Relocation for qualified hire!
 
 
The Director of Operational Excellence leads SEARHC’s improvement function, translating annual operating plan priorities into measurable, sustainable operational results. Reporting directly to the System Director of Enterprise Portfolio & Organizational Excellence, the Director supervises Associate Program Managers, Program Managers, and Senior Program Managers, develops improvement and change capabilities, balances team assignments and capacity, and oversees delivery quality and benefits measurement. This hands-on leader personally leads selected complex transformations and partners with executive sponsors and operational owners to diagnose problems, redesign processes, implement change, and sustain results. The Senior Program Manager level expands advanced program leadership capacity while the Director remains accountable for the function and continues direct involvement in transformational projects. The Director works with the PMO through one integrated portfolio and common reporting approach. The System Director retains enterprise direction and executive alignment; operational sponsors retain accountability for operational decisions, resources, and sustained performance.
 
 
SEARHC is a non-profit health consortium which serves the health interests of the residents of Southeast Alaska. We see our employees as our strongest assets. It is our priority to further their development and our organization by aiding in their professional advancement.
 
 
Working at SEARHC is more than a job, it’s a fulfilling career. We offer generous benefits, including retirement, paid time off, paid parental leave, health insurance, dental, and vision benefits, life insurance and long and short-term disability, and more.
 
 
**Key Essential Functions And Accountabilities Of The Job**

* Leads the Operational Excellence team and translates approved annual operating plan priorities into a coordinated improvement work plan; personally leads selected highly complex efforts while maintaining capacity for staff leadership and development.
* Integrates related improvement work across functions and operational owners; develops coherent transformation approaches, resolves cross-workstream dependencies, and coordinates supporting projects with the PMO through shared portfolio processes.
* Advises sponsors on competing approaches, sequencing, risks, and tradeoffs; facilitates difficult cross-functional decisions and escalates resource and priority decisions through established governance without assuming executive approval authority.
* Synthesizes complex operational, quality, service, and financial information with specialist partners; establishes credible baselines and benefits measures, examines performance variation, and evaluates outcomes, unintended effects, and sustained benefits.
* Assigns improvement work, balances team capacity, and oversees plans, milestones, risks, dependencies, and delivery quality within approved priorities and resources; partners with the PMO on common reporting and escalates capacity and priority tradeoffs to the System Director.
* Leads change-impact assessment, stakeholder alignment, readiness, and adoption planning for complex transformations; partners on communication and training and verifies that new practices are used across affected operations.
* Leads advanced performance diagnosis, workflow and operating-model redesign, structured testing, and implementation; establishes standard work, measurement ownership, review routines, and transition plans with operational owners to sustain results.
* Develops executive-level updates, governance materials, and strategic implementation reporting for leaders and decision-making bodies.
* Supervises, coaches, and develops improvement professionals at the Associate Program Manager, Program Manager, and Senior Program Manager levels; establishes role-appropriate performance expectations, evaluates performance, supports recruitment and onboarding, and builds reusable improvement and change methods to strengthen team capability and consistency.
* Demonstrates SEARHC’s values and supports work that advances the organization’s mission, vision, strategic plan, and operating plan.
* Other duties as assigned

Supervisory Responsibilities
 
 
This position reports directly to the System Director of Enterprise Portfolio & Organizational Excellence and directly supervises improvement professionals at the Associate Program Manager, Program Manager, and Senior Program Manager levels. Responsibilities include staff performance management, coaching and development, assignments, workload balancing, and delivery oversight in accordance with organizational policies. Senior Program Managers provide technical coaching and program leadership; the Director retains personnel and assignment authority across all levels. The System Director retains enterprise direction, executive alignment, and escalation of enterprise priority and resource decisions.
 
 
**Additional Details**
**Education, Certifications, and Licenses Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business administration, public health, nursing, or a related field
* Equivalent combination of education and relevant healthcare, operational improvement, program management, or project management experience may be considered in lieu of a degree
* Master’s degree in business administration, healthcare administration, public health, or a related field preferred
* Project Management Professional (PMP), Lean Six Sigma, change management, or similar improvement methodology training/certification preferred

**Experience Required**

* Six to eight or more years of experience in healthcare operations, program management, project management, quality improvement, or operational improvement, including independent leadership of complex, ambiguous, enterprise-wide improvement programs with measurable and sustained results
* Experience advising executive sponsors, integrating changes across multiple operational owners, facilitating consequential cross-functional decisions, and supervising and developing professional staff
* Demonstrated advanced expertise in performance diagnosis, process redesign, change adoption, benefits measurement, and sustainment across complex healthcare operations, with experience managing staff performance, assignments, and workload

**Knowledge of**

* Healthcare operations, workflow design, and advanced performance improvement principles
* Advanced improvement methods, including process mapping, root cause analysis, structured testing, performance variation, operating-model redesign, and outcome, process, and balancing measures
* Project and program management practices, including planning, tracking, risk management, issue escalation, and cross-functional integration across large or interdependent initiatives
* Data analysis, reporting, and use of healthcare operational and performance metrics to support executive decision-making
* Advanced change-impact assessment, stakeholder engagement, readiness and adoption measurement, capability building, standard work, sustainment, and shared governance principles
* Regulatory, accreditation, and compliance considerations that affect healthcare operations and process redesign
* Staff supervision, performance management, professional development, workload planning, and improvement practice management

Skills in
 
 

* Building effective working relationships with leaders, providers, staff, and cross-functional teams, including senior leaders, governance participants, and executive stakeholders
* Facilitating complex meetings, work sessions, governance discussions, decision-making, and follow-through across multiple stakeholders
* Using standard business software and healthcare information systems to organize work, analyze information, and communicate effectively
* Communicating clearly and effectively in written, verbal, presentation, and executive reporting formats
* Coaching and developing improvement professionals, setting clear expectations, balancing assignments, and providing constructive performance feedback

Ability to
 
 

* Facilitate complex problem-solving, support conflict resolution, and help remove high-level operational barriers to execution across enterprise or highly interdependent initiatives
* Influence without direct authority, foster collaboration, and align diverse stakeholders around shared goals, tradeoffs, and execution plans
* Analyze complex issues, develop practical recommendations, and support implementation of operational change across multiple functions or enterprise priorities
* Work effectively with people from diverse disciplines, backgrounds, and perspectives
* Adapt to changing organizational priorities, healthcare environments, and operational demands while maintaining momentum across complex initiatives

**Position Information**
Work Shift:Exempt
 
 
*If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!*

new_roles.title: Director, Operational Excellence
new_roles.description:
Abbott is a global healthcare leader that helps people live more fully at all stages of life. Our portfolio of life-changing technologies spans the spectrum of healthcare, with leading businesses and products in diagnostics, medical devices, nutritionals and branded generic medicines. Our 122,000 colleagues serve people in more than 160 countries.
 
 
**Director, Operational Excellence**
We're advancing cancer care through innovative screening and diagnostic tests that help patients and healthcare providers make informed decisions before, during and after a cancer diagnosis. Our growing portfolio includes Cologuard®, Oncotype DX®, Cancerguard® and Oncodetect®, along with advanced genetic testing, supporting patients from cancer prevention and early detection through personalized treatment decisions and recurrence monitoring. We're focused on helping more people take action against cancer at its earliest, most treatable stages, so they can live longer, healthier lives.
 
 
This role is based on-site in Madison, WI.
 
 
**Position Overview**
Abbott is seeking a Director, Operational Excellence to lead the development, implementation, and sustainability of operational excellence practices across our Cancer Diagnostics operations.
 
 
This leader will partner closely with operations leadership and frontline teams to strengthen daily management practices, improve operational performance, and build a culture of continuous improvement and accountability.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities :**

* Lead the implementation of operational excellence practices that improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance.
* Establish and sustain tiered management routines, visual performance boards, standardized metrics, and structured performance reviews across hourly, daily, weekly, and monthly intervals.
* Partner with operations leaders to implement supervisor standard work, strengthen accountability, and develop consistent problem-solving and performance management practices.
* Apply Lean and Six Sigma methodologies to improve process flow, eliminate waste, reduce variation, and drive measurable operational results.
* Establish employee-driven improvement programs that encourage frontline participation, idea generation, and ownership of operational improvements.
* Lead change management efforts that ensure new processes are adopted, embedded into daily operations, and sustained over time.
* Collaborate with Operations, Quality, Engineering, Supply Chain, and other stakeholders to align improvement initiatives with business priorities.
* Lead and coach a team of operational excellence professionals while building continuous improvement capabilities across the broader organization.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Science, Operations Management, Business, Supply Chain, or a related field with a minimum of 10 years of relevant experience; or Master's degree in a related field with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience.
* Significant progressive experience in operations leadership, operational excellence, or continuous improvement within a manufacturing, laboratory, or complex operational environment.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and sustaining Lean practices, daily management systems, visual performance management, and structured problem-solving.
* Experience leading operational teams or working directly with frontline leaders to drive measurable performance improvements.
* Proven ability to lead organizational change, influence cross-functional stakeholders, and build accountability.
* Strong people leadership, coaching, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Direct leadership experience in manufacturing, laboratory, or other high-volume operations.
* Experience in regulated industries such as diagnostics, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, or healthcare.
* Lean Six Sigma Green Belt certification or equivalent practical experience.
* Experience implementing tiered management systems, supervisor standard work, and employee-driven continuous improvement programs.
* Demonstrated success sustaining operational improvements through frontline engagement and leadership ownership.

The base pay for this position is $149,300.00 – $298,700.00. In specific locations, the pay range may vary from the range posted.

new_roles.description:
1.0 FTE Full time Day - 08 Hour R2655441 Hybrid 108400006 SC Administration Business & Administration PALO ALTO, 1840 Embarcadero, California
 
 
If you're ready to be part of our legacy of hope and innovation, we encourage you to take the first step and explore our current job openings. Your best is waiting to be discovered.
 
 
Day - 08 Hour (United States of America)
 
 
**This is a Stanford Health Care job.**
**A Brief Overview**
The Director of Supply Chain Operational Excellence is a senior leadership role driving enterprise‑wide efficiency, innovation, and transformation across a Gartner top‑2 ranked healthcare supply chain. With system‑wide influence and a seat at the leadership table, this role partners closely with the Chief Supply Chain Officer and Vice President of Strategic Initiatives to turn strategy into measurable results. The ideal candidate combines healthcare supply chain expertise with strong program management skills and a passion for developing people, leading change, and delivering measurable, enterprise‑wide impact.
 
 
**Locations**
Stanford Health Care
 
 
**What You Will Do**

* Maintain continuous alignment with defined organizational and departmental strategic business objectives in conjunction with leadership.
* Direct and ensure the efficient operation of day-to-day activities of the team and ensure competency of all staff.
* Supports and partners on Change Management, Training and Communications activities as needed for effective performance improvement and project management.
* Act in an advisory capacity to all Supply Chain divisions, programs, staff and leaders.
* Provide expertise, guidance and training on Performance Improvement and Project Management best practices.
* Apply LEAN/Six Sigma principles and methods to identify waste reduction and performance optimization opportunities across Supply Chain operations.
* Implement, oversee and continuously improve Supply Chain systems, processes and standard work to drive the efficient management of operations across Logistics, Sourcing, Procurement, Business Office, Resiliency, Sustainability, Data Management and other functions.
* Build, develop and grow business relationships with Supply Chain’s key stakeholders and partners including but not limited to the Interventional Platform, A/P, Pharmacy, and IT.
* Lead cross-departmental initiatives, establishing strong governance, communication, and accountability to deliver progress measurable through mutually agreed KPIs.
* Align and collaborate with the enterprise Performance Improvement team and Stanford Operating System (SOS).
* Lead the implementation of programs and/or projects as assigned by the Administrative Director.

**Education Qualifications**

* Requires a Bachelor’s degree in a work-related discipline/field from an accredited college or university.
* Relevant experience in lieu of degree may be considered. Relevant experience in lieu of degree is in addition to the experience requirements for this position.

**Experience Qualifications**

* Seven (7) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

new_roles.title: Director - Corporate Continuous Improvement
new_roles.description:
**Description**
****Position Summary****
The Director of Corporate Continuous Improvement (CI) leads MacAllister’s enterprise CI strategy, Corporate CI team, and improvement portfolio. In partnership with the owner, executive team, and divisional leaders, the Director helps establish and build alignment around MacAllister’s CI vision, strategy, priorities, and multi-year roadmap. The Director identifies and prioritizes high-value opportunities, builds organizational problem-solving capability, and leads improvement work from opportunity identification through execution and sustainment.
 
 
The role establishes CI standards, tools, and training; coaches, mentors, and influences leaders and teams across the organization; and communicates CI priorities, results, and opportunities for support.
 
 
The ultimate objective is to build and sustain a culture in which continuous improvement becomes habitual and is reflected in how leaders and employees think, act, solve problems, and improve the way work gets done.
 
 
****Position Duties/Responsibilities****
**Primary Responsibilities**

* Partner with the executive team, and divisional leaders to develop and maintain MacAllister’s CI strategy, multi-year roadmap, priorities, and operating model aligned with company goals. Build leadership alignment and shared ownership of CI priorities and expectations across the organization.
* Own CI project identification, prioritization, approval, execution, and close-out, focusing on where CI creates the most value; support employee-driven improvement alongside leader-sponsored initiatives.
* Maintain consistent project close-out documenting results, lessons learned, and sustainment plans; verify improvements and results are sustained and take corrective action as needed.
* Set organization-wide CI standards, tools, and terminology; guide Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA application grounded in facts, data, and root cause analysis; coach project teams and facilitate select high-impact improvement events.
* Lead improvement-related change management, engaging affected employees early and ensuring process adoption and sustainment.
* Oversee CI training tailored to responsibility levels using consistent terminology and live projects; coach and support CI-trained departmental leaders who remain in their home departments outside CI.
* Define CI value primarily through capability measures—leaders solving problems independently, AI use cases adopted, and idea-to-approval cycle time—with financial results as supporting evidence.
* Communicate CI initiatives, results, and available support so leaders know when and how to engage the team; share success stories and recognize improvement contributors.
* Use coaching-first leadership to build team autonomy, confidence, and influence; foster problem reporting, experimentation, and learning from mistakes by supporting people publicly and coaching privately.
* Hire, develop, and manage CI personnel; oversee budget, resource allocation, and team structure as needs evolve.
* Play a leadership role in MacAllister’s Center of Practice for CI, AI, and problem-solving leadership, incorporating AI and other emerging technologies into CI methods where they improve problem solving, decision making, or productivity. Partner with MacAllister’s enterprise AI leadership on broader AI strategy, standards, and adoption.

**Supervisory Responsibilities**

* Directly supervises the Corporate CI team and oversees day-to-day operations of the CI department. Mentors and coaches CI team members to strengthen their capabilities as problem solvers, facilitators, coaches, and trusted business partners.
* Reviews and evaluates the work and performance of reporting employees; has authority for hiring and disciplinary actions.

****Position Requirements****
**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, engineering, or a related field.
* 10 years or more of experience in continuous improvement, operations, or business transformation.
* 5 years or more of experience leading leaders.
* Proven success coaching others to identify and solve problems independently.
* Working knowledge of Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, DMAIC, and PDCA.
* A valid driver’s license.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in business or a related discipline.
* Lean Six Sigma Master Black Belt or equivalent depth of experience designing and delivering CI training.
* Experience at a Caterpillar dealership or in the equipment sales, service, or rental industry.
* Demonstrated curiosity and willingness to learn and apply emerging technologies, including AI, to strengthen problem solving, process improvement, decision support, and organizational productivity. Experience applying AI in these areas is preferred but not required.
* Experience building on an existing CI function and growing its influence across a multi-location organization.

****Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities****

* Strong coaching and leadership development skills; leads through influence rather than authority.
* Ability to connect improvement work to business priorities and help leaders choose where to focus.
* Curiosity about and practical comfort with AI as a business tool.
* Exceptional communication and facilitation skills with all levels, from the front line to executives.
* Ability to build and maintain trusted relationships with executives, senior managers, and teams.
* Respect for existing culture and relationships, with the judgment to improve without unnecessary disruption.
* Strong organizational, prioritization, and project management skills.
* Effective computer skills with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn proprietary systems.

****Other Requirements of Position****

* Works under broad supervision. Designs and carries out programs and far-reaching objectives independently, informing management as appropriate.
* Major responsibilities require a wide degree of creativity and latitude.
* If an error is made while in this position, it will require some effort to identify and can significantly impact the company financially.
* Frequently communicates with coworkers, customers, company executives, and management.
* Maintain equipment and supplies to avoid waste, damage to areas and equipment, and to prevent accidents.

The duties and responsibilities outlined in this posting are not exhaustive and may evolve based on business needs.
 
 
All MacAllister Machinery companies are an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer, including Disabled and Veteran applicants.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality-Operations
new_roles.description:
**About Us:**
BW Papersystems, part of the Barry-Wehmiller Group, builds capital equipment that transforms paper into products for consumers - every day, around the world. We offer innovative technologies, service and parts, and years of global experience in corrugating, finishing; slitting and packaging; stationery; bookbinding and security documents. Customers rely on our machines to produce and convert items such as corrugated boxes, folding cartons, passports, notebooks, copy paper, board, and coated and other specialty papers. For more information, visit bwpapersystems.com.
 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world.
 
 
**Job Description:**
The Director of Quality will be responsible for developing the overall Quality Improvement Strategy and lead the team in the cross-functional adoption and execution of that strategy. In this critical role, the Director of Quality will be the leader in developing and maintaining a quality management system to improve operating efficiency, quality and productivity in operations, to improve customer satisfaction, and to increase profitability in a safe working environment.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Develop the overall Quality Improvement Strategy and lead the management team in the cross-functional adoption and execution of that strategy.
* Develop and maintain a business/quality management system to improve operating efficiency, quality and productivity in operations, to improve customer satisfaction and increase profitability in a safe working environment within the local business.
* Continuously assess the overall Quality Management System, Quality Plan and Quality Organization to determine priorities for quality improvement.
* Establish the key improvement priorities, and using a strategy deployment approach, develop and execute a cross-functional, strategic action plan to drive improvement.
* Identify the leading sources of customer dissatisfaction.
* Determine the underlying causes and develop/execute strategies to eliminate those causes.
* Determine the true, systemic root causes of internal failure and Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ).
* Execute a strategy consisting of well-planned and executed preventive actions that reduce COPQ and other forms of waste.
* Drive improvements in process quality, production efficiency, and the elimination of the factors that drive variability and unforeseen disruptions.
* Drive a strategy that incorporates standard work, effective training, and recurring process audits to ensure process discipline.
* Establish and maintain appropriate KPIs that provide objective evidence of improvement
* Participate in training and coaching teams in the standard quality improvement approach and quality management standard requirements to develop organizational capability.

**EDUCATION & EXPERIENCE:**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, quality, continuous improvement, or related field.
* 10+ years of professional experience leading a Quality Organization in capital equipment manufacturing environment.
* Experience with the execution of continuous improvement methodology such as Operational Excellence, Lean Manufacturing, Strategy Deployment, etc.

**KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, ABILITIES:**

* Requires the ability to independently resolve complex problems.
* Requires ability to manage a skilled and diverse staff, communicate effectively, represent the organization, act decisively, and influence decisions of senior managers and customers.
* Requires foresight to anticipate problems and recognize opportunities for cost-effectively improving operations.

**COMPETENCIES**

* Customer Focus – Building strong customer relationships and delivering customer-centric solutions.
* Instills Trust – Gaining the confidence and trust of others through honesty, integrity, and authenticity.
* Drives Results - Consistently achieving results, even under tough circumstances.
* Communicates Effectively - Developing and delivering multi-mode communications that convey a clear understanding of the unique needs of different audiences.
* Optimizes Work Processes - Knowing the most effective and efficient processes to get things done, with a focus on continuous improvement.
* Ensures Accountability - Holding self and others accountable to meet commitments.
* Collaborates – Building partnerships and collaborating with others to meet shared objectives.
* Decision Quality – Making good and timely decisions that keep the organization moving forward.

*The approximate pay range for this position is $155,000 to $210,000 base salary. Please note that the pay range provided is a good faith estimate for the position at the time of posting. Final compensation may vary based on factors including but not limited to background, knowledge, skills, and abilities as well as geographic location of the position.*
*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*
Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify.
 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments.
 
 
**Company:**
BW Papersystems

new_roles.title: Director of Operations
new_roles.description:
**At Materion, everyone is included, respected and offered opportunity to grow.
*Join us!***
Position Summary
 
 
The Director of Operations, Premium Targets provides strategic and operational leadership for a complex, multi-site manufacturing organization with domestic and international operations. This leader is accountable for safety, quality, delivery, cost, customer performance, talent development, capital execution, and continuous improvement. The individual in this role will lead Operations, Supply Chain, and Engineering teams, including manufacturing facilities across multiple locations. As the organization’s senior operations safety leader, the Director sets clear expectations, models visible safety leadership, empowers employees to identify and address hazards, and holds leaders accountable for proactive risk reduction and continuous EHS improvement. Working across Technology, Quality, Supply Chain, Commercial, Engineering, EHS, and other functions, the Director translates business priorities into sustainable results, standardizes manufacturing and business processes, and delivers exceptional service to internal and external customers. The role also leads operations strategy and financial performance, including gross margin, inventory turns, and cost management.
 
 
Operations Leadership and Execution
 
 

* Lead a proactive, prevention-focused safety culture in which every employee is empowered and expected to identify hazards, stop unsafe work, and take ownership of a safe and healthy workplace.
* Lead manufacturing operations across Buffalo, Wheatfield, Albuquerque, Limerick, and Brewster, with strong matrix partnerships supporting Alzenau and Taiwan.
* Own performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, and customer commitments; establish clear metrics, review performance routinely, and hold site leaders accountable for results.
* Set and execute the Premium Targets operations strategy, multi-year roadmap, and long-range capital and workforce plans.
* Ensure facilities consistently deliver high-quality products on time to internal business units and external customers.
* Partner with Technology, Quality, Supply Chain, Commercial, Engineering, EHS, and other functions to align priorities and improve end-to-end performance.
* Develop, coach, and hold operational leaders accountable for business results, team effectiveness, and talent growth.
* Strengthen communication, operating discipline, and knowledge sharing across all Premium Targets facilities.
* Provide clear, timely business updates and recommendations to senior leaders and key stakeholders.

Operational Excellence, Strategy, and Capital Leadership
 
 

* Champion EHS excellence by ensuring regulatory compliance, audit readiness, effective risk assessments, timely incident and near-miss investigation, corrective-action closure, and consistent use of leading and lagging safety indicators.
* Serve as executive sponsor for the Premium Targets Lean manufacturing transformation.
* Advance daily management, structured problem solving, kaizen, standard work, process improvement, and cost-reduction practices across sites.
* Partner with Lean resources and site leaders to implement improvements and sustain measurable gains.
* Lead major capital programs, equipment installations, expansions, and facility transitions in partnership with Engineering, corporate, business-unit, and capital teams.
* Ensure capital initiatives meet approved cost, schedule, quality, and performance objectives while integrating safety into design, installation, commissioning, and startup.
* Develop manufacturing and supply chain strategies that support production, maintenance, planning, EHS, technical capability, and customer requirements.
* Partner with Commercial teams to deliver an exceptional customer experience.
* Enable best-practice sharing and process standardization across manufacturing locations.
* Lead financial performance improvement, with a focus on gross margin, inventory turns, and cost management.

**Qualifications**
**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.
* At least 10 years of progressive experience in a manufacturing environment, including significant manufacturing operations people leadership responsibility with a demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build high-performing teams.
* Demonstrated success leading safety and EHS performance, manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, engineering, and capital projects.
* Ability to lead end-to-end processes and deliver results through cross-functional and matrixed teams.
* Ability to travel up to 50%.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Master’s degree in engineering, business administration, or a related field.
* Leadership experience in a multi-site or international manufacturing organization.
* Experience leading a Lean transformation or enterprise-wide operating system.
* Experience managing major capital programs, facility expansions, installations, or transitions.

**Leadership Competencies**

* Strategic and systems-oriented thinking, with the ability to translate business priorities into executable operating plans.
* Strong influence, collaboration, and negotiation skills, including the ability to secure alignment and resources across functions.
* Clear, concise written and verbal communication with team members, peers, customers, and senior leaders.
* Sound judgment and the ability to navigate ambiguity, reconcile differing viewpoints, and make timely decisions.
* Visible, values-based leadership grounded in safety, integrity, accountability, disciplined execution, and continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated commitment to coaching, succession planning, and the growth of talent across all levels.

**Pay Range**
$148,500.00 - $237,100.00
 
 
*Actual base salary offered varies based on factors, including but not limited to, relevant skill, prior experience, education, base salary of internal peers, demonstrated performance, and geographic location.*
**The selection of the person to be hired for this position is contingent on the candidate having export compliance eligibility for access to U.S. controlled technology which comes under the licensing jurisdiction of the U.S. Department of State, International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) and the U.S. Department of Commerce, Export Administration Regulations (EAR).**
**The candidate selected will have to qualify as either a U.S. citizen, a U.S. National, a lawful permanent resident of the U.S., a Person Admitted into the U.S. as an Asylee or Refugee., a National of a country that is not prohibited from having access to U.S. controlled technology (via a letter of assurance), or a Person to be approved for an export license by the governing agency whose technology comes under its jurisdiction. Please understand that any job offer that requires approval of an export license will be conditional on Materion’s determination that it will be able to obtain an export license in a time frame consistent with Materion’s business requirements.**
**Materion Corporation and its subsidiaries (the “Company”) is an equal employment opportunity employer. It is the Company’s policy to not unlawfully discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, sex, age, physical or mental disability, veteran or military status, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state or local laws, regulations or ordinances. The Company also prohibits harassment of applicants and employees based on any of these protected categories. It is also the Company’s policy to comply with all applicable federal, state and local laws respecting consideration of unemployment status in making hiring decisions. The information collected by this application is solely to determine suitability for employment, verify identity and maintain employment statistics on applicants.**
**Applicants with disabilities may be entitled to reasonable accommodation under the terms of the Americans with Disabilities Act and certain state or local laws. A reasonable accommodation is a change in the way things are normally done which will ensure an equal employment opportunity without imposing undue hardship on the Company. Please inform the Company’s personnel representative if you need assistance completing any forms or to otherwise participate in the application process.**
**Materion’s Veteran Employee Resource group supports veterans and promotes the benefits of hiring veterans in the workplace. We honor all those who have served and are a military friendly company. Veterans are encouraged to apply and military experience and skills are transferrable to Materion careers.**
**Please provide complete information. An incomplete application may affect your consideration for employment.**

new_roles.title: Director, Central Quality Audit, Pharmacovigilance
new_roles.description:
**Job Description Summary**
===========================

Managing, ensuring and improving capabilities to comply with external standards and regulations. Interprets internal and external business challenges and recommends best practices to improve products, processes or services. Stays informed of industry trends that may influence work. 
 
GE HealthCare is a leading global medical technology and digital solutions innovator. Our mission is to improve lives in the moments that matter. Unlock your ambition, turn ideas into world-changing realities, and join an organization where every voice makes a difference, and every difference builds a healthier world.

**Job Description**
===================

**Roles and Responsibilities**

* Own the Pharmacovigilance (PV) Audit Program: Develop, implement, and maintain the global PV audit strategy, ensuring alignment with regulatory expectations (e.g., EMA, FDA, MHRA, PMDA) and industry best practices.
* Manage Audit Operations: Oversee scheduling, planning, execution, reporting, and follow-up for PV audits, including internal audits and audits of service providers and affiliates. Fully participate in the audit program; actively owning and executing PV audits.
* Risk Identification and Communication: Identify high-risk compliance issues, escalate findings, and provide actionable recommendations to senior leadership.
* Regulatory Inspection Support: Prepare for and support PV-related health authority inspections, including back-room management and post-inspection follow-up.
* Metrics and Reporting: Define and track PV audit KPIs, ensuring visibility of compliance risks and trends to leadership.
* System Ownership: Manage audit-related modules within the electronic Quality Management System (eQMS), including support of configuration, UAT, and documentation.
* Team Leadership: Lead and develop a team of 3–5 auditors, providing coaching, mentorship, and performance management.
* Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with PV Operations, Quality, and Regulatory teams to ensure audit outcomes drive continuous improvement.
* Strategic Influence: Contribute to policy development and influence PV compliance strategy across the organization.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 5 years of people leadership experience, including team development and performance management.
* Qualified Lead Auditor with active certification.
* Master’s degree and 5+ years in pharmacovigilance or pharmaceutical industry; or Bachelor’s degree and 10+ years relevant experience.
* Minimum of 5 years’ experience driving Global programs to resolve quality compliance issues (directly).
* Experience with Pharmaceutical QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to cGMP, GDP, GPvP, GCP and GLP.

**Desired Characteristics**

* Experience with Medical Device QMS requirements and regulatory requirements including but not limited to FDA CFR 21 820 and ISO 13485.
* Prior Veeva and TrackWise Digital experience a plus.
* Prior health authority experience a plus.
* IRCA, ASQ (CQE, CQA, etc.) and/or Lean Certification a plus (green belt, black belt).
* Extensive experience in the Medica Device and Pharmaceutical industry.
* Understanding of product quality improvement using tools such as Six Sigma, DFR.
* Demonstrated ability to analyze and resolve problems.
* Exceptional conflict-resolution skills.
* Ability to interface with top organizational leadership and internal and external customers, responding in a professional manner.
* Demonstrated ability to lead programs / projects. Ability to prioritize and drive multiple programs.
* Ability to energize others by building a connection with the team through personal involvement and trust, providing feedback and coaching to develop others, and accountability of actions.
* Strong oral and written communication skills in English.
* Integrity: Accepting and adhering to high ethical, moral, and personal values in decisions, communications, actions, and when dealing with others.
* Ability to travel globally up to 15%.

We expect all employees to live and breathe our behaviors: to act with humility and build trust; lead with transparency; deliver with focus, and drive ownership –always with unyielding integrity.

Our total rewards are designed to unlock your ambition by giving you the boost and flexibility you need to turn your ideas into world-changing realities. Our salary and benefits are everything you’d expect from an organization with global strength and scale, and you’ll be surrounded by career opportunities in a culture that fosters care, collaboration and support.

We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this job opening. For U.S. based positions only, the pay range for this position is $142,400.00-$213,600.00 Annual. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the pay range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. The specific compensation offered to a candidate may be influenced by a variety of factors including skills, qualifications, experience and location. In addition, this position may also be eligible to earn performance based incentive compensation, which may include cash bonus(es) and/or long term incentives (LTI). GE HealthCare offers a competitive benefits package, including not but limited to medical, dental, vision, paid time off, a 401(k) plan with employee and company contribution opportunities, life, disability, and accident insurance, and tuition reimbursement.

**Additional Information**
==========================

GE HealthCare offers a great work environment, professional development, challenging careers, and competitive compensation. GE HealthCare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, national or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law.

GE HealthCare will only employ those who are legally authorized to work in the United States for this opening. Any offer of employment is conditioned upon the successful completion of a drug screen (as applicable).

While GE HealthCare does not currently require U.S. employees to be vaccinated against COVID-19, some GE HealthCare customers have vaccination mandates that may apply to certain GE HealthCare employees.

**Relocation Assistance Provided:** No

Application Deadline: December 21, 2026

new_roles.description:
Overview:

**Hospital Name: Ohiohealth Rehabilitation Hospital** 
**Joint venture/Partnership/Affiliation with Select Medical** 
**Position:** **Director of Quality Management** 
**Location: Dublin, OH**

* Bonus incentives
* Extensive onboarding and training program
* Customizable health insurance packages

**Who We Are**

Our inpatient rehabilitation hospital is committed to providing exceptional and compassionate care to best address the medical, physical, emotional, and vocational challenges for individuals with brain injuries, spinal cord injuries, neurological disorders, orthopedic issues, amputation, and multiple traumas

Responsibilities:

Coordinates the Medical Quality Management and Performance Improvement activities to measurably enhance the quality, process and cost effectiveness of patient and customer services rendered. Coordinates the Performance Improvement and Patient Safety programs in accordance with the guidelines and regulatory requirements of Federal and State regulations on a hospital-wide basis. Oversees operations of the Infection Control and Employee Health Programs. Develops and Reviews policies and procedures to ensure compliance with all regulatory and accrediting standards. Collects data to monitor compliance and/or trends.

 

* Institutes and monitors the Hospital’s CQI Processes, utilizing data analysis measuring tools. Oversight/coordination of operations of the Infection Control & Employee Health Program based upon hospital size and configuration.
* Assists with the design and compliance of quality processes/activities in the areas of clinical/medical staff PI for all applicable clinical/medical TJC /CARF/DOH standards. Assists with all assigned activities to assure that the hospital maintains accreditation, certification and licensure. Assumes leadership with the Joint Commission and DOH as well as other regulatory agencies with regard to CQI activities.

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
**About the Role:**

As Director of Quality, you’ll lead Helix’s quality department and drive the development of systems, practices, and people to ensure product excellence, regulatory compliance, and customer satisfaction. You’ll hire, train, and manage the team, own the quality system, and make it clear who is responsible for quality at every step.

You’ll report directly to the Chief Executive Officer, partner closely with Engineering, Operations, and our customers to build a proactive, scalable, and right-sized quality system that enables growth.

### **Key Responsibilities:**

**Strategic Leadership & Systems Development**

* Develop and continuously improve a scalable Quality Management System aligned with AS9100 and customer requirements
* Lead departmental strategy, structure, and capital planning to support business growth
* Serve as ISO/AS Management Representative

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Lead and mentor a team of 5+ quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians
* Develop people and build team capabilities in metrology, inspection, and quality engineering
* Foster a culture of collaboration and real-time problem-solving on the shop floor

**Customer & Compliance Management**

* Lead customer and supplier audits; own response and resolution of corrective actions
* Ensure documentation, compliance, and audit readiness
* Build trusted relationships with key customers and act as the face of Quality

**Quality Engineering & Continuous Improvement**

* Partner with operators to implement in-process quality at the machine (not just post-process inspection)
* Drive root cause analysis, SPC implementation, and corrective actions to reduce scrap and improve first-pass yield
* Support new product introductions and ensure proper gauges, fixtures, and inspection plans are in place

**Internal Inspection & Production Support**

* Oversee first-piece, in-process, and final inspection plans
* Continuously simplify and optimize inspection methods to reduce bottlenecks without sacrificing quality

### **What Success Looks Like**

* Promoting Operational Excellence by initiating and helping implement continuous improvement objectives.
* Maintaining a robust QMS system and compliance to AS9100 and ISO 9001 standards.
* Leading the company during customer audits and independent audits towards successful (re)certification.
* Lowering scrap and increasing first pass yield.
* Cross functional collaboration with Production and Engineering to help build quality into the process.
* Implementing solid Corrective Actions to reduce RMAs and DMRs.
* Establishing best practices for the Quality department and the organization as a whole

### **Who You Are**

* A pragmatic quality leader who blends systems thinking with real-world shop floor experience
* Confident navigating between big-picture strategy and hands-on process improvement
* A builder of systems and people, able to lead a team and train on complex equipment
* Comfortable in a customer-facing role and able to communicate clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders
* Committed to continuous improvement, collaboration, and delivering value across departments

### **Qualifications:**

**Must-Haves**

* 10+ years in manufacturing quality, preferably in machining-based environments
* Strong knowledge of AS9100 and ISO 9001 standards
* Experience leading customer and regulatory audits
* Proven people management skills
* Working knowledge of metrology, CMM, GD&T, and SPC tools
* Experience balancing compliance with operational efficiency

**Nice-to-Haves**

* Mechanical or technical degree
* Experience supporting New Product Development (NPD)
* Six Sigma, Lean, or ASQ certifications (CQE, CQA, CQM)
* Familiarity with vision systems, statistical software (e.g., Minitab), and automation of inspection processes

**About the Company:**

Helix Linear Technologies designs and manufactures high-precision motion control systems for industries where performance matters most, like aerospace, medical devices, and industrial automation. We’re in a phase of strategic growth, investing in R&D, advanced equipment, and new product lines, including aerospace-grade ball screws.

Our clean, climate-controlled facility is built for precision, focus, and continuous improvement. At Helix, you’ll join a team that values ownership, technical excellence, and curiosity.

We offer competitive compensation, comprehensive health, dental, and vision benefits, a retirement savings plan with company match, and paid time off and company holidays.

Helix Linear Technologies is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Due to U.S. export control laws, applicants must be U.S. persons (U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident).

new_roles.title: Director, Health Access & Quality Operations
new_roles.description:
The American Diabetes Association (ADA) is committed to expanding access to care, advancing health access, improving quality, and achieving better health outcomes for people living with diabetes, prediabetes, and obesity. The Director, Health Access & Quality Operations provides operational and financial oversight for the Health Access & Quality Department, ensuring effective planning, resource management, project execution, and performance accountability. Working closely with department leadership, Finance, Enterprise Strategy, the Program Management Office (PMO), and other internal stakeholders, this position translates departmental priorities into actionable plans, financial analyses, performance dashboards, and executive-level reporting.

 

The Director brings strong expertise in project and portfolio management, financial planning and analysis, dashboard development, and executive communications. The individual must demonstrate the ability to engage directly with Finance leaders on budgeting, forecasting, revenue and expense projections, financial variances, and resource allocation. Equally important is the ability to synthesize complex financial and operational information into meaningful insights, recommendations, and compelling presentations for executive leadership and Board-level audiences.

 

**Responsibilities** 
***Financial Planning & Analysis***

* Lead annual budget development and ongoing forecasting with Finance, including revenue and expense projections, reforecasts and scenario modeling.
* Prepare monthly budget-to-actual reports, analyze variances and recommend corrective actions.
* Track restricted and unrestricted funding, including grants, sponsorships and contracts, to ensure spending is compliant and aligned with funding requirements.
* Develop cost models, cost-benefit analyses and ROI assessments for new initiatives and investments.

 

***Project & Portfolio Management***

* Oversee the department's project portfolio, aligning priorities, resources, timelines and budgets with strategic goals.
* Develop project plans, timelines, risk logs and status reports, and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver on scope, schedule and budget.
* Partner with the PMO on governance, intake, prioritization and capacity planning.
* Monitor project budgets and burn rates, flagging risks early and proposing ways to reduce them.

 

***Performance Reporting & Executive Communications***

* Build and maintain executive dashboards and KPI scorecards that combine financial, operational and programmatic data.
* Prepare executive presentations, Board materials and management reports that explain complex information clearly.
* Present financial results, forecasts and project status to senior leadership to support decision-making.
* Show how financial investment connects to program outcomes and measurable impact.

 

***Operations & Process Improvement***

* Translate strategic priorities into operating plans with clear owners, timelines and success measures.
* Manage resource allocation, vendor contracts and spending controls in line with ADA policies.
* Identify inefficiencies and lead process improvements that produce measurable results.
* Serve as a trusted advisor to department leadership on financial, operational and project matters.

 

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, Project Management, Operations, or a related field required.
* Formal finance education or training required, demonstrated through a degree, formal coursework, professional certification, or recognized financial management/financial planning and analysis training.
* Formal project management education or training required, demonstrated through a Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) certification, or completion of a recognized project management training program.
* Equivalent combinations of education, professional training, and relevant experience may be considered, provided formal training in both finance and project management is demonstrated.
* Minimum of 7 years of progressive experience in business operations, financial planning and analysis, project or portfolio management, or a related discipline.
* Demonstrated experience managing complex projects, developing project plans, coordinating cross-functional teams, and monitoring deliverables and outcomes.
* Substantial experience working directly with Finance leaders or Finance business partners on annual budgeting, revenue and expense forecasting, budget-to-actual analysis, variance reporting, and financial projections.
* Demonstrated ability to interpret financial statements, analyze financial performance, identify trends and variances, and translate findings into actionable recommendations.
* Experience developing and maintaining executive dashboards, KPI scorecards, financial reports, and performance management tools.
* Demonstrated ability to integrate financial, operational, and programmatic data to communicate organizational performance and measurable impact.
* Experience developing executive-level presentations, Board materials, and management reports that communicate complex information clearly and effectively.
* Demonstrated experience engaging senior executives and presenting financial, operational, and performance information to leadership audiences.
* Experience managing multiple projects, priorities, and stakeholders within a complex, matrixed organization.
* Experience identifying operational inefficiencies and implementing process improvements that produce measurable results.

 

***Preferred Qualifications***

* Advanced project management certification or additional specialized training in portfolio management, program management, or business process improvement.
* Experience in nonprofit, healthcare, public health, or mission-driven organizations.
* Experience managing financial performance across multiple programs, funding sources, grants, or geographic markets.
* Familiarity with financial planning and analysis (FP&A), enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, and business intelligence platforms.
* Experience with Microsoft Project, Smartsheet, or comparable dashboard and project management platforms.
* Experience supporting executive leadership teams and preparing materials for Boards of Directors, Finance Committees, or other governance bodies.

 

**Why Work Here** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) offers a rewarding career working for one of the premier voluntary health organizations in the world supporting people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Our employees consistently say that our mission, culture, work-life balance, and total rewards package are what they like most about working at the ADA. benefits and our culture:

* Industry competitive base pay. Base offers are determined by several factors including but not limited to your relevant work experience, education, certifications, location, internal pay equity, etc.
* A culture of recognition including new hire welcome announcements, service anniversary awards, referral bonuses, monthly All Employee Assembly, appreciation awards
* Generous Paid Time Off, including holidays, vacation days, personal days and sick days
* Comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA), disability & life insurance, pet insurance, and retirement savings
* Guided by our mission, we provide full diabetes supply coverage through our medical benefits program
* A company focus on offering mental health programs and work/life balance with most of our employees working remote
* Joining our dedicated team affords the gratification of knowing beyond a doubt that you will impact the lives and well-being of millions

 

**About the Organization** 
The American Diabetes Association ® (ADA) is the nation’s leading voluntary health organization fighting to end diabetes and helping people living with diabetes thrive. Since 1940, we have driven discovery and research to prevent, manage, treat, and ultimately cure diabetes. We advocate for policy changes and improved access to quality care for all people living with diabetes and/or obesity. Through the Obesity Association, a division of the ADA, we are also working to reduce the prevalence of obesity—a leading risk factor for type 2 diabetes.
