### **POSITION****SUMMARY:**

Working closely with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team, the Director of Program Quality and Training of Youth Programs documents best practices, designs tools to measure staff and youth outcomes, and supports collaboration among youth-serving organizations. This role provides strategic leadership for quality improvement, staff development, and outcomes assessment across Cambridge Youth Programs’ five youth centers serving more than 1,200 youth ages 9–19, partnering with the Division Head and CYP Leadership Team to codify best practices, build measurement tools, and strengthen collaboration among youth-serving organizations. The Director directly supervises an Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector, and manages organization-wide partnerships, grant implementation and reporting, and recruitment and outreach efforts.

### **ESSENTIAL****JOB****FUNCTIONS****and****DUTIES:**

*The**essential**functions**or**duties**listed**below**are**intended**only**as**illustrations**of**the**various**type**of**work**that may be performed. The omission of specific statements of duties does not exclude them from the position if the work is similar, related, or a logical assignment to the position.*

* Support expanded learning and out-of-school-time programs serving youth ages 9–19 across the City’s youth centers, including afterschool programs, evening programs, school vacation programming, and specialized youth activities.
* Assist the Division Head for Youth Programs in establishing program goals, objectives, and operational priorities.
* Assist with oversight of programs and activities across the City’s youth centers and collaborate with

 Youth Program staff as part of the Cambridge Youth Programs Leadership Team.
* Provide strategic oversight and support for program quality improvement initiatives and develop systems to assess, track, and manage program performance using positive youth development principles.
* Develop and implement systems to identify staff training and professional development needs and design and deliver training programs that support best practices in youth development, out-of-school-time programming, and effective supervision.
* Provide guidance and support to program staff in program planning, implementation, and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop and manage organization-wide partnerships, initiatives, and grant partnerships, including implementation oversight and grant reporting; support recruitment materials development and outreach to prospective participants and partner organizations.
* Supervise a Youth Connector who develops and supports sites around middle school and teen transition programs, pre-teen, middle school, and teen recruitment and enrollment, and the organization’s social media plan.
* Provide direct coaching support to assigned youth center sites, working with Program Directors on a weekly basis to develop, implement, and assess both site-based plans and collective projects across the organization.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations to design and implement tools that measure staff and youth outcomes, support organizational accountability, and evaluate program effectiveness.
* Collaborate with the Director of Youth Program Operations, develop, coordinate, and manage staff trainings and professional development for full-time and part-time staff.
* Conduct program evaluations, analyze data, and prepare quarterly reports that support performance measurement and continuous improvement efforts.
* Develop relationships with internal and external stakeholders and support collaboration and resource sharing among youth centers, schools, community organizations, families, and public safety partners.
* Perform related duties as required.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

***Education/Experience***

* A bachelor’s degree required, preferably in a related field; master’s degree preferred.
* Three (3) years of out-of-school time (OST) program management experience required.
* Five (5) years of experience supervising staff and working with diverse populations required.
* Demonstrated knowledge of positive youth development principles and experience in program development required.
* Experience developing and implementing systems for program delivery, staff training, program quality improvement, evaluation, and assessment processes.
* Demonstrated ability to influence without direct line authority and provide leadership in developing and sustaining collaborative internal and external partnerships.
* Experience working with community agencies, youth, and schools required.
* Strong interpersonal, communication, presentation, writing, organizational, and facilitation skills required.
* An equivalent combination of education, training, and relevant lived or professional experience may be considered.

***Knowledge,******Skills,******and*** ***Abilities:***
-------------------------------------------------------

* Deep knowledge of positive youth development, out-of-school time program models, and trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and linguistically responsive practices.
* Skill in designing, facilitating, and evaluating staff training using adult learning principles, coaching strategies, and reflective supervision techniques.
* Ability to develop and implement program quality frameworks and assessment tools and use qualitative and quantitative data to support continuous improvement efforts.
* Strong facilitation, presentation, and written communication skills, including the ability to convene diverse stakeholders and lead collaborative problem-solving initiatives across multiple sites.
* Proficiency with data management, project management, and budgeting tools and systems.
* Ability to manage complex projects, timelines, and competing priorities while ensuring compliance with applicable policies and regulations.
* Strong interpersonal, organizational, and leadership skills with the ability to build and sustain collaborative partnerships.
* Commitment to anti-racism, diversity, equity, and inclusion.
* Ability to work and interact effectively with individuals and groups across diverse identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.

### **SUPERVISION****RECEIVED:**

### **Works****under****the****general****direction****of****the****Division****Head****of****Cambridge****Youth****Programs;****exercises****considerable independent judgment; and has work reviewed through conferences, reports, and achievement of program** **objectives.**

### 

### **SUPERVISION****EXERCISED:**

### **May****directly****supervise****two full-time staff members:****an****Administrative Assistant and a Youth Connector.****Also provides functional supervision and coaching support to Program Directors and staff across assigned youth center sites; may oversee consultants or interns engaged in training, program quality, and evaluation** **initiatives.**

### 

### **WORK** **ENVIRONMENT:**

### **Work is performed in a standard office setting with fluorescent lighting, carpeted floors, air conditioning, and moderate noise levels. Evening and weekend hours may be required to support operational needs.**

### 

### **PHYSICAL** **DEMANDS:**

### **Ability****to****use****a****computer****to****access,****input,****and****retrieve****information;****answer****telephones;****maintain****multiple****files; and lift items weighing up to 25 pounds. Ability to travel throughout the City of Cambridge to multiple Youth Center locations as required.**

*The City of Cambridge's workforce, like the community it serves, is diverse. Applicants must have the ability to**work and interact**effectively**with**individuals**and**groups**with**a variety of**identities, cultures, backgrounds, and ideologies.*

**COMPENSATION PHILOSOPHY**

The City of Cambridge is committed to providing fair, transparent, and competitive compensation to all employees. The salary range listed in this job posting reflects the full range for this position's pay grade (Steps 1–10). New employees joining the organization are hired within the hiring range, Steps 1 through 5, with placement at the midpoint reserved for the most qualified candidates. Starting placement is based on directly related education and experience relative to the minimum qualifications of the position, required licenses or certifications, internal equity with current employees, and relevant labor market factors. Employees progress through the 10 steps over time through the City's established step and pay progression policies.

This compensation philosophy applies to non‑union positions. For union positions, please refer to the applicable collective bargaining agreement.

Current City employees applying to another position should refer to the Compensation & Classification Manual for the policies governing promotions, lateral transfers, and other internal salary changes.

**ABOUT THE CITY OF CAMBRIDGE**

The City of Cambridge is a diverse and vibrant community that 120,000 residents of different ethnic, racial, religious, U.S. nationals and other backgrounds call home. We take pride in our City’s diversity and strive to create a workplace that is reflective of the community we serve - one in which all employees can thrive. The City is also deeply committed to creating an environment in which all our employees are treated equitably and feel included. In joining our team, you would work in a workplace environment that advances and values antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion (ADEI), and that is committed to embedding ADEI best practices and tenets in all aspects of our work. City of Cambridge residents are especially encouraged to apply to job openings.

**EQUAL OPPORTUNITY / AFFIRMATIVE ACTION**

The City of Cambridge is an Affirmative Action/Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate based on race, color, sex, religion, age, national origin, disability, or any other protected category. Women, minorities, veterans, members of the LGBTQ+ Community, and persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. The City is committed to advancing a workforce culture of antiracism, diversity, equity, and inclusion. Auxiliary aids and services, written materials in alternative formats, and reasonable modifications in policies and procedures will be provided to qualified individuals with disabilities free of charge, upon request by contacting Human Resources at humanresources@cambridgema.gov.

new_roles.description:
**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-264366 **Date posted** 19/11/2026

 

**WHY JOIN US?**

At AstraZeneca, we are dedicated to being a Great Place to Work, where you are empowered to push the boundaries of science and unleash your entrepreneurial spirit. With an ambitious goal of delivering 20 new medicines by 2030, there is no better place to make a difference in medicine, for patients, and in society.

Join us on this exciting journey to pioneer the future of healthcare. Our inclusive culture champions diversity and collaboration, and we are always committed to lifelong learning, growth, and development. As part of our team, you'll contribute to groundbreaking advancements that will shape a healthier future for people everywhere. Be a catalyst for change at AstraZeneca, where your work will have a real impact on improving people's lives.

Recognizing the importance of individualized flexibility, our ways of working allow employees to balance personal and work commitments while ensuring we continue to create a strong culture of collaboration and teamwork by **engaging face-to-face in our offices 3 days a week**. Our head office is purposely designed with collaboration in mind, providing space where teams can come together to strategize, brainstorm and connect on key projects.**This is a hybrid role located in Gaithersburg, Maryland. Candidates must reside within commuting distance of Gaithersburg or be willing to relocate for this opportunity.****About the Role**

The Director, Quality Systems is a senior leader within Development Quality Biologics (DQB), accountable for strategy, governance, performance, and continuous improvement of the Quality Management System (QMS) supporting Biologics Development.

The role provides leadership and oversight for critical Quality Systems processes, including Deviation and CAPA Management, Change Control, Quality Risk Management, Inspection Management, Documentation Management, Quality Management Review, and GxP Training and Learning. The Director also leads Business Process Management (BPM) within DQB, ensuring business and quality processes are effectively owned, defined, governed, measured, and continuously improved.

The Director leads a team of up to 12 employees and partners broadly across DQB, Biopharmaceutical Development (BPD), Development Quality, Global Quality, and other functions to deliver a compliant, efficient, risk-based, and future-ready QMS.

**Key Accountabilities**

* Lead the DQB Quality Management System, providing strategy, governance, and oversight to ensure Quality Systems are compliant, effective, risk-based, phase-appropriate, and fit for purpose.

* Provide leadership for core Quality Systems processes, including deviations and CAPAs, change control, quality risk management, inspection management and readiness, documentation management, Quality Management Review, GxP training, and associated metrics and trending. Champion excellence in fundamental Quality processes like root cause analysis and effective CAPA development, risk mitigation, inspection readiness, and continuous improvement.

* Lead Business Process Management within DQB, establishing clear process ownership, governance, performance measures, and improvement mechanisms. Drive simplification, standardization, and elimination of non-value-added activities while maintaining appropriate compliance and control.

* Drive QMS performance and continuous improvement through meaningful metrics, trending, management review, risk identification, and data-driven insights. Translate QMS performance into clear priorities and actions for DQB and BPD leadership.

* Ensure sustainable inspection readiness, including effective preparation, execution, response, and follow-up for regulatory inspections and audits, ensuring learnings are incorporated into Quality System improvements.

* Lead and develop a team of up to 12 employees, building capability in Quality Systems, process ownership, risk-based decision-making, data and digital fluency, continuous improvement, and critical thinking.

**Shaping the QMS of the Future**

The Director will play a key role in evolving the DQB QMS to support the future needs of the Biologics’ development portfolio and AZ's 2030 Vision. The role will champion a phase-appropriate, risk-based and digitally enabled QMS that is fit for purpose, reduces unnecessary complexity, enables innovation, and maintains strong regulatory compliance and patient-focused quality.

The Director role will lead the responsible adoption of AI, advanced analytics, automation, digital workflows, and other emerging technologies to simplify processes, reduce manual work, improve knowledge access, identify quality signals earlier, and strengthen data-driven decision-making. The role will help advance the QMS from primarily retrospective management of quality events toward a more proactive and predictive model, while ensuring appropriate human accountability, transparency, data integrity, traceability, and GxP controls.

**Measures of Success**

**Success in the role will be demonstrated through:**

* A compliant, effective, phase-appropriate, and fit-for-purpose QMS that enables delivery of the AZ portfolio.

* Strong QMS health, including effective management of deviations, CAPAs, changes, risks, training, documentation, and inspection readiness.

* Mature Business Process Management with clear accountability and measurable improvements in process effectiveness, efficiency, and simplicity.

* A Quality Management Review with processes and metrics that provide actionable insights, identify emerging risks, and enable timely leadership decisions.

* Increased and appropriately governed use of data, digital solutions, automation, and AI to improve QMS performance and reduce administrative burden.

* A capable, engaged team prepared to lead and support the QMS of the future.

**Essential Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in a scientific or technical discipline such as Pharmacy, Biology, Chemistry, Biotechnology, or a related field.
* 10+ years of progressive experience within Quality in the pharmaceutical or biopharmaceutical industry, including significant people leadership experience.
* Demonstrated experience leading a sizeable (10+) Quality team/function and delivering measurable improvements.
* Strong knowledge of Quality Management Systems (QMS), including deviations/CAPA, change control, Quality Risk Management, documentation, training, and inspection readiness.
* Strong understanding of GxP requirements, regulatory expectations, and SOP-driven environments, with experience driving compliance and sustainable Quality practices.
* Experience using Quality metrics, trending, risk indicators, and management review to identify priorities and drive continuous improvement.
* Demonstrated experience leading complex, cross-functional initiatives and significant process or organizational change, including management of resources, stakeholders, vendors, and budgets.
* Strong leadership, communication, and influencing skills with the ability to partner across Quality, Development, and senior leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience within biologics, Development Quality, or pharmaceutical development.
* Experience managing managers or leading leaders within a Quality organization.
* Experience with Business Process Management, Operational Excellence, Lean, or continuous improvement.
* Experience leading QMS transformation, harmonization, or process simplification.
* Experience with digital Quality systems, automation, advanced analytics, or AI-enabled Quality solutions in a regulated environment.
* Experience with non-GMP biopharmaceutical work and its phase-appropriate requirements for compliance.

**SO, WHAT’S NEXT?**

To be considered for this exciting opportunity, please complete the full application on our website at your earliest convenience – it is the only way that our Recruiter and Hiring Manager can know that you feel well qualified for this opportunity. If you know someone who would be a great fit, please share this posting with them.

**Are you interested in working at AZ, apply today!**

AstraZeneca is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to diversity and inclusion and providing a workplace that is free from discrimination. AstraZeneca is committed to accommodating persons with disabilities. Such accommodation is available on request in respect of all aspects of the recruitment, assessment and selection process and may be requested by emailing AZCHumanResources@astrazeneca.com.

Benefits offered included a qualified retirement program [401(k) plan]; paid vacation and holidays; paid leaves; and, health benefits including medical, prescription drug, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms and conditions of the applicable plans.*

If hired, employee will be in an “at-will position” and the Company reserves the right to modify base pay (as well as any other discretionary payment or compensation program) at any time, including for reasons related to individual performance, Company or individual department/team performance, and market factors.*

new_roles.title: Director of Quality
new_roles.description:
**About Us:**

BW Design Group is a fully integrated architecture, engineering, construction, system integration, and consulting firm committed to helping our clients realize their most critical goals from Strategy to Commercialization. As the only firm born from a manufacturing technology company to become an independent and fully integrated firm, we combine deep domain expertise in the manufacturing environment with an approach that is built to serve the dynamic needs of our clients. Rooted in our distinct culture of Truly Human Leadership, we cultivate the leaders who will define tomorrow and partner with our clients in the food & beverage, life sciences, industrial, and advanced technology industries to build the future of manufacturing and technology. 
 
Barry-Wehmiller is a diversified global supplier of engineering consulting and manufacturing technology for the packaging, corrugating, sheeting and paper-converting industries. By blending people-centric leadership with disciplined operational strategies and purpose-driven growth, Barry-Wehmiller has become a $3 billion organization with nearly 12,000 team members united by a common belief: to use the power of business to build a better world. 
 

**Job Description:**

**Who You’ll Work With**

At BW Design Group, you'll collaborate with experienced leaders, technical specialists, and subject matter experts to solve complex challenges for some of the world's leading companies. You'll join a growing team of more than 2000 professionals across nearly 50 U.S. offices where you'll be empowered to make an impact, develop your expertise, and grow your career.

As Director, Quality for our Boston office, you will join our Regulatory Compliance Practice, leading the local quality team while serving as a trusted quality subject matter expert, industry thought leader, and client lead for life science clients across New England.

**What You’ll Do**

This role balances hands-on, billable project/service delivery with growing our Boston team, client relationships, and reputation in the industry.

* Lead a team of quality professionals and interface with clients
* Train, mentor, and recruit talent, championing the career growth of early-career professionals through Individual Development Plans and on-the-job coaching.
* Serve as the firm’s local quality SME across QMS maturity, supplier quality, CAPA and deviations, audit and inspection readiness, remediation, and product development, and advise clients on evolving regulatory guidance.
* Lead delivery of multiple concurrent projects, owning scope, budget, schedule, quality, risk, and client satisfaction.
* Drive thought leadership through publications, white papers, and industry conference presentations, and contribute to firmwide quality standards and best practices.
* Maintain a personal billable utilization target of approximately 60–70% while managing team staffing and utilization to meet billable hours goals.
Develop scopes, estimates, and proposals, and expand engagements with new and existing clients through your industry network. 

**What You’ll Bring**

* A minimum of fifteen years of increasing responsibility in quality services and project management for life sciences, biotech, medical device, or other FDA regulated projects.
* A minimum of five years of people leadership experience, including hiring, coaching, and developing quality professionals.
* Proven success in a consulting or professional services environment, including meeting billable utilization goals and leading client relationships
* Experience leading quality teams across capital project handover, QMS establishment, quality audits, root cause and deviation resolution, and remediation planning.
* Working knowledge of quality regulations for medical device, pharmaceuticals, biologics, C&GT, and aseptic/sterile manufacturing (21 CFR Parts 11, 210/211, and 820; ISO 13485; EU GMP), along with cGMP, good documentation practices, and risk management tools (ICH Q9, FMEA, PFMEA/DFMEA).
* Recognized industry expertise and thought leadership through publications, presentations, or professional associations such as ISPE, PDA, or ASQ; a Boston/New England life science network is preferred.
* Strong communication and technical writing skills, with experience developing proposals and estimates is preferred.
* A willingness to travel regionally to client sites throughout the Boston/New England area, as well as for company sponsored meetings, training, and industry events.
A Bachelor of Science in engineering or a related technical degree; an advanced degree or ASQ certification is preferred. 

 

Our culture and commitment to our people is what sets us apart. We foster an environment of mutual respect, integrity, and unconditional interest in the individual and collective success of our professionals. Our model and entrepreneurial mindset offer a rewarding, challenging, and highly flexible path.

 

As Director of Quality, you will build a meaningful and fulfilling career with the support of professional development resources and mentorships including our First Year Experience program, Individual Development Plans, and Career Path resources and tools. You will be surrounded by exceptional talent who will support your development as both a world-class professional and a highly effective leader.

 

*At Barry-Wehmiller we recognize that people come with a wealth of experience and talent beyond just the technical requirements of a job. If your experience is close to what you see listed here, please still consider applying. We know that our differences often can bring about innovation, excellence and meaningful work—therefore, people from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply to our positions. Please let us know if you require reasonable accommodations during the interview process.*

Barry-Wehmiller is an equal opportunity employer. M/F/D/V This organization uses E-Verify. 
 
Applicants may be subject to pre-employment screening which may include drug screening, reference checks, employment verifications, background screening and/or skills assessments. 
 

**Company:**

Design Group

new_roles.title: Director Quality
new_roles.description:
### **Activités**

**SUMMARY:**

Reporting to the President, C.E.O., Directs and coordinates activities of personnel at all Hutchinson Sealing Systems facilities engaged in Quality Management System to prevent or eliminate defects in new or existing products or process by performing the following duties personally or through subordinates. This position is designated as a sensitive function for quality, engineering, manufacturing, supplier, audit, compliance, and operational information, including quality performance data, customer requirements, product and process development information, audit findings, corrective actions, supplier performance records, and proprietary company information. The incumbent is responsible for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of information assets in accordance with company policies and customer requirements.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Include the following. Other duties may be assigned.

* Analyzes, evaluates, and presents information concerning factors such as quality performance, production capabilities, manufacturing problems, customer quality trends, and quality planning of new products for consideration by other members of the management team.
* Presents and evaluates alternative methods and procedures to establish standardized quality systems based on best practices.
* Participates with other top management personnel in formulating and establishing company policies, operating procedures, and goals.
* Participates in review of product development activities and APQP milestones.
* Conducts Quality System Management review meetings with top management to assess performance and compliance to customer quality requirements.
* Reviews technical problems and procedures of departments and recommends solutions to problems or changes in procedures.
* Confers with engineers and managers about quality assurance of new products and process to improve manufacturing capability.
* Reviews technical publications, articles, and abstracts to stay abreast of technical and quality system developments in industry.
* Travel required on a frequent basis to suppliers and customer facilities as well as other Hutchinson facilities.
* Provides internal quality system audit of Hutchinson Sealing Systems locations.

**EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE:**

Master's degree (M.A.) or equivalent; or four to ten years’ related experience and/or training; or equivalent combination of education and experience.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Qualifications may be waived by management. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS:**

None.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:**

Manages subordinates in department. Is responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of this unit. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the organization's policies and applicable laws. Responsibilities include interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complains and resolving problems.

**TEAM SKILLS:**

Hutchinson is built around teamwork. This position requires the use of good team skills such as cooperation, information sharing, task sharing, timely completion of assignments, good listening and communication skills and overall respect for other team members.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS:**

Ability to read, analyze, and interpret common scientific and technical journals, financial reports, and legal documents. Ability to respond to common inquiries or complaints from customers, regulatory agencies, or members of the business community. Ability to write speeches and articles for publication that conform to prescribed style and format. Ability to effectively present information to top management, public groups and/or boards of directors.

**MATHEMATICAL SKILLS:**

Ability to work with mathematical concepts such as probability and statistical inference, and fundamentals of plane and solid geometry and trigonometry. Ability to apply concepts such as fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions to practical situations.

**COMPUTER SKILLS:**

Ability to use word processing, spreadsheet applications. Must be familiar with internet research, Microsoft Office software, and the use of e-mail.

**REASONING ABILITY:**

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts, and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract and concrete variables.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT:**

The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts. The employee is occasionally exposed to fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals. The noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS:**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to walk; sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; climb or balance; stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl; and talk or hear. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds and occasionally lift and/or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close, vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

**HEALTH AND SAFETY:**

Must actively support our Health Safety and Environmental policy, immediately report all Safety hazards and correct them when able to safely do so, participate in all required Safety Training, meetings, inspects, and use all required PPE.

Tout au long de votre carrière, vous bénéficiez de missions variées et de formations sur mesure. Vous développez pleinement votre potentiel dans un environnement qui encourage l’innovation et l’excellence. Intégrez des équipes engagées et solidaires, où la réussite se construit ensemble.

new_roles.title: Senior Director, Manufacturing, Power Transmission, NA
new_roles.description:
**Date:** Nov 24, 2026

**Location:** Denver, CO, US, 80202

**Company:** Gates Corporation

Are you inspired by challenging the status quo? Do you thrive in collaborative environments that drive results? If so, Gates could be for you.

Gates is a leading manufacturer of application-specific fluid power and power transmission solutions. We push the boundaries of material science to engineer solutions that continually exceed customer expectations.

Let's simplify it, think belts and hoses. Found in motorcycles, conveyor belts, cars, tractors, blenders, vacuum cleaners, bicycles, & 3D printers just to name a few. Because why not do it all?

**Short Description**
---------------------

Gates Corporation has an exciting opportunity for a Sr. Director of Manufacturing, Power Transmission, North America (5 sites). This role will provide leadership and guidance in the development and implementation of product and process improvements for optimal and efficient operation of new and existing products and processes within Gates' North America Power Transmission facilities.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**
-----------------------------------------

* Manage Power Transmission plant operations to deliver daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual operating plan.
* Responsible for delivering on Safety, Cost, Delivery, Quality and Inventory targets for the US, Canada, and Mexico Power Transmission facilities.
* Drive sustainable, predictable weekly, monthly, quarterly output/revenue.
* Manage 5 Power Transmission Plants and Integrated Supply Chain.
* Develop trust and alignment with commercial team to profitably grow business.
* Successfully communicate execution and results to senior executives as well as those within the business unit.
* Evaluate and determine key investments in equipment, infrastructure, and talent.
* Provide a safe workplace environment by enforcing all safety regulations, policies, rules, and procedures.
* Utilizing the principles of the Gates Production System (GPS), produce product that meets or exceeds Gates and customer's expectations for a quality product at an expected cost.
* Develop a superior workforce that emphasizes safety, quality, continuous improvement, high performance, and employee retention.
* Monitors the performance of all operations within the department to identify opportunities for improvement and increased efficiency.
* Develops plans and oversees all aspects of production including equipment purchases, staffing needs, work schedules, and material requirements.
* Plans, organizes, executes, and monitors plant output objectives to meet customer shipment, cost, quality, and revenue goals; resolves issues to maintain smooth flow of work; drives product quality improvement initiatives; coordinates with materials, and process engineering, to achieve initiatives.

**Keys to Success**
-------------------

* Advanced knowledge of lean manufacturing systems processes, products, and customers.
* Strong commitment to safety and a track record of continuously improving safety in operations.
* Demonstrated ability to effectively engage and function within matrixed teams' environment including Finance, Commercial, Engineering, HR, and Marketing.
* Performs work without appreciable direction while providing leadership on future manufacturing direction and continually improving organizational policies in the manufacturing area of the organization.
* Excellent oral, presentation, written and listening skills.
* Commitment to building a culture accountable to serving customers and employees with an urgency to meet or exceed expectations.
* Track record of, and commitment to, doing things the right way.
* Ability to coach, mentor and develop talent within the company.
* Demonstrated successful change management experience.
* The ability to articulate a compelling vision to all levels of the organization to accomplish cultural improvements which are sustainable, and people oriented.
* Proven ability to successfully develop and implement systems and processes which deliver quality, customer satisfaction, efficiency, and safety goals.
* Strong business and financial acumen.
* Demonstrates knowledge of establishing milestones and implementation (execution skills) while meeting commitments, prioritizing, scheduling, planning, anticipating obstacles, and managing risk.

**Supervisory Responsibilities, Travel Requirements, Work Environment**
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

* 5 direct reports.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally 90+%.
* World Class Manufacturing facilities engaged in high volume manufacturing and manufacturing support processes.

**Requirements and Preferred Skills**
-------------------------------------

* BA/BS in industrial, mechanical engineering, or business administration (MBA preferred)
* Minimum of 15+ years' multi-plant managerial experience leading manufacturing and operations teams in industrial, automotive supplier or industrial technology
* Experience in both Union and non-Union environment
* Expertise in plant automation/robotics and/or experience in automating plant operations
* Experience managing an industrial manufacturing environment as a hands-on senior operational leader.
* Experience in a high growth atmosphere with rapid hiring and training.
* Experience working with manufacturing-based technology, processes, and principles.
* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without company sponsorship.
 

**Physical Requirements**

* The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
* Plant: Move minimum of 30lbs., spatial awareness/depth perception, walk, climb, bend at the waist, reach, forceful use of hand tools, vocal projection.
* While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, tools, or controls; see, talk or hear. The employee is required to stand, walk, and reach with hands and arms.
* Personal protective equipment will be required when physically in manufacturing settings, including hearing protection, eye protection, and safety shoes.
 

#LI-LP1

**Pay & Benefits**

* Full-Time
* Salary range from $220,000 to $265,000
* Bonus Eligible
* Equity Eligible
* Relocation is provided
* Medical, Dental, Vision insurance and other voluntary benefit options: benefits begin on the first day of the month immediately following your date of hire
* Eligible for Flexible Time Off
* 401(k): 3% company contribution and additional 3% company match
* Tuition Reimbursement
 

**Why Gates?**

Founded in 1911 in Denver, Colorado, Gates is publicly traded on the NYSE. While we might operate in a vast amount of time zones we operate as 'One Gates' and have a common goal of pushing the boundaries of materials science. We invest in our people, bringing real-world experience that enables us to solve our customers' diverse challenges of today and anticipate those of tomorrow.

 

**Work Environment**

Gates is an Equal Opportunity and is committed to ensuring equal employment opportunities for all job applicants and employees. Employment decisions are based upon job-related reasons regardless of race, sex, color, religion, age, disability, pregnancy, citizenship, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, genetic information, marital status, or any other consideration defined by law.
 
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit; use hands and fingers to work with objects, tools, or controls; and use office equipment including computers, telephones, and/or copiers/scanners. The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 10 pounds.
 
For individuals assigned and/or hired to work in Colorado, Gates is required by law to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role. This compensation range is specific to the State of Colorado and takes into account various factors that are considered in making compensation decisions, including but not limited to the candidate's relevant experience, qualifications, skills, competencies, and proficiency for the role.

 

**Nearest Major Market:** Denver

new_roles.title: Director of Production
new_roles.description:
**Company Overview**

Delta Galil USA, Inc. is a global manufacturer and marketer of branded and private label apparel products for men, women and children. Since its inception in 1975, the company has continually endeavored to create products that follow a body-before-fabric philosophy, placing equal emphasis on comfort, aesthetics and quality. Delta Galil develops innovative seamless apparel, including bras, shapewear and socks; intimate apparel for women; underwear for men, including under its owned brands Schiesser, Eminence, Organic Basics and Athena; babywear, activewear, sleepwear and loungewear, including under its owned P.J. Salvage and Delta brands. Delta Galil also designs, develops, markets and sells branded denim and apparel under the brand 7 For All Mankind®, and ladies’ and kids’ apparel under the brand Splendid®. In addition, it sells its products under brand names licensed to the company, including adidas, Wolford, Wilson, Columbia, Tommy Hilfiger and others.

**Position Overview**

At Delta Galil, great product only matters if it reaches the shelf at the right cost, at the right quality and on time. As Director, Production & Sourcing, you’ll make that happen. You’ll own Sourcing and Production for your programs, from the first seasonal projection to the moment goods land at our Distribution Center, steering a global network of mills, factories and overseas offices that supply some of the biggest names in mass-market retail.

This is a role with real levers. You’ll negotiate the costs that shape the department’s margin, decide where programs are placed and how capacity is allocated, and lead the cross-functional team through every approval milestone, from BOM handoff to TOP. You’ll partner every day with Design, Planning and our Domestic and Offshore QA teams, and you’ll be the person everyone looks to when a delivery is at risk.

You’ll thrive here if you’re a natural negotiator and a hands-on leader who knows a garment down to its cost components, stays calm when a test fails or a vessel slips, and gets energy from turning a complex calendar into on-time deliveries.

**Key Responsibilities**

Sourcing, Costing & Vendor Strategy

* Share seasonal projections with mills and factories early, locking in key delivery dates and a generic TNA well ahead of order placement.
* Lead program-level cost negotiations that drive best costs and help the department meet or beat seasonal margin goals.
* Build and grow a strong vendor matrix that supports the business’s long-term needs.
* Place programs with overseas mills, factories and offices on time, with program-specific TNAs, the right capacity allocation and production plans that hit contracted deliveries.

Production Execution & Approvals

* Lead the cross-functional team through program TNAs, driving approvals from completed BOM handoff through color and components, fit, pre-production, testing and TOP.
* Work with stakeholders to resolve approval issues and testing failures quickly, escalating to leadership when needed.
* Assess production issues for delivery impact and lead cross-functional decisions on quality levels and ship-mode changes to protect customer deliveries.

Planning, Capacity & Delivery

* Partner with the Planning team to support the business at the right stock levels.
* Own and communicate monthly program capacity plans to mills and factories, flagging loading or capacity risks early.
* Keep POs current in the system, hold factories to timely bookings and approve vessel schedules that line up with customer deliveries.
* Build and maintain delivery reports for weekly team review.

Quality & Continuous Improvement

* Partner with Domestic and Offshore QA, sharing planned program allocation before placement.
* Champion critical QA steps before, during and at the end of production so product arrives at the Distribution Center free of quality issues and every customer order ships on time.
* Work with management to improve process flow and roll out new initiatives.

 
Requirements: 
 

* Minimum years of apparel experience across Product Development, Production, QA and Testing.
* Experience supplying a big-box, mass-market retailer such as Target or Walmart.
* Cut-and-sew knits experience (activewear strongly preferred).
* Deep knowledge of manufacturing, testing and quality control, including fabrics, trims and garment cost components (YY, CM, AU).
* A proven team leader with exceptional negotiation and problem-solving skills with factories and material suppliers.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect with factories, suppliers and internal teams at every level.
* Highly organized and detail-oriented, with strong follow-up, a sense of urgency and the ability to juggle multiple projects and teams.
* Advanced Excel skills (VLOOKUPs, pivot tables) and proficiency in Word and Outlook.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Activewear, intimates, loungewear, or knits experience.
* CPM and SMV knowledge, with a thorough understanding of cost component breakdowns.
* Experience traveling overseas to mills and factories.

**This is a hybrid role, with 4 days in our NJ office.**

**PAY RATE: $150,000/yr-$170,000/yr**

At Delta Galil, we strive to hire and nurture amazing talent. Actual salaries will vary depending on factors including but not limited to experience, specialized skills, and internal alignment.

DIVERSITY VISION STATEMENT:

We are committed to creating an inclusive environment that welcomes and values the differences among all of our associates, customers, suppliers, and the communities in which we live and conduct business. We are an equal employment opportunity for minorities, females, protected veterans, and the disabled.

We are committed to providing equal opportunities in employment and treating our associates and applicants without discrimination based on their race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, citizenship, disability, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected factor.

 
Hybrid position:
 
Hybrid 
 
Company Benefits: 
 

As a Delta Galil Associate, you’ll be part of a global fashion company that values innovation, craftsmanship, and people. We’re committed to offering comprehensive and competitive benefits that reflect our culture of care, creativity, and collaboration — but most importantly, benefits that fit you.

Our diverse range of programs is designed to support your total well-being — empowering you to make the best choices for yourself, your loved ones, and your lifestyle.

Below are a few of the benefits available to our Associates:

* Multi-brand merchandise discount, including Splendid, 7 For All Mankind, and PJ Salvage
* Comprehensive Health Coverage: Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance, as well as Basic Life/Voluntary Life/Disability/Critical Illness
* Financial Wellness: 401(k) Retirement Program with Company match and 529 College Savings Plan, as well as Tax-Advantage Health & Transit Accounts
* Personal and sick time off, vacation time, floating days, and company-observed holidays
* Paid Volunteer Time Off to dedicate your skills and time towards charitable activities
* From weekly breakfasts and monthly milestone celebrations to leadership-led panels, and, team-building events, we offer plenty of fun ways to connect—both in person and virtually

**ABOUT US:** 
With a dedication to our people and our products, The Honickman Companies® are collectively one of the largest independent beverage employers in the country. Our Pepsi business includes distribution for brands like Pepsi-Cola, Starbucks, Lipton Teas, Gatorade, Evian and more, throughout the 5 Borough’s, Long Island, Westchester and Pennsauken NJ. If you are excited to work with some of the biggest brands in the world, in the biggest brand market in the world, come see what we have to offer. a passionate, self-motivated, and detail-oriented team player who is committed to the success of our customers. You will focus on growing and developing existing clients, as well as generating new business by identifying, implementing and executing new strategies.
 
 
**SUMMARY:** 
Leads the day-to-day operations of a large-scale beverage manufacturing facility, with overall accountability for Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing. Establishes operating priorities and develops leaders and teams to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective and efficient production. Applies practical business judgment, disciplined execution and continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System to improve plant performance and support the Company’s business strategy.
 
 
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:** 

* Provides visible, hands-on leadership and direction for all plant operations, including Production, Quality, Maintenance, Shipping, Receiving and Warehousing.
* Establishes clear operating priorities, performance expectations and accountability; aligns staffing, resources and production plans with customer and business requirements.
* Ensures production schedules are achieved while meeting safety, food safety, quality, efficiency, cost and customer service expectations.
* Monitors and acts upon key performance indicators, including safety performance, schedule attainment, production efficiency, equipment utilization, downtime, waste, labor productivity, inventory accuracy and service levels.
* Identifies operating constraints and performance gaps; leads root cause analysis, corrective actions and practical solutions that improve throughput, reliability and execution.
* Ensures manufacturing processes, standard operating procedures and controls are documented, consistently followed and improved as business needs evolve.
* Partners with Quality leadership to maintain effective food safety, sanitation, preventive control and quality systems and to resolve customer complaints, audit findings and corrective actions promptly.
* Provides leadership and oversight for preventive and predictive maintenance, work-order execution and equipment reliability; aligns maintenance priorities with production requirements and long-term asset needs.
* Supports capital planning and execution, including equipment upgrades, facility improvements and other investments that improve safety, capacity, reliability or cost performance.
* Oversees warehouse, inventory control, shipping and receiving operations to ensure accurate inventory, efficient material flow, appropriate space utilization and timely customer shipments.
* Drives practical, results-oriented continuous improvement through the Honickman Management Operating System; ensures initiatives produce measurable gains in safety, quality, productivity, waste, cost and equipment effectiveness.
* Develops and manages operating plans and budgets; controls labor, overtime, waste, operating expense and other key financial measures while balancing service and production needs.
* Leads, develops and holds department managers and supervisors accountable; builds leadership capability, cross-functional collaboration and a strong succession pipeline.
* Builds a culture of teamwork, communication, employee engagement and ownership by maintaining a regular presence on the plant floor and engaging employees at all levels.
* Establishes productive relationships with employees and union representatives; ensures consistent application of Company policies, procedures and applicable collective bargaining agreements and addresses employee relations matters promptly and professionally.
* Promotes a proactive safety culture and ensures compliance with applicable OSHA, environmental, food safety, regulatory and customer requirements; directs timely incident investigations and corrective actions.
* Provides accurate and timely operating reports, communicates plant performance and risks, and recommends actions needed to achieve business objectives.
* Performs other related duties as required and assigned

**KNOWLEDGE AND SKILLS:** 
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
 

* Comprehensive knowledge of large-scale manufacturing operations, production planning, equipment reliability, quality systems, food safety, warehousing, distribution and inventory controls.
* Strong business and financial acumen, including the ability to develop operating plans, manage budgets and labor costs, interpret performance data and translate findings into action.
* Practical knowledge of continuous improvement, root cause analysis, standard work and performance management; ability to implement solutions that deliver measurable operational results.
* Demonstrated ability to lead a complex operation through multiple levels of management and to establish priorities, accountability and disciplined execution across functions.
* Working knowledge of OSHA, environmental and food-manufacturing regulatory requirements and the ability to maintain effective safety, quality and compliance systems.
* Proven ability to lead and develop managers and supervisors, engage a diverse hourly workforce and build effective labor-management relationships in a union environment.
* Excellent judgment, problem-solving, organizational and follow-up skills; able to manage competing priorities and make timely decisions in a fast-paced operation.
* Effective oral, written and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate expectations, performance, risks and recommendations to employees, leaders and senior management.
* Strong computer skills, including Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook; familiarity with manufacturing, maintenance, warehouse and performance-reporting systems.

**EDUCATION AND WORK EXPERIENCE:** 

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Operations Management or a related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing leadership experience will be considered.
* Minimum 10 years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience, including prior overall responsibility as a plant, site or operations leader for a large, complex manufacturing facility.
* Prior responsibility for multiple functions, including Production, Quality, Maintenance and Warehouse/Distribution operations, with demonstrated success improving plant performance.
* Beverage manufacturing experience strongly preferred; significant food manufacturing experience will also be considered.
* Experience leading a unionized manufacturing workforce strongly preferred.
* Experience managing operating budgets, labor costs, productivity, equipment reliability, quality, safety and overall plant performance required.
* Any equivalent combination of education, experience and training that provides the required knowledge, skills and abilities.

**PHYSICAL DEMANDS / WORK ENVIRONMENT / TRAVEL:** 

* Manufacturing, warehouse and office environments; regular presence on the production floor is required.
* Must be able to work around moving equipment, elevated noise levels, temperature variation and other conditions typical of a beverage manufacturing facility, with required personal protective equipment.
* Ability to move throughout the facility and occasionally lift, push or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to work a flexible schedule and respond to operational needs outside normal business hours; limited travel may be required.

**COMPENSATION RANGE:** 
Potential earning is from $190,000.00 - $215,000.00 annually
 
 
The statements herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees and are not to be construed as an exhaustive list of responsibilities, duties, and skills required by personnel so classified. Furthermore, they do not establish a contract for employment and are subject to change at the discretion of the company.

new_roles.title: Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation
new_roles.description:
Why Hershey:

At The Hershey Company, our culture is rooted in purpose and inspired by Milton Hershey’s enduring vision that business should create opportunity for others. Through our commitment to corporate philanthropy, we create positive impact by supporting communities, helping children thrive, and operating as a business for good. This includes our deep and long standing partnership with Milton Hershey School, where we invest in education, workforce readiness, and hands on engagement to help students succeed beyond the classroom. Supported by strategic grantmaking, product donations, cross brand collaboration, and strong employee volunteerism, Hershey offers a place to work where making a difference—locally and globally—is part of how we do business every day.

 

Location: This role is based in Hershey, PA with an expectation of 3 days in office per week.

**About the Hershey Company**
-----------------------------

At The Hershey Company, we make more moments of goodness through some of the world's most iconic brands, including Hershey's, Reese's, Kit Kat®, Jolly Rancher, Twizzlers, Dot's Pretzels, Lesser Evil and more. Our team supports a global portfolio of over 90 brands, creating opportunities to shape strategies and drive impact across a breadth of businesses that few companies can offer. While many organizations focus on a handful of brands, Hershey provides exposure to a diverse portfolio of category-leading brands enjoyed by consumers around the world. What truly sets us apart is our legacy. Inspired by Milton Hershey's belief that business should create opportunities for others, we have been making a positive impact for more than a century through our commitment to communities, philanthropy, and our longstanding partnership with Milton Hershey School. When you join Hershey, you become part of a company where purpose, growth, and making a difference are woven into how we do business every day.

**How will you fit in the big picture?**
----------------------------------------

The Director, Hershey Lean System & Manufacturing Transformation serves as the enterprise owner of the Hershey Lean Production System, or HLPS, and leads the continued evolution of Lean manufacturing across Hershey’s global manufacturing network.

 

This leader defines strategy, governance, standards, maturity model, deployment approach and capability requirements for HLPS. The Director partners with plant and functional leaders to eliminate systemic losses, strengthen operator ownership and accelerate manufacturing transformation through digital Lean, connected-worker solutions, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacity optimization.

 

The role ensures a consistent enterprise operating system while enabling each site to deploy HLPS according to its business needs, maturity and performance priorities.

**What will you do?**
---------------------

* **Own HLPS strategy and governance:** Define and maintain the HLPS architecture, principles, pillar standards, maturity model, assessment methodology, deployment roadmap and governance routines. Set the multi-year strategy and annual priorities, benchmark externally and translate proven practices into enterprise standards.
* **Lead network deployment:** Partner with Plant Managers to establish site transformation roadmaps, conduct quarterly progress reviews, address enterprise barriers, require recovery plans for material gaps and accelerate the replication of successful practices.
* **Build Lean leadership capability:** Establish role-based capability expectations, learning pathways, qualifications and coaching models for plants, Operational Excellence, engineering and frontline leaders. Build internal coaches and assessors while strengthening Daily Management, Leader Standard Work, structured problem solving, Autonomous Maintenance and Focused Improvement.
* **Advance manufacturing transformation:** Lead strategy and governance for assigned initiatives in digital Lean, connected worker, labor optimization, automation enablement and capacityoptimization. Establish prioritization, pilot criteria, stage gates, value-realization requirements and scalable deployment standards in partnership with Engineering, Supply Chain Strategy, Digital/IT and Finance.
* **Deliver measurable business value:** Translate operational losses and capability gaps into an enterprise improvement portfolio. Connect HLPS maturity to safety, quality, delivery, cost, reliability, productivity and people outcomes, partnering with Finance to validate benefits.
* **Lead and develop the team:** Guide Lean Program Leads and transformation and technical resources, focusing support on the network’s highest-value opportunities.

**Minimum Education & Requirements**
------------------------------------

**Education:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business or related discipline.
* Master’s degree preferred.

 

**Experience:**

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing, operations, engineering or Operational Excellence, including 5+ years leading leaders, multi-site programs or enterprise-scale manufacturing transformation.
* Demonstrated success designing, deploying or materially advancing Lean, Total Productive Maintenance, or a manufacturing operating system across multiple sites.
* Strong knowledge of Lean management systems, TPM, Daily Management, structured problem solving, loss analysis, asset reliability and capability development.
* Proven ability to influence Plant Managers and senior cross-functional stakeholders without relying on direct authority.
* Strong executive communication, coaching and change-leadership skills.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent demonstrated experience preferred.
* Experience in automated or capital-intensive manufacturing is strongly preferred.
* Previous leadership of a manufacturing site, major production operation or enterprise or multi-site Operational Excellence transformation strongly preferred.
* Consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, or other regulated manufacturing experience preferred.

**Benefits and Perks**
----------------------

At Hershey, we offer competitive pay and a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support your wellbeing, financial security, and life outside of work.

* Health & Wellbeing: Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus wellness programs that support your physical and mental health begin on Day 1.
* Financial Security: Competitive pay, annual incentive opportunities, and a 401(k) with company match
* Time Off & Flexibility: Paid time off, company holidays, and flexible ways of working where applicable
* Growth & Development: Career development programs, learning opportunities, and internal mobility

 

*Benefits may vary based on role, location, and eligibility.*

The anticipated base salary range for this role is $166,400 to $208,000 per year. The actual base salary offered will depend on a variety of job‑related factors, including, but not limited to, experience, skill set, education, and training. In addition to a market-competitive base salary, our Total Rewards package includes performance‑based incentives and a comprehensive, competitive benefits package designed to support overall physical, mental, and financial well‑being (as applicable). Learn more about Hershey’s benefits and all the resources Hershey provides to support our employees’ physical, emotional, and financial well‑being by visiting the Hershey Digital Employee Experience at www.askHRbenefits.hersheys.com

The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer. The policy of The Hershey Company is to extend opportunities to qualified applicants and employees on an equal basis regardless of an individual's race, color, gender, age, national origin, religion, citizenship status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, transgender status, physical or mental disability, protected veteran status, genetic information, pregnancy, or any other categories protected by applicable federal, state or local laws. 
 
The Hershey Company is an Equal Opportunity Employer - Minority/Female/Disabled/Protected Veterans. You may request a reasonable accommodation if you are unable or limited in your ability to use or access our online application process as a result of a disability. 
You can request an accommodation via phone or email.To request an accommodation via phone, please call +1 877-804-1794 and leave a voicemail with your contact information. You may also email a request for accommodation to ApplicationHelp@hersheys.com. Please be sure to include “Accommodation Needed” in the subject line. This will ensure that your email is routed to the appropriate contact who will handle your request.

new_roles.title: Plant Director
new_roles.description:
**Accelerate the possible by joining a winning Amcor team that’s transforming the packaging industry and improving lives around the world.**
============================================================================================================================================

At Amcor, we unpack possibility through our innovative and responsible packaging to provide solutions that benefit our customers, our people and our planet. More than 10,000 consumers worldwide encounter our products every second and rely on us for safe access to food, medicine and other goods. We value their trust by making safety our guiding principle. It’s our core value and integral to how we do business.

Beyond this core principle, our shared values and behaviors unite us as we work together to elevate customers, shape lives and protect the future. We champion our customers and help them succeed. We play to win – adapting quickly in an everchanging world – and make smart choices to safeguard our business, our communities and the people we serve for generations to come. And we invest in our world-class team, empowering our colleagues to unpack their potential, because we believe when our people grow, so does our business.

To learn more about playing for Team Amcor, visit www.amcor.com I LinkedIn I Glassdoor I Facebook I YouTube

**Job Description**
===================

To manage and lead overall plant operations ensuring the achievement of plant targets for Safety, Quality, Service and Cost. This will be executed through providing strong leadership to the plant team and managing the systems, equipment, people and materials according to the established policies, procedures, specifications, and customer requirements. This individual reports directly to the Director-Manufacturing. The Plant Lead Team members will report directly to the Plant Manager (typically 6-10 direct reports) Scope for this Plant Manager role is a medium to large-sized facility with typically greater than 300 employees and mid to high-level complexity.

**WHAT YOU GET TO DO**

* Leads and drives plant safety culture and puts safety first in all responsibilities.
* Leads identification of opportunities and problem areas for targeted improvement by creating, reviewing and monitoring data or reports that show performance to KPI's. (specifically, safety, quality, waste, and productivity)
* Oversees all aspects of human capital planning & management for the facility, including HC goal setting, improvement targets for KPI's, salary planning, performance management.
* Attract, hire, develop direct reports and create strong succession plans
* Ensure compliance with department safety, product safety, fire protection, Company polices/procedures, and housekeeping programs.
* Ensures effective, timely and well-developed communications for all product associates.
* Manage process control initiatives by ensuring manufacturing SOP's exist, and that they are sufficient for quality, safety, and process control.
* Leads plant budgeting processes
* Ensures execution of plant Cap-Ex
* Lead and ensure growth of CI culture by providing resources, participating in teams, and leading teams as necessary.
* Ensures facility compliance with local, state and federal regulatory agencies.
* Drives employee engagement action planning for the facility
* Leads communication to all plant associates regarding business needs and results
* Leads efforts at Best Practice sharing with other facilities
* Meets safety targets and drives a safety culture and environment to send every employee home everyday without injury.
* Meets or exceeds plant business plan and KPI’s.
* Delivers on established budget.
* Best Practices leadership
* Effective, cost-efficient planning and utilization of manpower, materials and machinery.
* Strong Human Capital planning, development and management for the facility.
* Drives High Performance Culture
* Plant talent to deliver on plan

 **WHAT WE VALUE**
* Strong financial acumen
* Results Orientation / Delivers on Plan
* Team Leadership
* Develops Organizational Capability
* Strategic Orientation / Enterprise Thinker
* Collaboration & Influence
* Change Leadership
* Facility Business Acumen/Market Knowledge

**WHAT WE WANT FROM YOU**

* A Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business administration, or related field
* 10+ years of relevant experience in a production environment
* Demonstrated passion for safety
* 7+ years of leadership experience, preferably in flexible packaging
* Lives Amcor Values and leads by example
* Proven ability to lead and drive continuous improvement
* Strong Customer Service mindset
* Strong written and verbal communication skills
* Demonstrated knowledge of BNA customers and plant capabilities
* Demonstrated understanding of drivers of plant results, including ability to interpret financial results
* Demonstrated CI knowledge, Six Sigma Black Belt certification strongly preferred

**Our Expectations**
====================

We expect our people to be guided by The Amcor Way and demonstrate our Values every day to enable the business to win. We are winning when:

* Our people are engaged and developing as part of a high-performing Amcor team
* Our customers grow and prosper from Amcor’s quality, service, and innovation
* Our investors benefit from Amcor’s consistent growth and superior returns
* The environment is better off because of Amcor’s leadership and products

**Equal Opportunity** **Employer/Minorities/Females/Disabled/Veterans/Sexual** **Orientation/Gender Identity**
==============================================================================================================

Amcor is an Equal Opportunity Employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

If you would like more information about your EEO rights as an applicant under the law, please click on the *"Know Your Rights: Workplace Discrimination is Illegal" Poster*. If, because of a medical condition or disability, you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please call 224-313-7000 and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information.

**E-Verify**
============

We verify the identity and employment authorization of individuals hired for employment in the United States.

**Compensation**
================

The starting salary for this position is expected to be between $176,100 to $242,100 depending on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Base pay information is based on national averages and a geographic differential may be applied based on work location. Position may also be eligible for Amcor’s Management Incentive Plan / Sales Incentive Plan, which is an annual bonus program based on business and individual performance, as well as medical coverage and other health and welfare benefits. The salary range provided reflects the anticipated starting salary base pay for this role at the time of this posting and does not necessarily reflect full earning potential over the course of employment. This range is applicable to positions performed in jurisdictions with pay transparency requirements, including CA, CO, CT, HI, IL, MD, MA, MN, NV, NJ, NY, RI, VT, WA, Washington DC, as well as remote roles that may be performed in these locations. Compensation for roles performed outside of these jurisdictions may vary. The Company reserves the right to modify this range at any time.

**Benefits**
============

When you join Amcor, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits and compensation package that includes:

* Medical, dental and vision plans
* Flexible time off, starting at 80 hours paid time per year for full-time salaried employees
* Company-paid holidays starting at 8 days per year and may vary by location
* Wellbeing program & Employee Assistance Program
* Health Savings Account/Flexible Spending Account
* Life insurance, AD&D, short-term & long-term disability, and voluntary benefits
* Paid Parental Leave
* Retirement Savings Plan with company match
* Tuition Reimbursement (dependent upon approval)
* Discretionary annual bonus program (initial eligibility dependent upon hire date)
