identity_held_roles.description:
**Vice President Quality**

**Global Product Distribution Quality**

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a leading global medical technology company looking to appoint a hands-on VP Global Product Distribution Quality. Reporting directly to the SVP of Corporate Quality, you will be responsible for developing and implementing business strategies to effectively manage all global product distribution quality. In this role, you will lead the global product distribution quality organization and processes, holding quality management accountability for all captive and outsourced distribution centres across every entity worldwide.

This is a genuine turnaround and organizational design mandate, rather than a caretaker or step-up role. You will step in to stabilize day-to-day operations, manage significant FDA and global regulatory scrutiny, and reshape the commercial quality infrastructure into a world-class function. For a seasoned executive who enjoys building progressive systems at scale, there is a clear path to expanded enterprise responsibility within 6 to 20 months.

**Key Responsibilities**

* **Global Distribution Governance:**
 Own quality management systems/compliance performance across captive/3PL distribution centres globally - alongside full P&L, budget, and headcount accountability for the function.
* **Turnaround & Future-State Design:**
 Audit current teams, workflows, and systems to close compliance gaps, restructuring the global commercial quality organization into a streamlined, best-in-class model.
* **FDA & Global Regulatory Execution:**
 Act as the single accountable global executive for all distribution-related regulatory inspections, audit responses, and direct agency communications, including intensive FDA engagement.
* **Quality Systems & Digital Traceability:**
 Direct the IT partnership to optimize warehouse management systems (WMS), end-to-end product traceability, inventory controls, and nonconforming product containment.
* **Enterprise Leadership:**
 Serve as the global subject matter expert for distribution quality and contribute to enterprise-wide quality strategy as a senior member of the Global Corporate Quality leadership team.

**Candidate Profile**

* **Sitting or Recent Med-Tech VP:**
 Minimum 10 years of global organizational leadership at the Vice President level within medical devices, capital equipment, or adjacent life sciences—ready to deliver impact from day one.
* **Post-Manufacturing & 3PL Mastery:**
 Deep operational expertise in commercial, supply chain, and global distribution quality across multi-site networks (upstream supplier quality into manufacturing is out of scope).
* **Proven Remediation Track Record:**
 Demonstrated success leading quality turnarounds, organizational redesigns, and systemic remediation under active FDA scrutiny.
* **Global Trade & Customs Compliance:**
 Hands-on command of international medical device regulations, import/export laws, embargoes, import bans, and regional market-entry barriers.
* **Academic Foundation:**
 Bachelor of Science in a medical or applied science discipline

**What Sets You Apart**

You lead from the front with high energy and a clear appetite for complex turnarounds. You combine sharp analytical rigor with executive presence, enabling you to influence across commercial, supply chain, and regulatory stakeholders while building high-performing global teams.

identity_held_roles.title: VP, Regional Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
**Overview**

Primo Brands is a leading branded beverage company in North America with a focus on healthy hydration. We are proud to offer an extensive and iconic portfolio of highly recognizable, sustainably sourced, and conveniently packaged branded beverages distributed across more than 150,000 retail outlets.

**Compensation:**
$185,048 - $248,596. This position is eligible for an annual bonus.

**Location:**
Dallas, TX

**Health Benefits**

Benefits of working for Primo Brands:

Medical, prescription, dental, vision, flexible spending account (FSA), dependent care flexible spending account (FSA), health savings account (HSA)

**Retirement/Investing**

401K with a 5% match, Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP)

**Insurance**

Employee Life Insurance, short and long-term disability, critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, spouse/domestic partner/child life insurance, accidental death and dismemberment

**Other Great Benefits**

Employee discounts, save on auto, home, and pet insurance, tuition reimbursement, paid vacation and sick time, 9 paid holidays and 3 paid floating holidays, paid leave for when you have a baby, adopt a child, or become a foster parent, legal services, identity theft protection, employee assistance program (EAP), adoption reimbursement benefit, FEDlogic, commuter benefits.

**Responsibilities**

The Regional Vice President (RVP), Manufacturing is responsible for leading the end-to-end manufacturing operations across a multi-site regional network within Primo Brands. This executive leader drives safety, quality, production, cost, service, people, and continuous improvement performance across factories while ensuring alignment with enterprise Supply Chain strategies and business objectives.

The RVP, Manufacturing partners closely with Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Quality, Maintenance, Procurement, Planning, HR, and Finance leaders to deliver operational excellence, optimize manufacturing capacity, develop organizational capability, and support long-term business growth. The role is accountable for creating a high-performance culture that prioritizes safety, quality, associate engagement, customer service, and productivity improvements.

The Regional Vice President, Manufacturing reports to the Senior Vice President, Manufacturing Operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Safety & Compliance Leadership**

* Lead a culture where safety is the first priority and operational decisions reflect a zero-harm mindset.
* Ensure compliance with all federal, state, provincial, environmental, food safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Drive accountability for safety performance, incident reduction, risk mitigation, and compliance excellence.
* Serve as a visible champion for workplace safety and associate well-being.

**Manufacturing Operations**

* Lead manufacturing performance across multiple factories, ensuring consistent execution against operational objectives.
* Deliver production plans that support customer demand, service expectations, and inventory requirements.
* Drive schedule attainment, throughput, asset utilization, and manufacturing reliability.
* Optimize regional manufacturing capacity and network performance.
* Ensure disciplined execution of daily management systems and operational governance routines.

**Food Safety & Quality**

* Champion food safety and quality excellence across all facilities.
* Ensure manufacturing sites maintain compliance with applicable regulatory, customer, and company standards.
* Provide leadership oversight of quality management systems, audits, inspections, recalls, and corrective action processes.
* Promote a culture of first-time-right execution and continuous quality improvement.

**Financial & Productivity Performance**

* Own regional manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, conversion costs, and operating performance.
* Deliver annual productivity, cost savings, and efficiency targets.
* Identify opportunities to reduce waste, improve OEE, optimize labor deployment, and improve asset performance.
* Partner with Finance to ensure operational results support annual business plans and long-range objectives.

**Talent & Organizational Leadership**

* Build and lead high-performing teams through effective leadership, coaching, succession planning, and talent development.
* Develop strong Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Technical Managers, Operations Managers, and functional leaders.
* Drive leadership capability, workforce planning, succession readiness, and organizational effectiveness.
* Foster a culture of accountability, inclusion, collaboration, and associate engagement.

**Continuous Improvement**

* Lead implementation of manufacturing excellence initiatives across the region.
* Drive improvements in OEE, asset reliability, labor productivity, quality, and service performance.
* Leverage Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and continuous improvement methodologies to drive sustainable results.
* Establish performance metrics and governance processes that accelerate operational excellence.

**Strategic Leadership**

* Contribute to the development and execution of Supply Chain and Manufacturing strategies.
* Partner with cross-functional stakeholders to evaluate network optimization opportunities, capacity investments, automation initiatives, and capital projects.
* Lead manufacturing integration, transformation, and change management initiatives.
* Support enterprise growth through scalable operational solutions and disciplined execution.

**Scope of Responsibility**

* Multiple manufacturing facilities within assigned region.
* Direct leadership of Plant Directors, Factory Managers, Regional Engineering, Manufacturing Excellence, and operational support functions.
* Accountability for regional safety, quality, production, service, cost, talent, and financial performance.
* Significant influence on capital planning, organizational design, and operational strategy.

**Qualifications**

**Education**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations Management, Supply Chain, Business, or related field required.
* Master's Degree (MBA or related discipline) preferred.

**Experience**

* 15+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
* 10+ years leading multi-site manufacturing operations.
* Experience managing large-scale manufacturing networks in food, beverage, consumer packaged goods, or related industries.
* Proven success leading large teams through operational transformation and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Experience managing significant P&L, productivity, and capital investment responsibilities.

**Skills & Competencies**

* Executive leadership and influence.
* Manufacturing operations expertise.
* Safety and quality systems leadership.
* Financial and operational acumen.
* Strategic thinking and execution.
* Change leadership and organizational transformation.
* Talent development and succession management.
* Data-driven decision making.
* Cross-functional collaboration.
* Strong communication and stakeholder management skills.

**Success Measures**

* Safety Performance
* Quality Compliance & Customer Metrics
* OEE and Asset Reliability
* Production Attainment
* Cost per Case Equivalent
* Labor Productivity
* Service Levels / OTIF
* Associate Engagement
* Leadership Bench Strength
* Productivity Savings Delivery
* Capital Project Execution
* Manufacturing Excellence Maturity

**If you're ready to embark on an exciting journey with Primo Brands, apply now!**

**Salary Range Disclaimer**

The salary range provided for this position is an approximation based on market research, internal compensation data and the candidate’s qualifications and experience. Final salary offers are determined through a comprehensive evaluation of candidate qualifications and may vary depending on factors such as skills, experience, and geographic location of the position. Other components of the compensation package, including benefits and bonuses, will also be considered. We are committed to fair and equitable compensation practices, and we encourage open dialogue about compensation during the interview process.

Primo Brands’ established portfolio includes billion-dollar brands Poland Spring® and Pure Life®, premium brands like Saratoga® and Mountain Valley®, regional leaders such as Arrowhead®, Deer Park®, Ice Mountain® Ozarka®, and Zephyrhills®, purified brands, Primo Water® and Sparkletts®, and flavored and enhanced brands like Splash® and AC+ION®. Our extensive direct-to-consumer offerings and industry-leading line-up of innovative water dispensers create consumer connectivity through recurring water purchases across Water Direct, Water Exchange, and Water Refill. At Primo Brands, our more than 11,000 associates are at the heart of what we do and deliver on our mission to provide healthy hydration to consumers wherever, however and whenever they want it. We believe in fostering a respectful culture, which values our associates who are deeply invested in quality hydration, our communities, and the sustainability of our packaging and water sources for generations to come.

Primo Brands is proud to be an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action employer, seeking to create a welcoming and diverse environment. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, transgender status, sexual stereotypes, age, status as a protected veteran, status as an individual with a disability, or other applicable legally protected characteristics. We also consider qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law.

Candidates must possess strong English language skills to effectively communicate with customers and provide exceptional service. Proficiency in English is essential for understanding customer needs, resolving inquiries, and collaborating with team members.

**Location: East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX**

**Job Type: Full-Time | On-site**

**Typical Hours: Monday-Friday; 40-45 hours/week**

**Start Date: ASAP**

**Sponsorship is not available**

**Relocation assistance available**

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Description**

Our client in the manufacturing industry is looking for a Director of Manufacturing Operations to join their team in East Dallas, near Mesquite, TX. This newly created role will lead approximately 40 employees across production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and continuous improvement, through three direct report managers. You will build the operating systems needed to support continued growth, with an emphasis on improving production flow, standardizing work, strengthening material availability, and reducing order-to-ship lead times. The operation is low-volume, high-mix, and highly customized, making experience applying lean principles in complex manufacturing environments critical. Our client is looking for a manufacturing leader who has led multiple functions and personally delivered measurable improvements from batch production toward flow. This is an opportunity to build and improve an operating system while leading a growing manufacturing organization in a high-demand market.

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Responsibilities**

• Lead production, supply chain, inventory, quality, and facilities

• Develop production flow, capacity, scheduling, and standard work systems

• Reduce order-to-ship lead times and improve on-time delivery

• Build material replenishment, point-of-use, and inventory systems

• Improve supplier performance, sourcing, material availability, and lead times

• Move quality controls upstream to reduce defects reaching final testing

• Establish daily management and structured problem-solving systems

• Lead lean improvements across low-volume, high-mix production

• Develop operations leaders and an approximately 40-person team

• Build capacity to support growth without proportional labor or space increases

**Director of Manufacturing Operations Qualifications**

• 10+ years of manufacturing operations experience required

• 5+ years leading multiple manufacturing departments, including production, required

• Low-volume, high-mix or complex assembly experience required

• Experience leading production flow improvements or measurable lead-time reduction required

• Experience implementing and sustaining lean management practices in manufacturing required

• Experience scaling production capacity or output required

• Manufacturing ERP proficiency required

identity_held_roles.description:
**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
 
 
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
 
 
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
 
 
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
 
 
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is scaling from development programs into high-rate, repeatable production across a diversified portfolio of military and commercial systems, including satellites and spacecraft, propulsion systems, solar power systems, and the Dream Chaser spaceplane. As Director, Production Operations based in Madison, Wisconsin, you will play a critical role in executing the production strategy for propulsion development and manufacturing, building the operational systems required to deliver hardware at pace, at quality, and at cost.
 
 
This is an execution-focused leadership role for a proven operations professional with expertise in propulsion systems. Reporting to the Vice President, Production, you will lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines and additional enterprise products within Sierra Space's Madison facility. You will drive standardization of production processes, implement data-driven manufacturing systems, and build high-performing teams capable of scaling propulsion output while maintaining quality and efficiency. You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Program Management to ensure production readiness and on-time delivery of critical propulsion systems for space and defense applications.
 
 
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
 
 
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing and assembly operations for propulsion product lines, including day-to-day oversight of production floor activities, scheduling, and workflow management at the Madison, WI facility.
* Execute production strategy to scale propulsion manufacturing from development programs into repeatable, high-rate production with a focus on throughput, yield, and cost efficiency.
* Standardize propulsion production processes and workflows to create consistent, repeatable, high-quality build operations aligned with enterprise-wide best practices.
* Support capacity planning and facility buildout efforts for propulsion manufacturing, including layout optimization, equipment installation, and production line commissioning.
* Drive vertical integration initiatives by standing up and maturing internal propulsion manufacturing capabilities, including additive manufacturing, machining, assembly, and test operations for propulsion components and systems.
* Implement and mature manufacturing execution systems (MES) and production data infrastructure to enable traceability, repeatability, and real-time visibility into propulsion manufacturing performance.
* Establish and maintain production operating rhythm through KPIs, dashboards, and review cadences focused on cycle time, yield, throughput, labor efficiency, on-time delivery, and cost for propulsion production.
* Apply lean manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies, reduce waste, and improve quality in propulsion operations.
* Collaborate with Propulsion Engineering and Product Assurance to drive design-for-manufacturing (DFM) and design-for-test (DFT) into propulsion product development and support new product introduction (NPI) activities.
* Partner across Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Facilities, Security, and Program Management to ensure aligned production readiness, material availability, and execution against propulsion program schedules.
* Manage production budgets for propulsion operations and analyze manufacturing costs to implement cost-saving measures that maintain quality standards and support financial goals.
* Lead and develop production management teams at the Madison facility, including supervisors, engineers, and technicians, fostering collaboration and accountability while upholding company values and a culture of operational excellence.
* Ensure compliance with industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.) applicable to aerospace and propulsion manufacturing operations.
* Represent propulsion production operations in cross-functional forums and communicate status, risks, and mitigation plans to executive leadership and external stakeholders, including customers and regulatory bodies.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or a related technical field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* 10+ years of experience in manufacturing, production, or operations roles in complex technical industries, with a significant portion in leadership positions.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex production projects in high-rate manufacturing environments.
* Strong background in manufacturing processes, assembly & integration, and operational execution for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems, with emphasis on propulsion systems preferred.
* Demonstrated experience implementing and scaling production operations, including process standardization, workflow optimization, and capacity planning.
* Experience with data-driven manufacturing systems, MES, and production management processes, including OKR development and performance tracking.
* Knowledge of design-for-manufacturing (DFM) principles and ability to collaborate with engineering teams to optimize product designs for production.
* Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams and drive operational excellence in fast-paced, highly technical environments.
* Expertise in continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma) with proven ability to identify and eliminate production inefficiencies.
* Strong financial acumen with demonstrated ability to manage production budgets, analyze manufacturing costs, and implement cost-saving measures.
* In-depth knowledge of industry-specific production standards, safety regulations, and quality management systems (ISO, AS9100, GMP, etc.).
* Excellent cross-functional collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to represent production interests effectively to executive leadership and external stakeholders.
* Ability to uphold and model company values while holding others accountable and fostering a culture of operational excellence.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in propulsion manufacturing and test operations, including liquid or hybrid rocket engines, thrusters, or propulsion subsystems.
* Familiarity with additive manufacturing (3D printing) for propulsion components, including metal printing processes and post-processing.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, satellite, launch, or high-rate hardware manufacturing across both military and commercial product lines.
* Experience with vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities such as propulsion, fluid systems, PCBAs, structures, or integrated vehicle production.
* Experience with spacecraft or satellite integration and production.
* Familiarity with classified manufacturing and secure production operations.
* Experience implementing lean or continuous-improvement frameworks at scale in production environments.
* Experience with automated manufacturing, MES implementation, or production data systems.
* Experience leading organizational change initiatives specific to production environments, including technology implementation, process redesign, and workforce development.
* Experience building and scaling production teams during periods of rapid company growth.
* Master's degree in engineering, operations, business, or a related field.

Compensation:
 
 
Pay Range:
 
 
$164,513.00 - $226,205.00
 
 
Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.
 
 
**IMPORTANT NOTICE:**
This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance.  The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.
 
 
**Elevate Your Career**
At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.
 
 
We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.
 
 
Sierra Space is an industry-leading space and defense technology company providing satellites, spacecraft, and enabling mission systems and components. We deliver mission-proven technologies to our customers that safeguard our nation, protect space-based assets and enable space exploration.
 
 
*Application Deadline: This role will remain posted until a qualified pool of candidates is*
*identified.*
***Please note: Sierra Space does not accept unsolicited resumes from contract agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited resumes submitted to our website or to Sierra Space team members not through our approved vendor list or Talent Acquisition will be considered property of Sierra Space, and we will not be obligated to pay any referral fees.***
Sierra Space Corporation is an equal opportunity employer and is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to applicants with disabilities. If you need special assistance or a reasonable accommodation related to applying for employment with Sierra Space or at any stage of the recruitment process, please contact us.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Director of Manufacturing (Rubber)**

The Director of Manufacturing will oversee rubber production operations across 2 manufacturing plants with 200 total employees, 100 employees per plant, 1 union plant & 1 non-union, 5-8 Direct Reports (Department Managers) with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, and cost, acting as leader with accountability for both operations.

**Location**
: Columbia, Missouri (Relocation Assistance Offered)

**Compensation**
: $175,000 - $215,000 base salary + 15% bonus.

**Benefits**
: Medical, Dental, Vision, STD, LTD, 401k Match 6%, 3 weeks PTO, Tuition Assistance, etc.

**Job Description:**

*Operational Leadership & Plant Management*

* Hold full P&L, safety, quality, delivery, and cost accountability for both rubber manufacturing plants across textile & milling operations including mixing and cord production, acting as a multi-site operations leader.
* Lead, develop, and hold accountable a team of 6-8 managers who in turn lead roughly 200 salaried and hourly employees across multiple shifts.
* Develop and execute annual operating plans, capital plans, and budgets; manage conversion cost, yield, scrap, rework, material variance, and overhead against targets.
* Balance production schedules and capacity across both sites to meet downstream Belt and Hose demand, optimizing changeovers, inventory, and material availability.
* Partner with the VP of Manufacturing, plant managers of downstream operations, supply chain, and commercial teams on demand planning, capacity strategy, and make-versus-buy decisions.
* Spend meaningful time on the floor at each site (approximately 30% travel), maintaining a visible presence on all shifts and engaging directly with operators and supervisors.

*Compound Quality, Technology & Process Control*

* Own end-to-end compound consistency, using rheology (Mooney, MDR/RPA), physical properties, and downstream processing and molding results as the measures of success.
* Reduce process variation through structured methods such as design of experiments (DOE), statistical process control, capability studies, and root cause analysis.

* Evaluate and recommend mixing equipment, automation, weighing/batching, and tooling options for current and new processes and products.

* Experience in belt, hose, or other engineered rubber product manufacturing, with understanding of rheology and downstream extrusion, calendering, and molding.
* Experience with cord treatment, textile reinforcement, or adhesive systems.
* Experience managing multi-site operations and leading change across sites.
* Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Green Belt certification, or equivalent.

* Business acumen: manages cost, capital, and capacity with a P&L mindset.
* Learning agility: quickly learns new technologies and applies them to business needs.

identity_held_roles.title: Plant Manager I
identity_held_roles.description:
This position leads all plant operations for a70+ employee, 2 shift, manufacturing site. This leader ensures day-to-day operations are delivered with the aligned objectives of safety-first mindset, customer satisfaction along with growing and developing the leaders within the facility. This position also plays a critical role in developing and executing capital project plans for the facility to enable continuous improvement and growth in market share.

This full-time position reports directly to region General Manager and is located at Liberty Packaging’s manufacturing plant in Houston, Texas

**Duties And Responsibilities**

* Directly lead and supervise a team of direct reports to deliver major site functions across manufacturing, shipping, maintenance, and scheduling.
* Own end-to-end performance for the facility to meet KPIs in the areas of Safety, Quality, Cost, and Delivery. Establish, measure, and monitor performance across facility and root cause performance issues. Develop and deploy plans to drive improvements in manufacturing processes to ensure superior product quality, reduced cycle times, lead times, and minimize overall manufacturing costs.
* Provide day-to-day leadership for manufacturing team decision-making in the areas of production, labor, material costs, design, and production scheduling.
* In partnership with Continuous Improvement function, guide leaders and front-line staff through the identification and deployment of continuous improvement initiatives with an impact on key performance indicators.
* Ensure the right talent and capabilities are in place to meet strategic objectives; accountable for establishing goals, managing performance, and developing teams to ensure short- and long-range objectives are achieved
* Establish a two-way communication & engagement culture to ensure all plant employees are clear on plant performance and connection to business performance, including KPIs.
* Lead key change initiatives across the plant in partnership with regional and functional support systems (e.g., continuous improvement, engineering, human resources, sales, etc.)
* Lead the successful identification, business case design, and execution of capital projects in partnership with functional teams and executive leadership. Ensure multi-year capital plans support market growth and customer delivery
* Ensure employee relations stay connected with open and continuous dialogue
* Develop and grow community engagement presence by representing plant locally in key activities and through execution of frequent employee and community engagement activities
* Own direct P&L responsibility for plant site
* Provide leadership by connecting and being visible to all three shifts daily
* Other duties, as assigned

**Required Education, Experience And Skills**

* Bachelors’ degree and 7+ years manufacturing experience OR 10+ years manufacturing industry experience in lieu of education
* 5+ years people leadership experience
* Experience analyzing downtime, production, and financial variance trends, and identifying actions to deliver expected performance
* Previous experience developing and managing a budget, forecasting, and monitoring results
* Experience with identifying and executing capital projects to drive improvement against KPIs
* Demonstrated experience with organizational effectiveness, operations management, and a proven track record of achieving results
* Experience developing and presenting information to multiple levels of the organization from front-line to executive leadership
* Superior time management, attention to detail, verbal and written communication skills, decision-making, and organization skills
* Excellent computer skills required, including Microsoft Word and Excel skills.
* Demonstrated entrepreneurial spirit

**Preferred Education, Experience And Skills**

* Previous experience with Amtech / CTI or Kiwi
* Previous experience with ERP systems
* Previous experience in corrugated or paper manufacturing
* Lean and / or Continuous Improvement certifications
* Bilingual English / Spanish

**Compensation & Benefits**

The starting base salary range for this position is $110,078 - $137,598 per year plus eligibility in annual bonus program. The compensation posted is the anticipated pay for the position at the time of the posting. We may pay above or below posted amount based on several factors, including, but not limited to education and/or certifications, skills, experience, or work location. Some positions may qualify for additional compensation in the form of bonuses or deferred compensation options.

At LDI, we are pleased to provide employees with a comprehensive benefits package including health/dental/vision insurance options; paid time off; 10 paid holidays; 401(k) plus company matching and annual discretionary profit sharing; flexible spending and health savings account options; life and disability insurance; tuition assistance; wellness and mental health resources, and financial advising services. Eligibility in benefit programs is based on hours worked per week.

**Physical Requirements**

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

* Regular sitting, standing, and walking throughout the day to accomplish tasks
* Manual and finger dexterity used regularly with some repetitive finger motions
* Ability to work in front of a computer screen for long periods of time
* Specific vision abilities include close and distance vision; able to identify colors, small letters, and numbers; hand/eye coordination, depth perception and able to adjust focus
* Hearing and speaking
* Other conditions may include frequent reaching, stretching, pushing, pulling, pinching, grasping, and gripping.

**About Our Company**

Comprised of multiple companies with headquarters in New Hope, Minnesota, Liberty Diversified International (LDI) is a privately held company employing more than 1,900 individuals across our manufacturing facilities, production facilities and core business operations in Minnesota, Iowa, Nebraska, Illinois, Mississippi, Texas, Arizona, Virginia, California, and Mexico. With deep roots in the corrugated box manufacturing industry, we operate in the core markets of paper, packaging, workplace products, corrugated plastics and building products.

Since 1918, our values – Caring, Innovation, Trust and Excellence – have guided our day-to-day activities. We believe that when our employees are aligned with these values, we create superior service and solutions for our customers. The LDI family of companies includes Liberty Packaging, Liberty Paper, Liberty Plastics (Custom Solutions and Quarrix Building Products) and Safco.

Liberty Diversified International is an equal opportunity employer and makes all employment decisions without regard to race, color, sex, religion, age, creed, sexual orientation, national origin, marital status, disability, or any other protected class.

We may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of the hiring process, such as reviewing applications, analyzing resumes, or assessing responses. These tools assist our recruitment team but do not replace human judgment. Final hiring decisions are ultimately made by humans. If you would like more information about how your data is processed, please contact us.

**A bit about us:**
We are seeking a hands-on Engineering Operations Leader to drive performance, efficiency, and team development within a fast-paced SMT / PCB manufacturing environment. This role will lead engineering and operations initiatives focused on continuous improvement, process optimization, and operational excellence, while developing and scaling a high-performing technical team.
 
 
The ideal candidate brings a strong Lean Manufacturing mindset, deep experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT/PCB), and the ability to drive accountability and measurable results across the organization.
 
 
\*\*Relocation assistance available for those not local to the area

Medical, Dental, Vision coverage
 
401(k) with company match
 
Relocation assistance

Generous PTO & sick leave
 
 
 
**Job Details**
Key Responsibilities:
 
 
Operations & Continuous Improvement
 

* Lead Lean Manufacturing initiatives to improve throughput, yield, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE)
* Identify and drive process improvements across SMT lines, PCB assembly, and supporting operations
* Implement and sustain Lean tools (Kaizen, 5S, value stream mapping, standard work, etc.)
* Analyze production data to identify inefficiencies and drive corrective actions
* Reduce scrap, rework, and downtime through structured problem-solving methodologies

Engineering Leadership
 

* Oversee engineering activities related to process development, troubleshooting, and optimization
* Partner with production to resolve complex technical and process challenges
* Support new product introductions (NPI) and ensure smooth transition into production
* Drive best practices across SMT processes including soldering, reflow, pick-and-place, inspection, etc.

Team Development & Leadership
 

* Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers, technicians, and support staff
* Build a culture of accountability, ownership, and continuous improvement
* Establish clear KPIs and performance metrics for engineering and operations teams
* Identify skill gaps and implement training / development plans

Cross-Functional Collaboration
 

* Partner with quality, supply chain, and production leadership to align operational goals
* Drive collaboration between engineering and manufacturing teams to improve execution
* Support customer needs and ensure alignment with delivery and quality expectations

Qualifications:
 
 
Required:
 

* 7–10+ years of experience in electronics contract manufacturing (SMT / PCB environment required)
* Proven leadership experience managing and developing technical teams (engineering or maintenance)
* Strong background in Lean Manufacturing / Continuous Improvement
* Hands-on experience with SMT processes (pick-and-place, reflow, inspection, etc.)
* Demonstrated success driving operational efficiency, process improvements, and accountability
* ITAR eligibility required; experience working in an ITAR-regulated environment is a strong plus
* Individual must be a US Citizen due to ITAR regulations

Preferred:
 

* IPC certification (IPC-A-610, IPC-7711/7721, etc.)
* Experience with high-mix, low-volume or high-speed production environments
* Exposure to automation, process engineering, or advanced manufacturing technologies

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description**
**Description & Requirements**
**About AESC US LLC**
AESC is a global leader in the development and manufacturing of high-performance batteries for zero-emission electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Founded in Japan in 2007 and headquartered in Yokohama, AESC has been building manufacturing capabilities around the world in the U.S., U.K., Europe, Japan and China to serve key markets and leading customers locally for over 14 years. Today, AESC has become the partner of choice for the world's leading OEMs and energy storage providers in North America, Europe, and Asia. Its advanced technology powers over one million electric vehicles and provides more than 15GWh of installed capacity for battery energy systems in over 60 countries.
 
 
AESC is expanding its footprint in the United States, and the Blythewood Repack Operation supports the broader South Carolina production network. AESC is committed to our local communities where it is making its investments, creating jobs, and supporting local charities.
 
 
**About The Role**
The Senior Operations Manager provides comprehensive leadership of manufacturing operations, driving safe, reliable, efficient, and cost-effective production. This role is responsible for integrating production execution with workforce planning, material flow, equipment availability, quality performance, and operational readiness.
 
 
The successful candidate must possess a broad understanding of plant operations and demonstrate the ability to lead across functions rather than operate solely as a production manager.
 
 
****What You Will Do****

* Direct daily manufacturing operations across assigned shifts and production areas.
* Establish and execute production plans that align labor, equipment, materials, and customer delivery requirements.
* Manage operational KPIs including throughput, OEE, labor productivity, downtime, scrap, cost, and on-time delivery.
* Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering to ensure equipment availability, preventive maintenance execution, and effective downtime response.
* Partner with Quality to manage manufacturing defects, process compliance, containment, and corrective actions.
* Coordinate with Supply Chain and Logistics to maintain effective material flow, inventory accuracy, and production readiness.
* Lead production supervisors and team leaders, establishing clear expectations for attendance, timekeeping, staffing, overtime controls, and employee performance.
* Manage operating expenses, labor utilization, and production resource requirements.
* Promote a disciplined safety culture with EHS and enforce manufacturing operating standards.
* Support commissioning, production ramp-up, process stabilization, and future plant expansion.
* Develop staffing, succession, and workforce capability plans.
* Complete other duties as assigned.

**Qualifications**
****What You Need****

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Manufacturing, or a related discipline, or equivalent substantial manufacturing leadership experience.
* At least 10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including five years in plant operations leadership.
* Demonstrated accountability for manufacturing performance, staffing, safety, cost, and cross-functional execution.
* Experience with ERP/MES systems, Lean manufacturing, and operational performance management.

****What is "Nice to Have"?****

* Automotive OEM or Tier 1 experience.
* Battery manufacturing experience.
* High-volume automated manufacturing experience.
* Plant launch or greenfield ramp-up experience.

****Travel Requirements****
20% International Travel
 
 
****What We Offer****
Welcome to AESC, where you'll have the opportunity to tackle the world's most fascinating challenges alongside exceptionally talented individuals who are driven to make a difference. We strive to ensure that our employees are well taken care of, enabling them to focus on their work and contribute to our collective mission.
 
 
**We Offer**

* Comprehensive compensation packages including a competitive salary and a rewarding bonus program.
* An inclusive and diverse work environment that fosters and encourages professional and personal development.
* Highly automated, clean, safe, and temperature-controlled production environment.
* Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance.
* HSA and Flexible Spending Accounts.
* 401K with company match.
* Life Insurance (Company paid and additional voluntary life available).
* Paid Vacation and 14 Paid Holidays.
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage (Company Paid).
* Tuition reimbursement.

****Equal Employment Opportunity****
At AESC, we are committed to providing Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) to all individuals. We participate in E-Verify and will provide the federal government with your Form I-9 information to confirm that you are authorized to work in the U.S. Join us in our passion to design, manufacture, and sell high-performance products, contributing to a sustainable and zero-carbon emission future.
 
 
****Physical Requirements****
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable otherwise qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
 
 

* Ability to stand, walk, and work on a concrete production floor for extended periods of time.
* Ability to read, write, speak, hear; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach and lift with hands and arms frequently throughout the day.
* Ability to wear all required PPE when working on the production floor.
* Required to occasionally lift, push, pull and/or move up to 10 pounds, and occasionally required to lift, push, pull and/or move up to 35 pounds.

****Work Environment****
The work environment is primarily a semi-automated/automated plant with a concrete floor and is characterized as climate controlled, moderate noise, and forklift traffic. The individual must be able to perform all essential functions as appropriate on the plant floor, in meetings, and with employees, management, customers and suppliers.
 
 
Candidate must perform the essential duties and responsibilities with or without reasonable accommodation efficiently and accurately, and without causing significant safety threat to self or others. The statements made herein are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by employees assigned to this job classification. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive and inclusive list of all responsibilities, duties, and/or skills required of personnel so classified.
 
 
Hiring is contingent upon successful completion of a drug screen and background check, and verification of the candidate's eligibility to work in the United States. AESC US LLC is a drug-free workplace.

identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Manager, Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Office
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
DESCRIPTION:
 
 
As a Senior Manager of Quality at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you will guide strategic quality initiatives and support a culture of continuous improvement across our organization. You'll oversee quality management systems, ensure regulatory compliance, and enhance customer experience through excellent quality standards. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you'll develop and implement quality strategies that support our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.
 
 
In this role, you'll manage quality assurance and quality control teams while building strong partnerships with operations, R&D, commercial teams, and customers. You'll guide process improvements through Practical Process Improvement (PPI) methodologies and risk-based approaches. Your leadership will be essential in maintaining inspection readiness, managing customer relationships, and ensuring compliance with global regulatory requirements.
 
 
As a member of the site leadership team, you'll support quality initiatives that deliver consistent product excellence while meeting business objectives. You'll develop quality professionals, lead investigations, and implement data-driven solutions that enhance our quality systems and customer satisfaction.
 
 
REQUIREMENTS:
 
 

* Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience, or Bachelor's Degree plus 8 years of experience in pharmaceutical, medical device, or regulated life sciences industry
* Preferred Fields of Study: Science, Engineering, Chemistry, or related technical field
* Professional certifications desired (ASQ, Lean Six Sigma, etc.)
* 5+ years of quality management/leadership experience
* Expert knowledge of global quality standards (ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 17025)
* Strong understanding of quality management systems and GMP requirements
* Demonstrated experience leading quality investigations, CAPA, and change control processes
* Experience implementing continuous improvement initiatives
* Experience with quality tools including FMEA, Risk Analysis, and Root Cause Analysis
* Excellent project management and cross-functional leadership abilities
* Strong data analysis and problem-solving capabilities
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills
* Ability to build collaborative relationships at all levels
* Experience hosting regulatory inspections and customer audits
* Proficiency with quality management software systems
* Ability to travel up to 10%

identity_held_roles.title: R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager, Project Management
identity_held_roles.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.

**What You Will Experience In This Position**

The R&D NPI Engineering Senior Manager will be a strategic and hands-on leader who drives on-time delivery and best practices for our new product introduction (NPI) programs within our Data Solutions business. This role will lead, coach and mentor a team of project and program managers to ensure alignment with business goals through effective portfolio and process management. The manager will work closely with business unit leaders, product managers, and engineering leaders to drive and improve on-time delivery and cross-functional collaboration for our portfolio of NPI programs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership & Development:**
Lead, mentor and inspire a high-performing, global project management team specializing in NPI Program execution. Develop a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement, and empower the team to drive excellence in project delivery.

**NPI Execution and Delivery:**
Oversee end-to-end execution of projects, ensuring on-time delivery, within scope and on budget while maintaining high quality outcomes.

**Cross-Functional Coordination:**
Partner closely with engineering, product management, integrated supply chain, manufacturing and operations teams to ensure alignment of project priorities, resources, and timelines, facilitating seamless execution of programs.

**Resource Allocation:**
Optimize resource planning and allocation across projects, balancing capacity dynamically to meet changing business priorities and ensure effective utilization

**Portfolio Management:**
Collaborate with key partners to drive the selection and prioritization of NPI projects, connected to our strategic objectives and business goals.

**Continuous Improvement**
: Own and evolve the NPI phase-gate process to ensure consistent and efficient product development lifecycle execution. Drive continuous evaluation and enhancement of our project management processes, tools and methodologies to improve efficiency and scalability of programs.

**Performance & Reporting:**
Define and track KPIs to measure project health and business impact. Lead monthly business reviews to communicate progress, risks, and opportunities to senior leadership.

**You Have**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering
* Ideally 10+ years of proven experience in NPI or PMO leadership roles, preferably in data or technology-driven environments of which 2+ years of people leadership experience, including coaching, mentoring, and developing high-performing teams
* Proven record of leading large-scale, complex projects and driving successful product introductions
* Proficiency in demonstrating expertise in PMO practices, methodologies, tools and processes.
* Outstanding ability to lead and influence cross-functional teams and drive results in a matrixed organization.
* Excellent communication, coaching, and stakeholder management skills.
* Strong analytical, problem solving and decision-making abilities to drive efficiency and optimize project outcomes.
* Experience in manufacturing, industrial, or engineering focused organizations

**We Have**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
* nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
* Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.
* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
* We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
* Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

* Innovative & adaptable
* Dedicated to absolute integrity
* Focused on the customer first
* Respectful and team oriented
* Optimistic and energizing
* Accountable for performance
* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency**

nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.

**Compensation Range**

$123,500.00 - $229,500.00

Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.

**Benefit Overview**

At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:

* Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
* A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
* Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.

At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
 
 
Reporting to the Vice President, Regal Rexnord Business System (RBS) for the Automation and Motion Control (AMC) Segment, the Continuous Improvement (RBS) Director for the AMC Segment serves as the strategic leader responsible for accelerating operational excellence and driving sustainable business performance improvements across assigned manufacturing sites. This role partners closely with site leadership teams to deploy CI (RBS) principles, develop leadership capabilities, improve operational metrics, and create a culture of continuous improvement.
 
 
The Director, RBS acts as both coach and change agent, ensuring that RBS tools and behaviors become integrated into daily management systems and leadership practices. Success in this role is measured by measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth, employee engagement, and overall business results.
 
 
The role is accountable for translating AMC strategic objectives into clear RBS roadmaps, prioritizing initiatives with the highest business impact, and ensuring disciplined execution through leaders, site teams, and RBS/CI talent. The Director, RBS will regularly communicate progress, risks, and business impact to segment and division leadership and will influence stakeholders outside of the direct function to align priorities, resources, and decisions.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**
This Role Will Make an Immediate Impact By:
 
 

* Partner with site leadership teams to align operational strategies with division and enterprise objectives.
* Facilitate the development and execution of annual and multi-year operational strategies.
* Lead deployment of the Regal Business System across assigned facilities.
* Ensure site improvement priorities support commercial growth, profitability, customer service, and capacity requirements.
* Drive accountability for achievement of business objectives and key performance indicators.
* Drive a culture where performance gaps are addressed through structured problem solving.
* Partnering with division and segment leadership to prioritize improvement initiatives, recommend resource plans, and support staffing and talent decisions within the RBS/CI organization.

**Other Key Responsibilities Include**

* Assess site maturity and develop roadmaps to advance RBS capabilities.
* Standardize the use of RBS tools and systems across sites.
* Conduct regular RBS assessments, audits, and gemba reviews.
* Ensure sustainability of improvements through standard work and leader accountability.
* Coach site leaders on RBS principles, lean leadership, and continuous improvement behaviors.
* Develop leadership capability in daily management, problem solving, visual management, and accountability systems.
* Facilitate workshops, training sessions, and leadership development activities at sites.
* Build organizational capability to achieve self-sustaining continuous improvement.
* Establish and improve visual management systems throughout manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and support functions.
* Drive implementation and effectiveness of tiered accountability processes.
* Ensure performance measures are visible, actionable, and aligned to business objectives.
* Improve management routines to accelerate issue identification and resolution.
* Develop problem-solving capabilities at all levels of the organization.
* Facilitate Kaizen events, Rapid Improvement Events, and cross-functional improvement projects.
* Coach teams in root cause analysis methodologies including A3, 5 Whys, Fishbone, and PDCA.
* Ensure countermeasures are implemented, verified, and sustained.

**Required Skills & Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, marketing, operations, supply chain, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of continuous improvement, manufacturing or operations experience. Experience leading Lean/RBS transformation and maturity improvement across multiple sites, divisions, or business functions.
* Proven application of multiple CI tools, including 80/20, value stream mapping, 6S, flow, standard work, visual management, and structured problem solving.
* Black Belt in Lean/Continuous Improvement preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through others, influence senior leaders, and align cross-functional stakeholders around strategic improvement priorities.
* Experience developing CI/RBS talent, coaching leaders, and building organizational capability through formal training, Gemba coaching, and leader standard work.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with plant teams, peers, executives, and external stakeholders as needed.
* Ability to travel up to 75% of the time to support assigned plants and divisions, regionally and internationally.

**Preferred Skills & Qualifications**

* MBA Preferred
* Lean deployment experience within a large, global, decentralized manufacturing environment.
* Industrial manufacturing industry experience.
* Knowledge of enterprise-wide business system tools or and continuous improvement frameworks.
* Experience in engineer-to-order or configure-to-order business environments.
* Experience improving transactional process areas such as customer care, engineering, finance, commercial, product management, or quote-to-cash.

**Pay Transparency**
Expected Base Salary Range: $132,000 – $205,600
 
 
The salary range provided is intended to display the value of the company's base pay compensation for this position. Salary is dependent on a multitude of factors, including but not limited to the physical worksite location, the geographic market of that location, candidate's skill set, level of experience, education and internal peer compensation comparisons among other potential factors.
 
 
**Export Controlled ITAR/EAR Compliance (Location & Position Dependent)**
Restrictions imposed by federal export control laws may limit this job opportunity to candidates who are a ‘U.S. Person’, which includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted asylum in the United States, and refugees in the United States, or who otherwise can qualify for a license that permits them to hold the position.
 
 
**Sponsorship**
Candidates must be eligible to work in the United States without requiring company sponsorship to obtain or keep U.S. work authorization.
 
 
**Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Drug Coverage
* Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
* Paid Time Off and Holidays
* 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions
* Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
* Paid Leaves
* Tuition Assistance

**About Regal Rexnord**
Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.
 
 
The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.
 
 
Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. Regal Rexnord has offices and manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**
Regal Rexnord is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex/gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, age, ancestry, national origin, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status (unless required by the applicable law or government contract), disability or protected veteran status or any other status or characteristic protected by law. Regal Rexnord is committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse and inclusive backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. If you’d like to view a copy of the company’s affirmative action plan for protected veterans/individuals with disabilities or policy statement, please email Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com. If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please e-mail Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
Equal Employment Opportunity Posters
 
 
**Notification to Agencies**
: Please note that Regal Rexnord Corporation and its affiliates and subsidiaries ("Regal Rexnord") do not accept unsolicited resumes or calls from third-party recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Master Service Agreement or similar contract and approval from HR to submit resumes for a specific requisition, Regal Rexnord will not consider or approve payment to any third-parties for hires made.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Manufacturing
identity_held_roles.description:
***Ready to lead a function, not just a shift? This is your next step.***

American Armor Gloves makes high-quality nitrile gloves here at home in South Carolina. Healthcare workers, first responders, and essential workers across the country rely on what we build. Our purpose is simple: **We strengthen America by building quality protection at home.**

We're a lean, growing manufacturer scaling toward 320–350 people, and we've spent the past year building the foundation for that growth: a redesigned organization, a clear vision with quarterly milestones, defined leadership roles, and a new leadership and compensation architecture. Manufacturing is the heart of that growth, and we need a leader ready to own it.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Director of Manufacturing is one of the most essential roles in our company. You'll own the end-to-end performance of our Manufacturing department, turning business plans into consistent, safe, high-quality production results.

This role is built for an accomplished Manufacturing Manager who is ready to take the next step. You've proven you can run a strong operation. Now you're ready to **lead through systems and leaders rather than personal effort on the floor**, and to build a manufacturing function that performs at a high level no matter which team is on shift.

Reporting to our VP of Operations, you'll be the bridge between enterprise strategy and shift-by-shift execution. You'll set the systems, build the leaders, and own the results.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* **Own manufacturing performance.** Deliver results across safety, quality, OEE, throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, scrap, and downtime through accountable leaders and strong systems.

* **Build repeatable production systems.** Design shift handoffs, accountability routines, labor deployment standards, and scheduling so performance never depends on heroics.

* **Lead and develop your Shift Manager team.** Coach your Shift Managers as leaders, not only as production operators, and build the next generation of manufacturing leadership.

* **Integrate compounding and batching.** Keep material availability, formulation compliance, and production demand aligned and well governed.

* **Drive continuous improvement.** Lead projects that reduce waste, improve workflow, raise OEE, and close performance gaps, in partnership with Process Engineering.

* **Partner across the business.** Work side by side with Quality, Process Engineering, Maintenance, Logistics, and People & Culture to remove barriers to production.

* **Build workforce capability.** Own training plans, manufacturing career pathways, and engagement so our workforce is ready to support growth.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

You'll set daily and weekly production priorities, deploy labor across shifts, manage Shift Manager performance, and direct improvement projects within manufacturing. You'll shape manufacturing KPI targets, capacity planning, equipment needs, and staffing structure through your recommendations to the VP of Operations. You'll lead Shift Managers, Production Planning, and Batching/Compounding leadership, with a frontline team of Production Supervisors and Manufacturing Associates across multiple shifts.

**A REAL CAREER PATHWAY**

We grow leaders deliberately, and this role is designed as a launch point, not a ceiling. Our leadership framework defines exactly what it takes to grow from functional leadership into executive leadership, and we invest in getting high performers there.

* **Where you go next.** The Director of Manufacturing is a direct pathway to VP of Operations or other senior operations leadership, based on demonstrated enterprise judgment, cross-functional partnership, and the strength of the leadership bench you build.

* **How you get there.** Expect direct mentoring from the VP of Operations, exposure to enterprise planning and capital decisions, cross-functional visibility, and formal leadership development.

* **A clear standard.** Your growth is measured against the same competency framework used for job descriptions, performance reviews, and succession planning, so you always know where you stand and what comes next.

* **Visibility at the top.** Our annual bench-strength review puts strong leaders on the executive team’s radar early.

**WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**

* **Essential to the mission.** Every glove we ship runs through the function you lead.

* **Build, not just run.** Our organization is lean and still forming, so you'll shape systems and standards that scale with the business.

* **A clear operating rhythm.** A shared vision, quarterly milestones, and a common scorecard keep leaders aligned and connect your work to company priorities.

* **Leave a legacy.** You'll develop Shift Managers into future Directors and Supervisors into future Shift Managers, building a team that carries the company forward.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent progressive leadership experience

* 8–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership in a high-volume environment

* Proven success leading multiple shifts and developing frontline leaders

* A track record of owning department performance through KPIs, systems, and accountable leadership

* Strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and HR

* Solid knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and manufacturing quality systems

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, ERP/MRP systems (NetSuite preferred), KPI dashboards, production scheduling, and QMS

**Bonus points for:** experience in medical device, PPE, chemical processing, or FDA-regulated manufacturing; Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement practice; ERP implementation; and leading through growth and scale.

**HOW YOU LEAD**

You lead safely, every shift, not only when incidents happen. You hold leaders accountable through systems, not by stepping in for them. When something breaks, you fix the system, not just the shift. You raise problems early and directly. You treat Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance as partners, and you understand how manufacturing affects the entire business.

**READY FOR YOUR NEXT STEP?**

If you're a Manufacturing Manager ready to own a function, build leaders, and grow into enterprise leadership with a company that's scaling with purpose, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

*American Armor Gloves is an equal employment opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, mental or physical disability of a qualified individual, veteran or military status, pregnancy, marital status, familial status, genetic information, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state or local law.*
