identity_held_roles.title: Sr. Director, Additive Manufacturing Systems Engineering
identity_held_roles.description:
**Hadrian - Manufacturing the Future**
======================================

Hadrian is building autonomous factories to reindustrialize America. By combining AI, advanced software, robotics, and full-stack manufacturing, we help aerospace and defense companies build rockets, satellites, aircraft, ships, and other mission-critical systems up to 10x faster and at significantly lower cost.

Following our $1.37B Series D at a $7.87B valuation, Hadrian is rapidly expanding our manufacturing footprint, launching new capabilities across welding, casting, forging, electronics, additive manufacturing, and more, while scaling our Factory-as-a-Service platform to transform how critical products are built.

Backed by leading investors including JPMorgan Chase, Valor Equity Partners, Andreessen Horowitz, Founders Fund, 137 Ventures, Lux Capital, T. Rowe Price, and Morgan Stanley, we’re building the future of American manufacturing—and looking for exceptional people to help make it happen.

If you’re ready to take on the most challenging and rewarding work of your career while helping create American manufacturing jobs for generations to come, you’re exactly who we’re looking for.

**Why This Role Exists**
------------------------

Hadrian is building an additive manufacturing capability that runs as part of an autonomous factory, not as a room full of printers. The hard problem is not any single machine, material, or line of code. It is making all of them behave as one system. Systems engineering is the glue that holds that system together, and this role owns the glue.

The Senior Director leads three engineering functions, materials and process engineering, hardware engineering, and software engineering, and is accountable for the digital backbone that binds them to each other and to applications engineering: the architecture, interfaces, and data that connect Hadrian’s Opus platform to cutting-edge additive manufacturing equipment, add automation where it makes sense, fuse sensor data into the part record, and turn a collection of parts into a full, integrated digital manufacturing system built around additive.

The measure of success is not three strong teams. It is one manufacturing system that a customer part flows through, from design intent to qualified hardware, with every decision and every data point captured along the way.

**What You’ll Do**
------------------

* **Architect the system.** Define and control the end-to-end architecture for additive at Hadrian: requirements, interfaces, data model, and acceptance criteria that hold across multiple equipment platforms, modalities, and sites. Treat the factory as the product.
* **Build the digital backbone.** Connect additive equipment, peripherals, and inspection assets to Opus with the same discipline a semiconductor fab applies to connecting tools to the host: standardized state models, telemetry, event streams, and data contracts, with security and configuration control built in.
* **Fuse the sensors.** Bring in-situ monitoring, machine telemetry, environmental data, and downstream inspection into one correlated record per part, then move from monitoring to data-driven release and, where it is justified, closed-loop control.
* **Automate where it pays.** Lead automation across additive cells (material and powder handling, build changeover, part removal and depowdering, post-processing flow, robotics, controls, and safety) with a written case for each: safety, repeatability, and data capture first; labor second. Never automate an unstable process.
* **Lead the three functions as one.** Set standards, priorities, and cadence for materials and process, hardware, and software engineering. Resolve conflicts between them at the architecture level, not the escalation level.
* **Own the applications engineering interface.** With the Head of Applications Engineering, define what a production-ready hand-off looks like, publish the process capability and design-rule data applications engineers build to, and close the loop from floor results back into design guidance.
* **Industrialize the equipment.** Through the hardware engineering leader, own factory and site acceptance, commissioning, reliability (preventive maintenance, spares, MTBF/MTTR), and configuration-controlled modification and upgrade of additive systems, and lead the technical relationships with equipment partners that unlock deeper integration. The machine-level depth lives in that team; the standards and the outcomes live here.
* **Design for the factory.** Partner with Factory Development and Factory Automation on cell and site design: material flow, capacity, simulation, utilities, and the path to lights-out operation for additive.
* **Build quality in.** Make the system itself the evidence: traceability, data integrity, and process control that stand up to AS9100 audits and customer qualification without a separate paper trail.
* **Be the additive voice in Hadrian’s platform.** Carry additive requirements into Core Engineering and the Opus roadmap, and bring platform capability back to the floor.
* **Hire, develop, and retain.** Build a leadership bench under you, set a high technical bar, and make Hadrian the place the best additive systems engineers in the country want to work.

**What We’re Looking For**
--------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a physical science; an advanced degree is strongly preferred.
* 12+ years in advanced manufacturing, with real depth in at least three of these six domains: factory design and industrial automation; semiconductor or other high-reliability capital-equipment engineering; manufacturing software and data systems; materials science and process engineering; quality systems in regulated industries; sensing, process monitoring, and sensor fusion.
* 5+ years leading engineering teams, including leading through managers and building at least one function from the ground up.
* Production experience with metal laser powder bed fusion, as a user of the equipment, a developer of it, or both.
* Has led the integration of complex equipment into factory-level software (manufacturing execution, equipment host, or data platforms), including requirements, interface standards, and acceptance criteria.
* Has taken at least one production automation or capital-equipment program (robotic cells, material handling, or equipment with safety systems and controls) from concept through commissioning in a regulated environment (aerospace and defense, semiconductor, medical, or similar), and has owned the reliability of production equipment afterward.
* Fluent across the stack: can review a process flow, a data schema, a metallurgical cross-section, and a controls narrative in the same meeting, and knows which one is lying.
* Has worked as a true peer to a customer-facing or design function, with a record of building clean interfaces rather than absorbing the other team.
* Willing to travel up to 20%, including to Hadrian sites and international partners. Must meet the ITAR requirements below.

**What Will Set You Apart**
---------------------------

* Ph.D. in materials science, mechanical engineering, systems engineering or a related discipline.
* Semiconductor capital-equipment background: equipment-to-host integration, tool matching, fleet data, fault detection and statistical process control at scale.
* Equipment-maker experience developing or launching metal additive systems (new product introduction, cost-productivity trades, design reviews) in addition to user-side experience.
* In-situ monitoring and sensor fusion implemented in production, with data-driven release or closed-loop control.
* Factory design: material flow planning, discrete-event simulation, and highly automated or lights-out operations.
* AS9100 and customer qualification pathways; familiarity with AM specifications (ASTM F42, ISO/ASTM 529xx, SAE AMS 7xxx series).
* Budget or P&L ownership of a capital-intensive program, with a record of making the build-versus-buy and automate-versus-wait calls well.
* Modern software fluency: APIs, event streaming, OT/IT architecture, industrial interoperability standards (OPC UA, MTConnect), and cloud data platforms.

**Compensation**
----------------

For this role, the target salary range is $300,000 - $350,000 (actual range may vary based on experience).

This is the lowest to highest salary we reasonably and in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. We may ultimately pay more or less than the posted range, and the range may be modified in the future. An employee's pay position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, performance, and business or organizational needs.

**Benefits for Full-time Employees**
------------------------------------

* Medical, dental, vision, and life insurance plans for employees
 
 401k
* Relocation support may be provided for certain situations, based on business need.
* Flexible vacation policy
* Equity

**ITAR Requirements**
---------------------

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen or national, lawful permanent resident, protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

**Use of AI in hiring**
-----------------------

Hadrian uses AI-assisted tools in our recruiting and hiring processes to help our team work more efficiently. This may include tools that help organize and analyze recruiting data, as well as an AI-powered notetaker that can record and transcribe interviews and help coordinate feedback. These tools support our team and are not used to make hiring decisions. All candidate evaluations and hiring decisions are performed by humans. If an interview will be recorded, you will be notified in advance and may opt out at any time with no impact on your candidacy. Candidate data processed through these tools is subject to the same protections described in our Privacy Policy.

**Consideration of Criminal History**
-------------------------------------

Hadrian will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the requirements of all applicable laws. We do not ask about criminal history on our application, and we do not consider criminal history before making a conditional offer of employment.

**Hadrian Is An Equal Opportunity Employer**
--------------------------------------------

Hadrian does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, marital status, mental status, physical disability or any other legally protected status. When necessary, the Company also makes reasonable accommodations for disabled candidates and employees, including for candidates or employees who are disabled by pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions.

Compensation Range: $300K - $350K

identity_held_roles.title: Senior Manager, Manufacturing Infrastructure
identity_held_roles.description:
Founded in 2015, Shield AI is a venture-backed deep-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include the V-BAT aircraft, Hivemind Enterprise, and the Hivemind Vision product lines. With nine offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and the Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit Shield Open . Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.

### **Job Description**

Shield AI is seeking a Senior Manager, Manufacturing Infrastructure to lead the server and network infrastructure for our new 400,000 sq ft manufacturing facility in the Seattle-Tacoma area, home to our newest flagship product. You will own the systems and network engineering that keep the factory running, from build-out and commissioning through ramp to high-rate production, including compute, virtualization, storage, backup and recovery, IT and OT networks, wireless, and the infrastructure behind manufacturing systems such as MES and PLM. You will lead a site-based team of systems and network engineers and partner closely with Manufacturing Engineering, Operations, Facilities, Cybersecurity, Cloud Platform, Network Engineering, and Service Delivery.

This position is based on site in the Seattle, Tacoma, or surrounding SeaTac, WA area.

### **What You’ll Do**

* Own the infrastructure strategy, architecture, roadmap, and budget for the manufacturing facility.
* Lead technology readiness for the facility from design through construction, commissioning, and production ramp, working with Facilities, contractors, and Manufacturing Engineering.
* Build, lead, and develop an on-site team of systems and network engineers, including hiring, on-call coverage, and performance management.
* Own design and operation of the factory network, including core, access, wireless, IT/OT segmentation, and connectivity to Shield AI sites and cloud, in partnership with Network Engineering.
* Own server, virtualization, storage, backup, and disaster recovery infrastructure for manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP and PLM integrations (including Teamcenter), quality, and test systems.
* Provide management oversight for the servers, virtualization, storage, and network infrastructure that host and connect production systems and test and inspection equipment, partnering with Manufacturing Engineering, controls teams, and equipment vendors.
* Oversee site data center, MDF/IDF, and server room infrastructure, including capacity, power and cooling, cabling, and documentation, in coordination with Facilities.
* Partner with Cybersecurity to apply segmentation, patching, vulnerability management, and access controls aligned with NIST 800-171, CMMC, and ITAR requirements.
* Define uptime targets, change governance, and maintenance windows that fit production schedules; lead major incident response and root-cause analysis.
* Drive standardization, automation, and observability, and build repeatable site blueprints for future lines and facilities.
* Manage vendors, integrators, contracts, and budgets, and communicate site readiness, risks, and status to technical and executive stakeholders.

### **Required Qualifications**

* 10+ years of experience in enterprise infrastructure, network, or systems engineering, including 5+ years leading engineers, with direct experience supporting a manufacturing or production environment.
* Experience standing up or significantly expanding infrastructure for a new or large facility, from design through operations.
* Strong knowledge of enterprise networking, including switching, routing, wireless, segmentation, firewalls, and WAN connectivity.
* Experience designing and operating compute, virtualization, storage, backup, disaster recovery, and Windows and Linux server environments.
* Experience supporting manufacturing systems such as MES, ERP, PLM, or quality platforms, and familiarity with how production equipment connects to the network.
* Strong understanding of high availability, capacity planning, patching, and monitoring in an environment where downtime affects output.
* Strong people leadership skills, including hiring, coaching, and developing technical talent.
* Experience managing vendors, budgets, and capital projects, with clear written and verbal communication.
* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
* Ability to participate in after-hours work and travel periodically to other Shield AI locations.
* This position may require access to export-controlled information, and employment may be contingent on U.S. person status or export authorization.

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, or other regulated manufacturing, including ITAR and CUI environments.
* Experience with high-rate production ramp and Siemens Teamcenter or other MES platforms.
* Experience with VMware, Hyper-V, NetApp, Cohesity, Active Directory, and Entra ID.
* Experience with automation and infrastructure as code (PowerShell, Python, Ansible, Terraform).
* Familiarity with OT security guidance such as IEC 62443 and industrial protocols such as OPC UA.
* Relevant networking, security, or infrastructure certifications (for example CCNP, CISSP, or ITIL).

Compensation Range: $200,240 - $300,360

identity_held_roles.description:
**Position Overview:**

As the Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR, you will have the unique opportunity to partner closely with several different teams at multiple sites (including IC leadership, reconditioning, and support teams) to drive the strategy behind the development and deployment of Post Production & Quality programs, as well as manage continued performance of internal and external vendors. We are looking for a resourceful self-starter who will set the tone for the successful and fast-paced growth of our Inspection Centers. The Regional Senior Manager of Post Production/IQR role will be heavily focused on leading our teams to effectively close operational gaps and establishing standardized practices that will drive exceptional quality.

**What you'll be doing:**

* Driving successful execution amongst our Post Production teams by effectively leading and developing team members and creating and implementing new processes and systems.
* Identifying issues or roadblocks to execution and quickly taking action to problem solve and implement effective solutions across a large and quickly evolving platform.
* Providing clear direction and necessary support to ensure operational gaps are being closed in a timely manner.
* Working with key business partners to develop systems, metrics, reporting, and staffing models for our Post Production processes and teams.
* Effectively leading and developing onsite personnel at third-party production locations.
* Managing quality of internal and external vendors responsible for producing units for Carvana.
* Establishing effective working relationships with internal and external partners.
* Creating and successfully executing large-scale change management initiatives and new process rollouts.
* Other duties as assigned.

**What the job requires:**

To be able to do your job at Carvana, there are some basic requirements we want to share with you.

* Minimum of 8 years of leadership, people development, and operations experience
* Experience working in a Lean Manufacturing environment
* Experience developing effective and scalable operating systems and processes
* Proven track record of production process improvement and innovation
* Proven track record of managing complex change across large teams
* Proven track record of leading and developing others
* Proven ability to obtain project deliverables and company metrics
* Strong analytical thinking and organizational skills
* Strong written and verbal communication skills; Ability to learn quickly and transfer knowledge
* Requires standing for extended periods of time with frequent stretching, reaching, walking, stooping, pushing, and/or pulling in an environment that may be cold, hot, noisy, and wet and may have fumes or odors due to vehicle maintenance
* Ability to maintain high volume and high-quality content in a fast-paced environment.
* Ability to travel up to 80% (multi site responsibility)
* Ability to provide valuable and actionable feedback
* Proficient computer skills
* Must be at least 18 years of age
* Valid driver's license with a clean driving record (no DUIs and no more than two moving violations in the last 3 years).
* Ability to read, write, speak and understand English

This job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Compensation Range: $120K-$140K annually

**Legal stuff** 
Hiring is contingent on passing a complete background check. This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship. 
Carvana is an equal employment opportunity employer. All applicants receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, marital status, national origin, age, mental or physical disability, protected veteran status, or genetic information, or any other basis protected by applicable law. Carvana also prohibits harassment of applicants or employees based on any of these protected categories.

Please note this job description is not designed to contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Position Title: Regional Director of Operations**

**Salary:** $170,000 - $180,000

**Other Forms of Compensation:** Annual Performance Bonus Opportunity (Up to 25% of Base Salary)

As the leader in business and industry dining, Eurest is the company to join if you want a rewarding career packed with limitless opportunities. We feed the employees of the nation's largest and most-prestigious companies - in every state and across all industries. As a member of Eurest's leadership and professional support team, you will help our 16,000 chefs, and in-unit associates excel as they deliver world-class meals in corporate cafes and executive dining rooms with on-site catering through vending innovations and more.

Our company is innovative, high performing and fast growing. Our teammates are enthusiastic, committed to quality and thrive on consistently delivering unparalleled results. And did we mention we work with exciting companies and at interesting locations? Come grow your career with Eurest.

**Job Summary**
---------------

If you're energized by building, growing, and improving operations, this role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful impact. Supporting a growing portfolio of hospitality operations, you'll help launch new locations, build high-performing teams, design innovative programs, and create exceptional guest experiences.

We're seeking a leader who embraces change, thinks creatively, and enjoys turning ideas into operational success. As the business continues to expand, you'll partner with leaders across multiple markets to drive growth, develop talent, and bring new concepts and initiatives to life.

***This position requires up to 90% travel throughout the Midwest and plays a key role in supporting operations within a dynamic 24/7 environment.***

***This role includes a car allowance. Relocation assistance may be offered for the right candidate, subject to company guidelines.***

The **Regional Director of Operations** provides strategic leadership across multiple districts, driving service quality, operational consistency, and business success. Overseeing District Managers (DMs), this role champions operational best practices, efficiency, and team development. Reporting directly to senior executive leadership, the Regional Director ensures compliance with brand standards, financial growth, operational consistency, and high employee engagement throughout the region. The role fosters a culture of accountability, innovation, and exceptional customer experiences while managing regional budgets and performance strategies.

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

* **Multi-Unit Operational Leadership:** Provide direct oversight and strategic direction to District Managers and General Managers, ensuring operational excellence, brand consistency, and compliance across all locations.
* **Talent Management & Leadership Development:** Recruit, mentor, and evaluate DMs; build a strong leadership pipeline and drive succession planning and team engagement across the region.
* **Financial Performance & Business Strategy:** Oversee regional financial results, P&L performance, budgeting, and revenue growth strategies, analyzing metrics to maximize profit and efficiency.
* **Quality Control & Brand Standards:** Conduct regular site visits and operational audits to ensure adherence to company policies, safety standards, and service quality.
* **Customer Satisfaction & Client Relations:** Partner with DMs and support partners to maintain high levels of customer satisfaction, resolve escalated operational issues, and foster strong client relationships.
* **Strategic Growth & Initiative Execution:** Lead regional rollouts of corporate initiatives, technology implementations, and operational enhancements to support business expansion.

**Preferred Qualifications & Competencies**
-------------------------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Hospitality Management, Operations, or a related field (or equivalent practical experience).
* 5+ years of multi-unit operations leadership experience in high-volume hospitality, corporate services, or retail environments, directly managing District Managers.
* Experience supporting new business openings, operational transitions, or multi-site growth initiatives is preferred.
* Proven track record of driving operational excellence, consistency, and process improvements across multiple districts while maintaining adherence to brand standards.
* Demonstrated capability in executive leadership, talent acquisition, succession planning, and mentoring district leadership teams to build strong operational capability.
* Strong financial acumen with extensive experience managing multi-site P&L budgets, revenue strategy, cost controls, and performance metrics analysis.
* Exceptional client relationship management, strategic communication, and change management skills, with the ability to lead strategic initiatives and support business growth.

**Our Core Values:**
--------------------

We believe we’re better together. As one team spanning coast to coast, our core values guide our actions, shape our culture, and define our service.

**Hospitality**

Great hospitality starts with demonstrating genuine care for others. We do this through great food, thoughtful service, and safe, responsible practices that protect our guests and teams.

**Kindness and Respect**

Two words that go hand-in-hand in what our work is truly about: taking care of people. Everyone has a seat at our table. We take the time to understand others and listen, valuing diverse perspectives and responding with compassion and empathy.

**Trust**

We earn trust by doing what we say we’re going to do and taking ownership. We understand people count on us to deliver with consistency, honesty, and accountability across every location and line of business.

**Innovation**

We embrace fresh thinking and collaboration to find smarter ways to serve. With the flexibility to adapt across industries, we design dining and workplace solutions that move our clients, partners and teams forward.

**Excellence**

Excellence is how we operate daily. We hold ourselves to high expectations and take pride in our work. We lead with energy, creativity, and a service mindset that turns everyday into something exceptional.

**Apply to Eurest today!**

*Eurest is a member of Compass Group USA*

**Click here to Learn More about the Compass Story**

**Associates at Eurest are offered many fantastic benefits.**

* Medical
* Dental
* Vision
* Life Insurance/ AD
* Disability Insurance
* Retirement Plan
* Paid Time Off
* Holiday Time Off (varies by site/state)
* Associate Shopping Program
* Health and Wellness Programs
* Discount Marketplace
* Identity Theft Protection
* Pet Insurance
* Commuter Benefits
* Employee Assistance Program
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs)
* Paid Parental Leave
* Personal Leave

Associates may also be eligible for paid and/or unpaid time off benefits in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. For positions in Washington State, Maryland, or to be performed Remotely, click here or copy/paste the link below for paid time off benefits information.

https://www.compass-usa.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/2026\_Wage-Transparency\_Eurest.pdf

**Compass Group is an equal opportunity employer. At Compass, we are committed to treating all Applicants and Associates fairly based on their abilities, achievements, and experience without regard to race, national origin, sex, age, disability, veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other classification protected by law.**

**Qualified candidates must be able to perform the essential functions of this position satisfactorily with or without a reasonable accommodation. Disclaimer: this job post is not necessarily an exhaustive list of all essential responsibilities, skills, tasks, or requirements associated with this position. While this is intended to be an accurate reflection of the position posted, the Company reserves the right to modify or change the essential functions of the job based on business necessity. We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with a criminal history (including relevant driving history), in a manner consistent with all applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the New York Fair Chance Act.**

Eurest maintains a drug-free workplace.

existing_roles.title: Director, Quality
existing_roles.description:
**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.

existing_roles.title: Director of Quality
existing_roles.description:
**Position Overview:**

The Director of Quality will lead the quality function across the organization and create the operating model required for the company’s next stage of growth. This leader will be accountable for enterprise quality strategy, product and process quality, supplier and customer quality, and the effectiveness of the company’s quality management systems. The role will maintain applicable certifications, including ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, while establishing a disciplined approach to quality diligence and integration for future acquisitions.

The Director of Quality must combine independent judgment with a practical understanding of manufacturing. This leader will know what strong quality looks like, but will build it in a way that fits the company's scale, products, customers, and maturity. Success requires the ability to move between enterprise strategy and a specific customer or production issue; challenge legacy practices while respecting operational knowledge; and bring people through change with clarity, evidence, and follow-through.

This is not a quality-systems-only position. The Director must remain close to manufacturing, customers, and the issues that affect product conformity, delivery, cost, and trust. The successful candidate will bring the rigor expected in regulated manufacturing, apply it without unnecessary bureaucracy, and build a quality organization that can identify risk early, solve problems at their source, and support sustainable growth.

**Essential Functions:**

* Set the global quality strategy. Assess the company's current quality environment and establish a multiyear roadmap aligned with business strategy, customer commitments, regulatory obligations, and acquisition plans. Translate the roadmap into clear priorities, resources, ownership, and measures of success.
* Lead the quality organization. Direct and develop quality leaders and teams across the sites. Define the structure, capabilities, decision rights, and functional accountability required to support a larger international manufacturing organization.
* Own the enterprise quality management system. Ensure effective governance and execution across document and change control, training, nonconformance, CAPA, complaints, risk management, supplier controls, internal audits, management review, and other core processes. Maintain applicable certifications and compliance with customer and regulatory requirements.
* Strengthen product and process quality. Partner with Operations and Engineering to improve quality planning, process validation and control, inspection, calibration, measurement systems, first-article or new-product readiness, and change execution. Use disciplined problem solving and prevention to reduce defects, scrap, rework, escapes, and recurring failures.
* Lead customer and supplier quality. Establish consistent expectations for customer issue response, supplier qualification and monitoring, supplier corrective action, and escalation. Ensure material issues are contained quickly, investigated to root cause, resolved with effective corrective action, and communicated with credibility.
* Create audit and inspection readiness. Lead the enterprise internal audit program and oversee registrar, customer, and regulatory audits. Maintain visibility to findings, commitments, certification status, and systemic risk, and verify that corrective actions are timely and effective.
* Use data to govern performance. Establish a focused set of enterprise and site quality measures, including customer complaints, defects, escapes, scrap and rework, supplier performance, CAPA effectiveness, and audit performance. Lead global management review and give executives a clear view of trends, risk, and required actions.
* Harmonize with purpose. Define the policies, standards, escalation requirements, and controls that must be common across the organization. Rationalize legacy processes and quality technologies, including eQMS capabilities, while preserving local differences that are justified by product, customer, regulatory, or operating needs.
* Lead quality through acquisitions. Support quality due diligence by assessing systems, certifications, audit history, customer and regulatory commitments, product and process risk, and organizational capability. Build and execute risk-based integration plans with clear Day 1 controls, remediation priorities, and a realistic path to the quality model.
* Exercise independent quality authority. Ensure that Quality has direct access to the information and leaders needed to escalate material risk. Maintain clear authority to contain nonconforming product and stop release or shipment when applicable requirements may not be met, while building shared ownership of quality across the business.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, science, quality, or a related technical field.
* At least 10 years of progressive quality experience in manufacturing, including at least five years leading quality teams or leaders.
* Demonstrated success leading quality across multiple manufacturing sites, business units, or regions.
* Experience with product and process quality, quality engineering, customer quality, supplier quality, and quality management systems in a regulated or highly technical environment.
* Strong working knowledge of ISO 13485, ISO 9001, and AS9100, including direct responsibility for audits, certification, corrective action, and management review. Equivalent experience spanning multiple regulated standards will be considered.
* Deep experience with CAPA, nonconformance, root-cause analysis, risk management, process validation and control, measurement systems, and data-driven continuous improvement.
* Ability to identify and communicate material product, customer, and compliance risk and to influence operational and executive decisions with sound evidence and judgment.
* Experience building teams, developing leaders, and driving change across a matrixed or decentralized organization.
* Ability and willingness to travel regularly within the United States and Europe.

**PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Experience in precision manufacturing serving medical device, aerospace, life sciences, or other regulated and quality-sensitive markets.
* Experience in an acquisition-driven, or rapidly scaling organization.
* Experience conducting quality due diligence and integrating acquired manufacturing businesses, sites, or quality systems.
* Experience with electronic quality management systems, quality data architecture, or digital quality transformation.
* Working knowledge of applicable medical device regulations and audit programs, such as FDA QMSR, EU MDR, or MDSAP.
* Lead Auditor, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Quality Engineer, or Lean Six Sigma certification.
* Experience leading quality across the United States and Europe.

existing_roles.title: Vice President, Quality
existing_roles.description:
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.
  
  
The Vice President of Quality is an enterprise leadership role accountable for enterprise quality performance, not just quality systems. This leader will define and execute nVent’s quality strategy across the full value chain, with direct accountability for improving customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality performance, warranty performance, product reliability, on-time-to-customer impact, and launch quality. The role will shift quality from a primarily compliance- and governance-centered function to a performance-driving enterprise capability that improves customer outcomes, operational execution, and business growth.
  
  
Reporting to the Chief Supply Chain Officer, the Vice President Quality will serve as the senior-most quality leader for nVent, setting the vision, operating model, performance expectations, capabilities, and accountability mechanisms required to scale quality as nVent grows. This leader will partner closely with segment presidents, operations, engineering, product management, sourcing and procurement, digital, commercial, legal, and finance leaders to embed quality into business decision-making and deliver measurable improvements in customer experience, reliability, warranty, launch readiness, supplier performance, operational quality, and quality-related business risk.
  
  
**What You Will Experience In This Position**
Enterprise Quality Performance and Accountability
  
  

* Own enterprise quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, launch quality, and the impact of quality issues on on-time-to-customer performance.
* Translate quality strategy into measurable business results, ensuring quality priorities are directly connected to customer experience, operational performance, growth, profitability, and risk reduction.
* Establish clear enterprise, segment, region, business unit, and site-level accountability for the quality metrics that matter most to customers and the business.
* Lead operating reviews that move beyond reporting activity to identifying performance gaps, driving root cause ownership, and sustaining measurable improvement.

New Product Quality and Launch Excellence
  
  

* Elevate new product quality as a core enterprise capability, ensuring quality is designed into high-growth platforms, strategic programs, and critical infrastructure solutions from concept through launch and field performance.
* Partner with engineering, product management, operations, and commercial leaders to strengthen quality planning, design validation, process validation, risk assessment, reliability requirements, and launch readiness across major programs such as Saturn, Avatar, Data Solutions growth initiatives, and other strategic launches.
* Ensure robust NPI quality gates, readiness reviews, and escalation criteria are in place to prevent launch defects, customer escapes, warranty exposure, and reliability issues.
* Build feedback loops from field performance, warranty, customer quality, and manufacturing quality data into product development and launch processes.

Digital Quality, Analytics, and Enterprise Quality Intelligence
  
  

* Lead the evolution of digital quality as an enterprise capability, including predictive quality, AI-enabled risk detection, manufacturing quality analytics, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
* Partner with Digital and Integrated Supply Chain leaders to modernize eQMS capabilities, automate quality workflows, strengthen data integrity, and establish a single source of truth for enterprise quality performance.
* Use advanced analytics to identify leading indicators of quality risk across product design, suppliers, manufacturing processes, field performance, warranty, and customer experience.
* Move the organization from lagging quality reporting to predictive and preventive insights that enable faster decisions, better prioritization, and measurable performance improvement.

Quality Management Systems, Compliance, and Standards
  
  

* Lead the modernization, standardization, and continuous improvement of nVent’s Quality Management System, ensuring systems and standards enable performance improvement rather than becoming ends in themselves.
* Ensure readiness and sustained compliance with applicable quality and regulatory standards, including ISO 9001 and other business-relevant standards such as ISO 14001, AS9100, customer-specific requirements, and regional regulatory expectations.
* Strengthen management review, internal audit, external audit, and corrective and preventive action processes to ensure systemic issues are identified, resolved, and prevented from recurring.
* Partner with legal, compliance, engineering, operations, and commercial teams to manage quality-related risk and ensure quality commitments are understood, objective, and executable.

Customer, Supplier, and Operational Quality
  
  

* Build customer quality capability that improves responsiveness, transparency, containment, corrective action effectiveness, customer confidence, and reduction of repeat escapes.
* Advance supplier quality strategy, qualification, audit discipline, scorecards, supplier development, and escalation processes to improve supplier performance and protect customer commitments.
* Embed quality into manufacturing and operational processes with a focus on defect prevention, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, error proofing, and flow to customer.
* Use customer feedback, warranty data, supplier performance, manufacturing quality, field performance, and operational metrics to prioritize systemic improvement opportunities.

Leadership, Talent, and Quality Culture
  
  

* Champion a quality-first culture where leaders model prevention-based decision-making and teams are empowered to stop, escalate, and resolve issues before they reach the customer.
* Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing quality leadership team with clear accountability, succession depth, and strong capability across enterprise, segment, regional, and site quality roles.
* Lead through influence in a matrixed environment, balancing enterprise standards with business-specific execution needs and measurable performance outcomes.
* Model executive leadership behaviors, including strategic thinking, courageous decision-making, stakeholder engagement, talent development, collaboration, adaptability, and self-accountability.

**You Have**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
* 15+ years of progressive quality, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience in a global manufacturing environment, including significant leadership of multi-site or enterprise quality functions.
* Demonstrated experience improving quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, and launch quality.
* Strong experience in new product quality, design validation, process validation, launch readiness, reliability engineering, and quality risk management for complex product portfolios.
* Experience advancing digital quality capabilities, including eQMS, quality analytics, digital traceability, predictive insights, and AI-enabled risk detection.
* Proven ability to lead enterprise-level change across a complex, matrixed, global organization.
* Exceptional communication, influencing, and executive presence, with the ability to translate quality priorities into business value.
* Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.

**Suggested Success Measures**

* Reduced customer escapes and repeat quality issues, with improved containment, responsiveness, and corrective action effectiveness.
* Improved cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, warranty performance, and on-time-to-customer impact from quality issues.
* Improved supplier quality performance through stronger qualification, development, governance, scorecards, and corrective action discipline.
* Stronger new product quality outcomes, including improved launch readiness, fewer launch defects, reduced warranty exposure, and better reliability performance.
* Expanded digital quality maturity, including predictive quality insights, AI-enabled risk detection, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
* Increased quality maturity from reactive issue management to proactive prevention, measurable performance improvement, and stronger enterprise accountability.

**We Have**

* A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day

+ nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
+ Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.

* Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work

+ We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
+ Through our nVent in Action matching program, we provide funds to nonprofit and educational organizations where our employees volunteer or donate money

- Core values that shape our culture and drive us to deliver the best for our employees and our customers. We’re known for being:

* Innovative & adaptable
* Dedicated to absolute integrity
* Focused on the customer first
* Respectful and team oriented
* Optimistic and energizing
* Accountable for performance
* Benefits to support the lives of our employees

**Pay Transparency**
nVent’s pay scale is based on the expected range of base pay for this job and the employee’s work location. Employee pay within this range will be based on a combination of factors including knowledge, skills, abilities, experience, education, and performance. Where federal, state, or local minimum wage requirements exist, employee pay will comply.
  
  
**Compensation Range**
$241,500.00 - $359,000.00
  
  
Depending on the position offered, employee may be eligible for other forms of compensation, such as annual incentives.
  
  
**Benefit Overview**
At nVent, we value our people and their health and well-being. We provide a broad benefits package with meaningful programs for eligible full-time employees that includes:
  
  

* Medical, dental, and vision plans along with flexible spending accounts, short-term and long-term disability benefits, critical illness, accident insurance and life insurance.
* A 401(k) retirement plan and an employee stock purchase plan — both include a company match.
* Other supplemental benefits may include tuition reimbursement, caregiver, personal and parental leave, back-up care services, paid time off including volunteer time, a well-being program, and/or legal & identity theft protection.

At nVent, we connect and protect our customers with inventive electrical solutions. People are our most valuable asset. Inclusion and diversity means that we celebrate and encourage each other’s authenticity because we understand that uniqueness sparks growth.

existing_roles.description:
Shape the future of quality and patient trust. Join us as the Vice President, Global Quality Control and lead a world-class laboratory network that powers our clinical and commercial programs across the globe. Reporting to the Chief Quality Officer, you will set the enterprise strategy and build a unified, high-performing Quality Control organization that delivers reliable data, inspection-ready laboratories, and timely product release support—while advancing standardization, digital innovation, scientific excellence, and operational performance.
  
  
**Company Overview**
The work we do at FUJIFILM Biotechnologies has never been more important—and we are looking for talented candidates to join us. We are growing our locations, our capabilities, and our teams, and looking for passionate, mission-driven people like you who want to make a real difference in people’s lives.
  
  
Join FUJIFILM Biotechnologies and help make the next vaccine, cure, or gene therapy in partnership with some of the most innovative biopharma companies across the globe. We are proud to cultivate a culture that will fuel your passion, energy, and drive - what we call Genki.
  
  
Fujifilm is globally headquartered in Tokyo with over 70,000 employees across four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging. We are guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles.” Visit: https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region/careers
  
  
**Job Description**
Your impact In this enterprise role, your leadership will directly influence patient safety, product quality, inspection outcomes, batch disposition timelines, and continuity of supply across a diverse global portfolio. You will advise senior executives on investment, capacity, technology, organizational design, and regulatory strategy—shaping multi‑year business and quality plans. Your decisions will strengthen client trust, accelerate revenue recognition, reduce the cost of quality, and protect the company’s license to operate.
  
  
What you will do
  
  

* Define and execute a global Quality Control strategy, operating model, and multi‑year roadmap across sites, modalities, and development phases. Establish enterprise standards, clear decision rights, and governance forums that enable consistent, phase‑appropriate control while allowing justified site or platform differences.
* Provide executive oversight of end‑to‑end Quality Control operations, including analytical, biochemical, biological, microbiological, raw‑material, in‑process, release, and stability testing; as well as environmental and utility monitoring. Ensure capacity, prioritization, and flawless execution to meet program milestones, product disposition, client commitments, and uninterrupted supply.
* Govern the analytical method lifecycle from early development through transfer, qualification, validation, comparability, continued performance verification, and retirement. Ensure control strategies and specifications evolve appropriately through clinical development, process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Set global expectations for current good manufacturing practice, applicable good laboratory practice principles, data governance, principles that ensure data are attributable, legible, contemporaneous, original, accurate and complete, laboratory investigations, out of specification and out of trend management, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, change control, and audit readiness. Lead enterprise strategy and executive response for regulatory inspections and critical client audits.
* Build and deliver the digital and technology roadmap for laboratory information management systems, electronic laboratory notebooks, laboratory execution systems, chromatography data systems, laboratory automation, advanced analytics, and instrument connectivity. Sponsor validated deployment, master‑data governance, cybersecurity, and adoption that improve right‑first‑time outcomes and cycle time.
* Direct enterprise Quality Control capacity planning, capital prioritization, make‑versus‑buy decisions, laboratory footprint strategy, and governance of external testing partners. Align resources and contingency plans with demand forecasts, technology transfers, new product introductions, and network resiliency needs.
* Establish enterprise metrics and management review for on‑time testing and release support, lead time, invalid results, out of specification and out of trend rates, investigation cycle time, corrective and preventive action effectiveness, stability execution, method performance, cost, and productivity. Drive risk‑based priorities, Lean practices, and cross‑site learning to deliver sustainable improvement.
* Serve as the senior Quality Control liaison for strategic clients, regulatory authorities, and executive governance. Translate complex laboratory, method, and compliance risks into clear business implications, negotiate technically sound solutions, and ensure commitments are realistic, documented, and delivered.
* Build and lead a global organization through senior leaders. Define capabilities and succession plans, develop technical career paths and communities of practice, and cultivate a culture of scientific rigor, transparency, accountability, inclusion, and proactive risk management.
* Own escalation and coordinated response for significant Quality Control events, laboratory constraints, critical data‑integrity concerns, assay failures, method or specification issues, and testing disruptions. Make or recommend risk‑based decisions on testing strategy, product impact, remediation, and continuity of supply.
* Perform other duties in support of the broader Global Quality strategy and company objectives.

**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Biochemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Engineering, or a related scientific discipline, with fifteen or more years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or contract development and manufacturing organization Quality Control; or a Master’s degree with ten or more years.
* Ten or more years of people leadership, including five or more years leading senior leaders with accountability for multiple laboratories, sites, or functional areas.
* Demonstrated leadership of Quality Control across development and commercial stages, including method transfer, qualification and validation, release and stability testing, microbiology, and environmental and utility monitoring.
* Proven experience with global regulatory inspections and client audits, and with complex out of specification, out of trend, data‑integrity, and laboratory‑compliance matters.
* Experience managing budgets, capital portfolios, headcount, capacity, external laboratories, and enterprise transformation in a matrixed global organization.
* Executive‑level communication and client‑facing experience in a regulated, technically complex environment.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced scientific degree and/or a Master of Business Administration.
* Global leadership within a contract development and manufacturing organization supporting biologics, vaccines, advanced therapies, or sterile manufacturing.
* Experience scaling Quality Control from clinical development through process performance qualification, launch, and sustained commercial supply.
* Working knowledge of the following: Food and Drug Administration; European Medicines Agency; Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency; Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency; International Council for Harmonisation guidelines Q2, Q5, Q6, Q9, Q10, and Q14; United States Pharmacopeia; European Pharmacopoeia; Japanese Pharmacopoeia; Title 21 of the Code of Federal Regulations Parts 210, 211, and 11; and European Union Good Manufacturing Practice Annexes 1 and 11; as well as applicable data‑integrity expectations.
* Experience deploying global laboratory information management systems and laboratory digitalization and automation.
* Credentials from the American Society for Quality, and training in Lean and Six Sigma or equivalent quality and operational excellence disciplines.

If you are a strategic, hands‑on executive who thrives at the intersection of science, operations, and leadership, we would love to hear from you. Apply today and help us raise the bar for quality worldwide.

Bio-Rad is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead our chemical manufacturing operations in Richmond, California, with additional responsibility for developing pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou, China.
  
  
This role provides leadership across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, Quality Control, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety. The Director is accountable for delivering strong performance in safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, and inventory while building manufacturing capabilities to support future business growth.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring strong manufacturing and technical leadership, business judgment, and experience leading complex operations in a regulated environment. This position partners closely with Quality, EH&S, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and business leadership to ensure reliable operations, successful new product introductions, and a resilient manufacturing network.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Lead chemical manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer service.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with business requirements, capacity needs, gross margin objectives, and long-term growth.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, QC, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.
* Ensure compliance with applicable quality, environmental, health and safety, chemical process safety, and regulatory requirements.
* Partner with EH&S, Quality, Regulatory, Legal, and other functions to proactively identify and mitigate operational, regulatory, and business continuity risks.
* Develop and execute equipment, infrastructure, automation, and capital investment strategies to improve reliability, capacity, and efficiency.
* Drive cost and productivity improvements across labor, yield, scrap, waste, material usage, manufacturing variances, and inventory.
* Partner with R&D and business teams to enable effective new product introduction, scale-up, industrialization, and technology transfer.
* Lead development of pilot manufacturing capabilities in Suzhou to support new product introduction and greater flexibility across the manufacturing network.
* Develop manufacturing budgets and capital plans and ensure disciplined management of operating expenses and investments.
* Build organizational capability through talent development, succession planning, employee engagement, and development of strong leaders.
* Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, continuous improvement, collaboration, and customer focus.

**What You Bring**

* Education: Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Life Sciences, Biochemistry, or another relevant scientific or technical discipline required; Master’s degree or PhD preferred.

* Experience working across functions and geographies in a global organization preferred.

**Richmond, CA**
and requires the employee to be located within commuting distance of the office.

Please review the job details below.
  
  
Intuitive Machines - West is currently seeking a courageous, innovative, multi-skilled Director of High-Rate AIT Production to join our spacecraft production team in Palo Alto, CA.
  
  
**Life with Us**
Your Project: Intuitive Machines is a world leader in high-power spacecraft, having delivered some of the largest and highest-power spacecraft in the world. We are now looking to take this legacy of excellence to the next level, architecting a high-volume production line to build a large number of advanced spacecraft.
  
  
In this role, you will architect and implement a high-volume assembly, integration, and test (AIT) production line for these next-generation vehicles. You will be responsible for transforming our AIT operations from low-rate to high-rate production, establishing scalable processes and organizational capabilities to support our ambitious production targets. The scope includes complete spacecraft AIT from component receipt through final acceptance testing, encompassing electrical systems integration, solar array integration with the spacecraft bus, battery integration, advanced thermal solutions, and comprehensive environmental testing at production scale.
  
  
A critical aspect of this role is developing an efficient, right-sized test program—one that provides high confidence the vehicles will perform as designed while eliminating non-value-added test activities that add cost and schedule without commensurate risk reduction. You will apply rigorous engineering judgment to distinguish between essential verification activities and legacy testing practices that may not be necessary for production-rate vehicles.
  
  
We are looking for leaders to bravely challenge conventional AIT approaches and establish production-rate processes for these advanced systems. You will play an essential role in applying design-for-manufacturing/design-for-test (DFM/DFT) principles to develop AIT specifications and manufacturing plans suitable for volume production. Additionally, you will represent AIT capabilities during customer proposal efforts, providing technical credibility and instilling confidence in our ability to execute high-volume production of complex spacecraft.
  
  
Your Career: We're very serious about professional development and continuing education at Intuitive Machines - West. We offer our team members the opportunity to define their own career trajectory. You will work with your manager to set goals and design a development plan to advance your career. This unique opportunity is a high-visibility role critical to our company's leadership position in spacecraft manufacturing.
  
  
What We Offer: Time for dedicated professional development, conference attendance, industry training, peer group collaboration, as well as paid certifications and education reimbursement.
  
  
Who you will work with: You will report to the VP of Spacecraft Production and Operations and collaborate closely with Engineering, Quality, and Supply Chain teams. You will lead a team of AIT production engineers and technicians while partnering with design engineering to ensure producibility of our spacecraft systems. You will also engage directly with potential customers during proposal phases to communicate our production and test capabilities.
  
  
**Your Responsibilities**

* Design end-to-end AIT production flow optimized for high-volume throughput
* Develop capacity models, takt time analysis, and process flow requirements for production-rate AIT
* Define capital equipment strategy including test equipment, handling systems, and tooling
* Establish scalable AIT work instructions, process controls, and quality gates
* Lead development of an efficient, risk-informed test program that ensures vehicle performance confidence while eliminating non-value-added testing
* Oversee spacecraft-level integration of solar arrays, batteries, and other major subsystems with the spacecraft bus
* Implement manufacturing execution systems (MES) tailored to provide assembly process documentation and production tracking for volume spacecraft production
* Define requirements for low-cost mechanical and electrical assembly, integration and test equipment, and production tooling
* Lead Voice of Manufacturing inputs to spacecraft design to ensure producibility at scale
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives leveraging lean manufacturing principles
* Build and mentor AIT production engineering team
* Represent AIT production capabilities to potential customers during proposal efforts, providing technical credibility on execution readiness
* Support business development with AIT cost models and production capacity commitments

**How You Will Be Evaluated**
Your performance will be measured against AIT production readiness milestones, test program efficiency metrics, production ramp targets, quality metrics, and cost per unit objectives.
  
  
**What We Look For In Team Members**
As a team member at Intuitive Machines - West, we expect you to demonstrate honesty, integrity, innovation, collaboration, and a commitment to excellence.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering or related technical field. Four additional years of experience may be substituted for a degree
* Minimum of 15 years related aerospace manufacturing/AIT experience
* Minimum of 7 years leadership experience in production or manufacturing engineering
* Experience working cross-functionally within a company and/or with external partners and contractors
* Proven track record scaling aerospace production operations
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience with volume production of spacecraft or complex aerospace systems
* Direct experience developing and implementing a spacecraft AIT production line
* Experience with large spacecraft systems (solar array integration, battery integration, high-voltage testing)
* Demonstrated experience developing efficient, risk-based test programs that balance verification rigor with schedule/cost efficiency
* Understanding of spacecraft environmental testing at production scale (thermal vacuum, vibration, EMI/EMC)
* Prior history as an AIT engineer, process engineer, or industrial engineer for aerospace products
* Experience with sustaining engineering processes such as Change Approval, NPI, breakpointing
* Advanced degree in a technical field
* Lean/Six Sigma certification
* Experience with AS9100 quality systems
* Capital project management experience (multi-million dollar equipment investments)
* Experience taking spacecraft products into production, including progressive design iterations to reduce delivered cost
* Demonstrated experience applying system engineering practices to AIT operations
* Excellent communication and presentation skills, with experience engaging directly with customers in technical/proposal settings
* Experience working directly with customers in the commercial space industry
* Ability to work independently with a high degree of organization and attention to detail

Votaw Precision Technologies has long been a trusted partner in building mission-critical hardware for some of the most advanced aerospace and defense programs in the world. Our precision components support the International Space Station, nearly every major launch vehicle in operation, high-performance spacecraft (including classified missions), as well as next-generation fighter aircraft, bombers, submarines, radar systems, and ground vehicles.

This individual will have full responsibility for the day-to-day management, technical excellence, production performance, staffing, scheduling, efficiency, and continuous improvement of the facility.

The ideal candidate is a seasoned machining professional with approximately 20 years of industry experience who understands metal cutting and CNC machining at a deep technical level and has progressed into a strong operational leadership role.

The company utilizes a variety of CNC machining technologies, including 3-axis, 4-axis, and 5-axis machining, as well as vertical milling, welding and large-scale assembly tooling.

* Work closely with programmers, machinists, and engineers to resolve technical machining issues.

* Experience managing multiple shifts and 24/7 operations
* Knowledge of complex, tight-tolerance, or high-value machined components.
* Experience with 5-axis machining and advanced CNC manufacturing.
* Implementing Lean Manufacturing or continuous-improvement initiatives.
* Knowledge of ERP/MRP and production scheduling systems.
* Managing capital equipment purchases and machine capacity planning.
* Experience in aerospace, defense, medical, automotive, or other high-precision manufacturing environments is a plus.

* Ability to effectively prioritize and execute tasks in a high-pressure environment.

**Director of Operations**

We are seeking a strategic, technical, and results-driven Director of Manufacturing to lead and optimize high-volume packaging blow molding facility. As a key member of the executive leadership team, you will bridge organizational strategy with daily shop floor execution by overseeing multi-shift operations, managing the operational budget, and driving performance across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and talent development. In terms of strategic leadership and daily operations, you will execute manufacturing strategies that maximize throughput, cycle times, and capacity utilization across all production lines. You will oversee multi-shift operations to foster a culture of accountability and high performance on the plant floor while maintaining disciplined daily management routines, including production reviews, KPI tracking, and systematic escalation procedures. Additionally, you will translate forecasting and demand data into actionable manufacturing plans, master schedules, and staffing models designed to meet fast-paced consumer goods delivery timelines.
  
  
From a technical and equipment management perspective, you will optimize processing parameters across a diverse fleet of plastic blow molding machinery and drive high-speed automation projects. You will also oversee material management to maximize the efficiency of high-volume grades. Partner closely with Maintenance and Tooling teams to minimize changeover downtime, and enforce rigorous preventive maintenance programs.

SoCal in your soul, attitude in your stride. If gravity doesn't stop you and "impossible" sounds more like "dare you," you're ROCKSTAR®— a born rebel, raising the bar with mind-body energy and zero compromise.

Together, we're Celsius Holdings, Inc.— a global CPG company united by three powerhouse brands and one incredibly talented team.

At Celsius, we pride ourselves on empowering our people. Every employee has a stake in our success. We create a collaborative culture built on inclusivity, innovation, and a belief that great ideas can come from anywhere.

Ready to take your career to the next level? Join our team and redefine what it means to be energized.

**Position Overview**

As the Director of Manufacturing, you will serve as the senior plant leader for a high-volume beverage canning operation responsible for batching, filling, seaming, and packaging canned CELSIUS® beverages. You will provide strategic and operational leadership across production, quality, food safety, maintenance, engineering, safety, warehousing, workforce development, and continuous improvement.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who has operated in a high-speed, automated food, beverage, packaging, or consumer products environment. Yes

VP of Manufacturing

* Ensure effective prerequisite programs, food defense, food fraud prevention, sanitation, traceability, lot control, allergen control where applicable, and environmental monitoring activities
* Oversee inspections, testing, product release, holds, deviations, nonconforming product, complaints, CAPAs, and corrective-action effectiveness in partnership with Quality
* Ensure beverage-specific quality controls are effective, including ingredient and batch accuracy, Brix and carbonation targets, fill levels and net contents, double-seam inspection, date/lot coding, and finished-product testing

* Collaborate with Human Resources to recruit, develop, retain, and engage a high-performing plant workforce
