**Job Description**
**Director, Production Operations in Springfield, MO**
Build your future at Curia, where our work has the power to save lives
  
  
Curia is a global contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) with over 30 years of experience partnering with pharmaceutical and biotech companies to provide life-saving treatments to patients. At Curia, we are on a mission to advance our customers’ therapies from curiosity to cure and ultimately to improve patients’ lives.
  
  
We proudly offer
  
  

* Generous benefit options (eligible first day of employment)
* Paid training, vacation and holidays (vacation accrual begins on first day of employment)
* Career advancement opportunities
* Education reimbursement
* 401K program with matching contributions
* Learning platform
* And more!

At Curia, manufacturing excellence is at the heart of everything we do. The Director, Production Operations is a key member of the Springfield leadership team, responsible for managing, planning, directing, and coordinating manufacturing processes across our large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations. This leader ensures our operations are safe, compliant, cost-effective, and positioned for growth.
  
  
This is a role for a proven leader who brings both strategic vision and operational discipline. The Director contributes to the development of business and functional strategies, communicates them clearly across the site, and translates them into action. Working cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, and other departments, this leader drives high performance in cGMP compliance, schedule adherence, and customer satisfaction.
  
  
As much as this role is about operational outcomes, it is also about people. The Director identifies and develops the next generation of leaders within the organization, fostering a culture of accountability, continuous improvement, and collaboration that reflects the Curia Way.
  
  
**Essential Responsibilities**
**Strategy and Planning**

* Develop and implement short and long range goals and objectives that align with business growth and profitability targets.
* Set strategic leadership goals for key section heads within the large scale, pilot plant, and technical services organizations.
* Review operational plans to assess manufacturing capacity requirements and make recommendations to improve capacity utilization and support business development planning.
* Develop, implement, and maintain Key Performance Indicators and monitoring systems to drive high levels of performance within the department and across the organization.

Operations and Compliance
  
  

* Oversee manufacturing operations to ensure safety, quality, productivity, and efficiency, working collaboratively with the management team to prevent and resolve operational, quality, financial, and facility issues.
* Partner with Quality and Regulatory departments to drive high performance in cGMP compliance and ensure operations meet organizational requirements for quality management, health and safety, legal, and environmental standards.
* Ensure proper planning and effective execution of production activities to minimize downtime and maximize output per the production schedule, working closely with supporting departments to maintain schedule adherence.
* Proactively lead local efforts to prepare for and execute productive customer visits.
* Analyze activities, costs, operations, and forecast data to assess progress toward goals and initiate corrective action as needed to meet business and financial objectives.
* Perform other related duties as may be reasonably assigned in the course of business.

**Good Manufacturing & Documentation Practices**
Quality is something we take pride in together. You’ll perform your work in alignment with cGMP requirements and Curia’s standards to ensure our facilities support the safe and reliable manufacture of products for our customers.

* Adhere to applicable cGMP documents including SOPs, batch records, protocols, change controls, and controlled forms.
* Keep all required cGMP training current and escalate quality concerns along with proposed solutions to the Quality department.

**Required**

* Bachelor’s degree in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, or a related field
* Minimum 5–10 years of mid to senior management experience in a manufacturing or process environment
* Demonstrated understanding of the responsibilities and functions of key departments within a pharmaceutical or industrial manufacturing facility
* Strong knowledge of cGMP compliance, technical operations, and quality systems within a manufacturing environment
* Proven ability to identify, develop, and inspire leaders at multiple levels of the organization
* Excellent communication skills with the ability to present strategy and performance clearly to site and functional leadership

**Preferred**

* Experience with API development and manufacturing processes
* Certification in Lean manufacturing or Six Sigma

* Regularly required to sit, stand, walk, talk, and hear.
* Frequently required to use hands to handle or feel objects, reach with hands and arms, and climb, balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl.
* May occasionally lift and/or move up to 55 pounds.
* Visual requirements include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, color vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.

* Production environment may include moving mechanical parts, fumes or airborne particles, extreme heat, wet or humid conditions, low levels of toxic or caustic chemicals, and outdoor weather conditions.
* Noise level in the work environment is typically moderate.

existing_roles.description:
Lasko is seeking a Director of Plant Operations to lead our manufacturing facility in Franklin, Tennessee. This leader will oversee plant performance, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.
  
  
The Director will translate business priorities into effective operating plans, strengthen manufacturing processes, and build a culture of accountability and continuous improvement. Working closely with Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, Human Resources, and Finance, this individual will ensure the facility consistently delivers quality products while improving productivity, controlling costs, and supporting Lasko’s growth.
  
  
The ideal candidate is a visible, hands-on leader who builds strong teams, uses data to guide decisions, and maintains a consistent presence on the production floor.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**
*Plant Leadership and Operational Performance*

* Lead daily plant operations, coordinating production, maintenance, manufacturing support, and material flow to meet safety, quality, cost, and delivery objectives.
* Develop and execute operating plans that align production capacity, staffing, equipment, and materials with business requirements.
* Establish clear performance expectations and operating metrics; review results regularly and drive corrective actions when performance falls short.
* Partner with Supply Chain and production planning teams to manage schedules, respond to changing demand, and maintain reliable customer service.
* Resolve operational challenges quickly while implementing lasting solutions that prevent recurring issues.

*Safety, Quality, and Compliance*

* Champion a culture in which employee safety is a daily priority and leaders take ownership of safe work practices.
* Oversee plant safety, environmental performance, and facility security in partnership with the appropriate support teams.
* Ensure consistent adherence to company policies, operating procedures, and applicable requirements.
* Partner with Quality and Engineering to improve process controls, reduce defects and rework, and ensure finished products meet established standards.
* Support audits, investigations, and corrective actions, ensuring timely follow-through and sustainable improvements

*Continuous Improvement and Manufacturing Excellence*

* Lead continuous improvement initiatives that increase throughput, improve equipment reliability, reduce waste, and strengthen overall plant performance.
* Apply Lean manufacturing principles, root cause analysis, standard work, and structured problem-solving to improve operating processes.
* Use production, quality, maintenance, and cost data to identify performance gaps and prioritize improvement opportunities.
* Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to strengthen preventive maintenance programs and address equipment constraints.
* Support new product introductions, process changes, and manufacturing readiness to achieve successful production launches.

*Financial and Resource Management*

* Develop and manage plant operating budgets, monitor spending, and take action to address cost variances.
* Improve labor productivity, material utilization, energy efficiency, and material handling costs while maintaining safety and quality standards.
* Partner with Finance and Supply Chain to strengthen inventory accuracy, control work in process, and support effective inventory management.
* Identify and prioritize capital investment needs; develop business cases for equipment upgrades, automation, and facility improvements.
* Ensure people, equipment, and materials are deployed effectively to meet production commitments.

*People Leadership and Development*

* Build, coach, and develop a strong plant leadership team with clear responsibilities and measurable goals.
* Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, hiring, onboarding, training, performance management, and employee relations.
* Foster a respectful, collaborative environment that encourages employee involvement, open communication, and ownership of results.
* Develop leadership capabilities and succession plans to support long-term operational stability.
* Maintain effective communication across shifts and departments to ensure consistent priorities and execution.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including substantial leadership responsibility for plant performance and people management.
* Demonstrated success leading a manufacturing facility or a significant manufacturing operation with responsibility for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and employee development.
* Strong understanding of production planning, inventory control, equipment maintenance, quality systems, and manufacturing cost drivers.
* Experience developing and managing operating budgets, evaluating capital investments, and improving financial performance.
* Demonstrated ability to lead continuous improvement initiatives and deliver measurable operational results.
* Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to balance immediate production needs and longer-term priorities.
* Effective communication skills and the ability to work across all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, and experience using ERP systems and manufacturing performance data.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in consumer products or another high-volume manufacturing environment.
* Familiarity with injection molding, assembly operations, automation, and related manufacturing processes.
* Experience leading operations across multiple shifts and managing seasonal changes in production demand.
* Lean or Six Sigma training or certification.
* Experience leading organizational change, developing plant leaders, and strengthening employee engagement.

*Work Environment*
This position is based onsite at Lasko’s Franklin, TN manufacturing facility and requires regular presence on the production floor. Flexibility is required to support plant operations across shifts and address business needs.
  
  
**About Lasko Products**
***Love Your Air*
™**
Lasko Products is the leading air solutions brand with a reputation for reliable products, peak performance, and perpetual innovation – our commitment to our customers for over a century. Founded in 1906 by Henry Lasko in Philadelphia, Lasko has evolved for over a century to become the global leader in air solution products. From our roots in small appliances, fans, and portable heaters, we’ve grown to become the leading home comfort company while maintaining our unwavering commitment to quality and value. Today, Lasko stands as a symbol of innovation, offering consumers around the world high-performance products; portable fans, heaters, air purifiers, humidifiers, and home ventilation solutions. Our well-known brands, Lasko, B-Air, BlueDri, Air King, and Guardian Technologies, serve both consumer and commercial markets across North America and internationally. As an American company for 120 years, we take pride in upholding the spirit of hard work, trust and accessibility, ensuring that Lasko remains available to all, for generations to come. Headquartered in West Chester, Pennsylvania, with manufacturing and distribution facilities in Tennessee and Texas, Lasko intends to set the standard in the air solutions category for another 100 years.
  
  
***Lasko’s mission is to provide comfort you can trust.***
Our company’s success is based on our culture of
**GRACE**
, with five core “
*Be*
” values outlining how we live it.
  
  
**Growth Mindset —**
*Be Bold*

* We are never the finished product ─ every failure is a data point, every setback is a setup.

**Recognition —**
*Be Together*


* We win together. We celebrate together! High performance deserves to be seen ─ named, specific, remembered.

**Authenticity —**
*Be Real*

* No masks. No politics. Show up as you are, say what you mean, and mean what you say.

**Clear Communication —**
*Be Clear*

* Say it plainly. Say it once. Say it to the right person. Clarity is kindness.

**Extreme Ownership —**
Be
*Accountable*


* No blame. No excuses. Own the win and the loss. No exceptions.

**Why Join Lasko?**
At Lasko, we believe people do their best work when they’re supported ─ personally and professionally. That’s why we offer flexible hours and a hybrid work schedule for our corporate team, promoting employees to balance life and work in a way that fits their lifestyle. Our dog-friendly corporate headquarters adds a fun, welcoming atmosphere, while our competitive salaries with bonus potential recognize and reward your contributions. We also offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes a strong 401(k) match, wellness incentives, and robust health coverage. Join Lasko and be part of a legacy of innovation – at a company that values flexibility, growth, and a culture where you can thrive.

**Director of Overseas Manufacturing and Quality**
**Chefman | Product Development | Mahwah, NJ**
**About Us**
Chefman is one of North America's leading brands of small kitchen appliances, committed to building best-in-class products that make cooking accessible and enjoyable. In 2020, we launched CHEF iQ, an ecosystem of connected smart kitchen appliances designed to transform how the world cooks through intuitive guided cooking experiences and IoT-enabled technology.
  
  
**About The Role**
As Chefman continues to scale, we're looking for a Director of Overseas Manufacturing and Quality to elevate how we partner with our overseas manufacturing network and ensure our growing product portfolio is built with the consistency and precision our customers expect.
  
  
This is not a desk job. We need a leader who has personally run a factory floor, someone who can walk into an assembly line, spot a process problem before it becomes a quality escape, and work directly with factory teams to fix it. You'll serve as the critical bridge between our design and product development teams here in Mahwah and our manufacturing partners in China, helping ensure that what we design translates seamlessly into what gets built at scale.
  
  
We're looking for a leader with deep, sustained manufacturing expertise, ideally 10 to 15 years building that expertise with one organization, who is ready to bring that experience to a fast-growing, entrepreneurial consumer brand. This role requires extensive travel to China and a genuine passion for being present where products come to life.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead manufacturing strategy and execution across our overseas partner network, from tooling and assembly process design through high-volume mass production
* Partner early and often with Product Development and Industrial Design teams, bringing manufacturing expertise directly into design decisions to support manufacturability, cost efficiency, and quality from day one
* Champion consistency and best-practice alignment across factory SOPs, assembly procedures, and quality control standards across all manufacturing partners
* Maintain a strong, regular presence on assembly lines, staying close to daily production and building the kind of trusted, collaborative relationships with factory teams that drive continuous improvement
* Build and maintain rigorous reporting and documentation systems that give leadership clear visibility into yield, quality performance, and production trends across all partner sites
* Lead structured root-cause investigations (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone) when quality or performance opportunities arise, partnering closely with factory teams to implement durable, lasting solutions
* Serve as the senior point of contact for resolving complex production challenges, balancing quality, cost, and delivery priorities
* Build and develop a team of manufacturing and quality engineers to support the company's growing production needs
* Evaluate and help develop new manufacturing partnerships and capacity as the business scales
* Own the manufacturing cost and efficiency relationship, driving continuous improvement in profitability alongside quality

**Qualifications**

* A demonstrated track record of driving measurable improvements to product quality, yield, and profitability through close factory partnership
* Deep, working-level understanding of injection molding, sheet metal, electromechanical assembly, and tooling processes, built through genuine hands-on experience
* Strong background in structured root-cause problem solving and driving continuous improvement initiatives with manufacturing partners
* Experience developing and aligning SOPs and best practices across multiple factory sites
* A natural inclination to stay close to product design conversations and offer manufacturing perspective early in the process
* Strong reporting and documentation discipline
* Willingness and ability to travel extensively to China, including extended stays as needed
* A career history reflecting deep, sustained expertise built over time
* Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field
* Mandarin fluency strongly preferred
* Experience with connected/IoT consumer products is a strong plus

Be part of the global Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) Engineering leadership team driving factory improvements, product improvements for producibility and cost savings, manufacturing technology implementation, and new product development for Honeywell Aerospace.
  
  
We are hiring a Sr Director to lead the global ISC Advanced Manufacturing Engineering (AME) team for New Product Introduction (NPI) supporting programs across the Aerospace portfolio.
  
  
In this role, you will leverage your extensive product development experience and leadership skills. You will drive continuous improvement to develop new products, processes, and standards in support of the organization's business strategies with a direct impact on development program success. You will develop strategy, hold teams accountable and deliver high impact business results.

* Operate as a change agent to embed producibility into our core design processes.
* Build Employee Engagement and Skills through the development of standard work, clear roles and responsibilities, and effective training programs.
* Design and develop Management Operating Systems to ensure effective team operations, driving results to program and department objectives.
* Work closely with the SBU engineering team, Program Management, and ISC leaders to build cross-organizational alignment

**Qualifications**
**YOU MUST HAVE**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited institution in a technical discipline such as the sciences, technology, engineering or mathematics
* 8 years of experience in New Product Development
* Knowledge of manufacturing processes
* Experience working with suppliers on technical issues
* Track record of managing multiple projects with demonstrated results on a macro scale
* Experience leading a team with direct line reporting responsibility
* Abitlity to travel 30%

**Us Person Requirements**
Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. Person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status or have the ability to obtain an export authorization.
  
  
**WE VALUE**

* Advanced degree in engineering or business
* Exceptional data analysis and communication skills
* Willingness to raise standards each year to drive organizational excellence
* Ability to make sound and timely judgments in ambiguous environment
* Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience.
* Diverse and global teaming and collaboration
* Balance between demand and capacity when establishing priorities for the organization.

**For Mn Candidates**
The annual base salary range for this position is $238,000-$297,000. Please note that this salary information serves as a general guideline. Honeywell considers various factors when extending an offer, including but not limited to the scope and responsibilities of the position, the candidate's work experience, education and training, key skills, as well as market and business considerations.
  
  
This position is incentive eligible.
  
  
**Benefits**
Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:
  
  

* Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
* Short-term and long-term disability coverage
* 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
* Employee assistance program and educational assistance
* Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
* Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits: https://honeywellaerospacebenefits.com/
  
  
**POSTING TIMELINE**
The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates.
  
  
Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At
**Honeywell Aerospace**
(NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.
  
  
Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.
  
  
Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.
  
  
Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.
  
  
Honeywell Aerospace Products And Services Are Found On Aircraft Across Commercial Aviation, Defense And Space. We Operate Through Three Business Areas
  
  
Electronic Solutions develops the avionics, navigation systems, sensors and electromagnetic defense technology on board 90% of the world's aircraft
  
  
Engines & Power Systems provides the propulsion, auxiliary power and electrical systems that keep those aircraft flying
  
  
Control Systems supplies the thermal and motion control systems that support takeoff, landing and the safety of everyone on board
  
  
With approximately 58,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, we are also advancing systems for autonomous and supersonic platforms — bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com
  
  
Join Honeywell Aerospace! Our aerospace innovations bring people together, make the world safer and more secure, and help humankind reach for the stars. Now we’re shaping aviation’s future with sustainable aviation fuels, smarter cockpits, ultra-efficient engines, smart airports, flying taxis and much more.

existing_roles.description:
About the company

We're an EV commercial vehicle manufacturer based in Orange County, California. We design and build our medium-duty electric vehicles in-house, and next year's production is already fully sold out.

* 1,000+ vehicles built so far
* A 2,000-vehicle order from one of the largest US parcel carriers, due by end of 2027
* $650M+ raised, including a $200M+ Series recently
* Growing beyond trucks into energy storage, autonomy and defense

The role

We've sold out of trucks, and we don't want it to happen again. We're hiring a
**Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering**
to grow our production capacity and own how we get there.

You'll lead the team that designs, buys and launches our new lines and equipment. Your decisions will show up directly in how many trucks leave the factory each month.

What you'll do

* Lead and grow the advanced manufacturing engineering team
* Own the manufacturing strategy and capital plan for scaling production
* Take new lines and equipment from concept through design, build, install, testing and start of production
* Plan capacity so production keeps ahead of customer demand
* Run equipment and facility projects to budget and schedule, and present them to the executive team
* Work closely with vehicle engineering, supply chain and operations so new designs can be built at volume
* Bring in integrators and equipment suppliers, and manage them through delivery

What you'll bring

**Must have**

* 8+ years in manufacturing engineering, with 4+ years leading teams
* A track record of growing production capacity: new lines, factory expansions or ramping to full rate
* Hands-on experience taking equipment from specification through install, testing and launch
* Experience building and managing capital budgets
* A degree in engineering (mechanical, manufacturing, industrial, chemical or similar)

**Nice to have**

* Background in EV, automotive, commercial vehicles or batteries. High-volume aerospace, heavy equipment or other complex hardware also welcome.
* Start-up or scale-up experience, ideally through early production and ramp-up
* Experience building a new factory from the ground up

**Sierra Space Careers:**
At Sierra Space, we build the missions and systems that keep our world secure in the domain above Earth.
  
  
Sierra Space team members share a spirit of innovation and collaboration and a belief that we can deliver on the boldest missions in space today. Together with our customers, we aim to safeguard our nation, sustain human presence in space, and secure the freedom of operations in low Earth orbit and beyond.
  
  
Our success is measured by the trust of those who rely on what we build and deliver, and our technologies keep the United States and its allies mission-ready throughout space.
  
  
We are mission-driven, and together, we are an extraordinary team.
  
  
**About The Role**
Sierra Space is expanding its satellite manufacturing plant in Englewood, Colorado, designed to deliver significant production and test capability for future civil and national security satellite programs. The Senior Manager, Production will be a foundational operational leader for this facility — translating strategic plans into the day-to-day objectives, processes, and workforce structure that define the plant from the ground up.
  
  
This role directly shapes how production is built and scaled at a new high-capability manufacturing site. The Senior Manager will oversee multiple disciplines or departments, manage large teams and complex cross-functional projects, and drive the operational initiatives that establish Dove Valley as a center of excellence for satellite and spacecraft component manufacturing, assembly, integration, and test.
  
  
The role requires regular interaction with executive leadership on sensitive, complex, and cross-functional matters, along with the financial acumen to manage budgets supporting both near-term production and long-term facility growth. The ideal candidate brings a proven record of managing large teams and complex projects, deep knowledge of aerospace and defense industry standards, and the leadership to foster a culture of excellence as Dove Valley matures to support civil and national security satellite missions.
  
  
**About You**
Our mission is driven by an unyielding commitment to advancing space-based technology in service of our customers and safeguarding national security. We seek individuals who are passionate about innovating beyond boundaries and relentlessly pursuing solutions that protect, preserve and empower – to join us in this critical mission.
  
  
We’re looking for team members who align with our values, mission and goals – while also meeting the minimum qualifications below. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities:**

* Translates functional plans into operational plans; identifies and executes operational initiatives.
* Ensures execution in accordance with financial plans; accountable for area budgets.
* Embodies our culture and great leadership; leads and supports change initiatives.
* Manages activities of two or more disciplines or a department, providing direct supervision to managers or individual contributors.
* Drives the strategy and success of larger projects which contribute to multiple areas of the organization.
* Translates functional plans into operational objectives to deliver results, providing guidance to subordinates.
* Contributes to financial planning and executes according to plans, goals, and priorities. Accountable for select budgets.
* Interacts regularly with leadership, including executive level, on cross-functional and/or customer matters requiring the ability to persuade in sensitive and complex situations.
* Works on issues where analysis of situations or data requires conceptual thinking and an in-depth knowledge of organizational objectives.
* Upholds and models company values; holds others accountable to values.

**Minimum Qualifications:**

* Requires bachelor’s degree in a related field (or equivalent work experience in lieu of degree).
* Typically, 8+ years of relevant work experience with a significant portion in a managerial or leadership role. Proven track record of successfully managing large teams and complex projects.
* The ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance is required
* Upholds and models company values; ability to hold others accountable to values.
* Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
* Able to translate functional plans into operational plans; identifies and executes operational initiatives.
* In-depth knowledge of industry standards, regulations, and best practices.
* Strong financial acumen and budget management skills.
* Experience supporting organizational changes.
* Current security clearance or the ability to obtain and hold a clearance

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Advanced degree in a relevant field.
* Extensive experience in the production of Satellites and Spacecraft Components.
* Demonstrated ability to lead through change and drive continuous improvement initiatives.
* Strong analytical skills and experience with data-driven decision-making.
* Familiarity with advanced project management tools and methodologies.
* Proven ability to interact effectively with executive leadership and external stakeholders.
* Familiarity with Lean, Six-sigma, and/or Theory of Constraints Manufacturing Principles
* Understanding of Assembly, Integration and Test practices
* Background in the Aerospace and Defense Industry, the US Department of Defense or US Military

Compensation:
  
  
Pay Range:
  
  
$151,141.00 - $207,841.00
  
  
Your actual base compensation will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on job-related knowledge and skills, education, experience, internal equity and market competitiveness.

This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Top Secret U.S. Security Clearance. U.S. Citizenship status is required as this position needs an active U.S. Security Clearance for employment. Non-U.S. Citizens may not be eligible to obtain a security clearance.  The Department of Defense Consolidated Adjudications Facility (DoD CAF), a federal government agency, handles the adjudicative aspects of the security clearance eligibility process for industry applicants. Adjudicative factors which affect the outcome of the eligibility determination include, but are not limited to, allegiance to the U.S., foreign influence, foreign preference, criminal conduct, security violations and illegal drug use.

At Sierra Space, we are committed to your personal and professional development. We empower you to make profound and meaningful contributions and foster a vibrant culture of collaboration, where teamwork ignites breakthrough innovations.
  
  
We also offer a generous benefit package, including medical, dental, and vision plans, 401(k) with 150% match up to 6%, life insurance, 3 weeks paid time off, and more.

It's exciting to work for a company that makes the world measurably better.
  
  
We're committed to bringing safety, quality, and customer focus to the business of advanced ceramics manufacturing.
  
  
**Job Title**
Sr Manager Manufacturing Operations
  
  
As the Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations you will be the senior production leader for the Oak Ridge Plant manufacturing execution, responsible for translating site priorities and customer requirements into safe, reliable manufacturing results. You will lead all production operations through a period of significant growth and increasing customer demand, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, productivity, capacity utilization, and workforce performance.
  
  
As a leader, you will create and drives urgency, clarity, and accountability across the manufacturing organization. You will lead through production managers and supervisors, partners across functions to remove barriers, and represents the plant on customer calls related to production performance, capacity, delivery, and recovery plans. Overall site strategy, P&L ownership, capital allocation, and leadership of non-production functions remain with senior plant/regional leadership.
  
  
**Roles & Responsibilities:**

* Lead production execution across the Oak Ridge manufacturing operation, establishing clear priorities and delivering safety, quality, output, delivery, productivity, and workforce objectives.
* Lead, coach, and develop production managers, supervisors, and frontline teams; set clear expectations, reinforce accountability, and build leadership capability for continued growth.
* Create a visible and engaging leadership presence on the manufacturing floor, connecting employees to customer commitments, business priorities, and daily performance expectations.
* Establish disciplined daily management systems, operating rhythms, performance metrics, and escalation processes that enable teams to identify issues early and respond with urgency.
* Identify and remove constraints across labor, equipment, process flow, materials, maintenance, quality, and manufacturing systems to improve throughput and capacity utilization.
* Partner with Planning, Supply Chain, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Human Resources, Finance, and Commercial teams to align resources, resolve barriers, and deliver production commitments.
* Represent the plant on customer calls and internal operating reviews, partnering with Commercial, Planning, Quality, and other teams to communicate production status, risks, recovery actions, and commitments.
* Lead the manufacturing response to customer-impacting issues, ensuring timely containment, clear communication, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and sustainable resolution.
* Use production, labor, maintenance, yield, quality, capacity, and delivery data to identify trends, prioritize actions, and drive measurable improvement.
* Champion Lean, Theory of Constraints, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement to reduce waste and variation, improve flow, and strengthen operational capability.
* Support approved equipment installations, capacity expansions, and manufacturing-readiness activities required to meet current and future demand.
* Ensure production activities comply with safety, environmental, quality, regulatory, and company requirements, reinforcing that safety and quality are never compromised.

**Job Requirements:**
**Education & Experience:**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, Business, or a related field; equivalent relevant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
* At least 7 years of progressive manufacturing or operations experience, including significant responsibility for leading managers, supervisors, or large production teams.
* Demonstrated success leading manufacturing through growth, capacity expansion, operational transformation, or substantial increases in customer demand.
* Proven results improving throughput, delivery, productivity, quality, capacity utilization, and operational stability.
* Experience applying Lean, Theory of Constraints, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement and problem-solving methods.
* Experience in complex, high-precision manufacturing such as advanced materials, ceramics, semiconductor, electronics, aerospace, or medical devices is preferred.

**Functional/Technical Knowledge, Skills & Abilities:**

* Visible, decisive leadership style that creates alignment, urgency, engagement, and accountability.
* Ability to lead through other leaders and strengthen the performance of a multi-layer manufacturing organization.
* Strong understanding of production planning, capacity management, equipment utilization, labor productivity, yield, quality, delivery, and manufacturing cost.
* Ability to influence across functions and resolve complex operational barriers without direct authority over partner teams.
* Executive-level communication skills and the credibility to represent manufacturing with customers, frontline employees, technical teams, and senior leaders.
* Composure and sound judgment during operational pressure, changing priorities, and customer escalations.
* Business acumen to connect manufacturing performance with customer outcomes, revenue delivery, and sustainable growth.
* Learning agility and leadership potential to progress toward broader plant leadership responsibility.

Why This Role Matters
  
  
Oak Ridge is entering an important phase of growth. This role provides the opportunity to shape how the manufacturing organization scales, strengthen leadership capability, improve customer performance, and build the operating discipline needed for sustained success. The position offers significant exposure to senior manufacturing leadership and an opportunity to develop toward broader plant leadership responsibilities.

existing_roles.description:
Divergent is building the new industrial age. Every day, our teams design, manufacture, and assemble advanced systems for some of the world’s most demanding industries. Our integrated engineering and manufacturing platform transforms complex designs into production-ready solutions, helping customers move faster, build smarter, and deliver critical systems when they matter most. Divergent is a qualified Tier 1 supplier to global automotive OEMs and supports leading U.S. aerospace and defense companies.
  
  
Join us and help push the boundaries of what can be built.
  
  
Purpose
  
  
We are seeking an exceptional, results-driven
**Senior Manager of Additive Manufacturing Operations**
to lead and scale our Factory 1 production organization. This is a high-impact leadership role responsible for driving world-class execution across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and people development while shaping the future of manufacturing.
  
  
The Additive Manufacturing organization leverages proprietary, state-of-the-art systems and processes to execute metal laser powder bed fusion (LPBF), depowdering, manual and automated support removal, surface finishing, heat treatment, and inspection across multiple factory sites supporting both prototype and high-rate production.
  
  
This role is ideal for an ambitious operations leader who thrives in fast-paced, high-growth environments and combines strong manufacturing fundamentals with data-driven decision making, automation, and continuous improvement. Beyond delivering daily operational performance, this leader will develop people, build scalable operating systems, and partner with engineering to industrialize new technologies that will define the next generation of manufacturing.
  
  
The ideal candidate is energized by difficult manufacturing challenges, inspires high-performing teams, and is passionate about building organizations capable of delivering exceptional results.
  
  
The Role
  
  
**Operational Leadership**

* Lead Factory 1 additive manufacturing operations to achieve world-class performance in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and equipment reliability.
* Build, develop, and mentor a high-performing team while fostering a culture of accountability, ownership, urgency, and continuous improvement.
* Drive disciplined daily management through standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and operational rigor.
* Optimize manufacturing flow by increasing equipment uptime, eliminating bottlenecks, improving process repeatability, and maximizing production throughput.
* Partner closely with Platform Development, Manufacturing Engineering, and Automation teams to successfully launch new equipment, technologies, and manufacturing capabilities.

**Operational Excellence**

* Champion Lean Manufacturing principles and continuous improvement across all additive manufacturing processes.
* Establish scalable operating systems that improve efficiency, stability, and manufacturing readiness as production grows.
* Utilize manufacturing data, KPIs, and analytics to drive operational decisions and prioritize improvement initiatives.
* Develop meaningful performance dashboards and operating rhythms that enable rapid identification and resolution of production issues.
* Lead initiatives to improve Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), first-pass yield, cycle time, labor productivity, and cost per part.

**Equipment Reliability & Technical Capability**

* Continue developing the in-house Additive Manufacturing Service organization by strengthening technical capability, preventive maintenance programs, troubleshooting processes, and technician training.
* Drive reliability initiatives that maximize printer availability, reduce unplanned downtime, and improve long-term equipment performance.
* Partner with technical teams to identify recurring equipment issues and implement sustainable corrective actions.

Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form!
  
  
In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by
*TIME*
as a “Best Invention”,
*MIT Technology Review*
as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and
*Fast Company*
as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia.
  
  
Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing - might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.
  
  
**Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.**
Role Description
  
  
As the Senior Manager of Assembly Manufacturing Engineering, you will serve as the primary architect of the production lifecycle, bridging the gap between research prototypes and high-volume factory operations. You will lead a multidisciplinary team of engineers to develop and internalize robust manufacturing processes for both battery enclosures and module/pack assembly—including robotic joining, sealing, electrolyte filling, and leak testing. By owning the full equipment lifecycle, from defining detailed user requirements through to factory testing and final site commissioning, you ensure that production lines are world-class, delivering a "machine that builds the machine" with precision and technical rigor.
  
  
Strategically, your objective is to drive operational scale by ensuring products are designed specifically for ease of manufacturing and assembly during the earliest development phases. You will champion a data-driven culture that utilizes failure mode analysis and advanced root-cause investigation to reduce production risks and achieve aggressive targets for quality, output rate, and equipment uptime. By fostering collaboration between Product Design, Quality, and Supply Chain, you will manage the critical transition from initial design to full-scale production, ensuring that every process is statistically validated to guarantee long-term reliability and cost-effectiveness.
  
  
**What You'll Do**

* Lead the development and optimization of battery manufacturing processes for battery assembly manufacturing.
* Ensure highly capable processes are identified and demonstrated for our production facilities ahead of detailed equipment design.
* Oversee the design and implementation of manufacturing processes such as: manual and robotic assembly, joining, sealing, system leak testing, and quality checks to achieve optimal performance and reliability.
* Collaborate with product design team, R&D, quality, and supply chain, to translate product requirements into a battery design and manufacturing process that achieve our company targets.
* Collaborate cross functionally to develop and maintain PFMEA, process specifications, measurement systems GR&R, control plan, and quality inspection methods (incoming, outgoing, and in-process).
* Lead troubleshooting efforts to identify root causes of manufacturing issues and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
* Internalize responsibility for delivery of equipment and processes that enable the operations team to achieve factory production metrics (quality, yield, rate, and availability).
* Identify trends/correlations, and make data-driven decisions for process optimization.

**What You'll Bring**

* Hands-on experience in a high-volume manufacturing organization.
* Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical engineering, Chemical Engineering, Electrical Engineering.
* 10 years of experience in engineering roles within battery manufacturing or a related industry, with expertise in complex assembly processes. 4+ leading technical teams.
* Demonstrated experience in manufacturing equipment procurement, setup, and commissioning, including a clear understanding of equipment qualification and validation protocols.
* Strong understanding of lean manufacturing principles and their application in a high-volume production environment.
* Proven track record of successfully leading cross-functional teams in the development and optimization of manufacturing processes for electrochemical systems.
* Proficiency in process engineering principles, statistical analysis, and quality management systems for process optimization and improvement.
* Strong communication skills with the ability to collaborate effectively with multidisciplinary teams and convey technical concepts to diverse stakeholders.
* Leadership and mentoring abilities with a commitment to fostering a culture of continuous learning and accelerated innovation through quick iteration.
* Experience working in a fast-paced startup environment is a plus.

*This opportunity is based out of Form Factory 1 – Form Energy’s 550,000-square-foot, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility located in Weirton, WV, a commutable distance from Pittsburgh. Purpose-built for high-volume, advanced battery production, Form Factory 1 is a hub of fast-moving, collaborative work driving a new era of large-scale American energy manufacturing in the heart of the Rust Belt.*
*Relocation assistance is available.*
*Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here.*
*When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.*
*To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.*
*If you may require reasonable accommodations to participate in our interview process, please contact accommodations@formenergy.com. Requests for accommodations will be treated with discretion.*
*Form Energy is committed to maintaining the privacy of our applicants. Please be aware that we will
**never**
solicit sensitive personal information such as Social Security numbers or bank account details during the recruiting or hiring process.*

**Job Description**
As an S&C Electric team member, you’ll work on projects that have real-world impact. You’ll help transform the grid for resilient and reliable power worldwide. S&C has more than a 100-year history of innovation and has been 100% employee-owned since 2012. We continue this legacy as a trusted, forward-thinking leader in the electrical industry. You will advance a safer, more reliable, and more resilient electrical grid. Our products help the grid adapt to severe weather and transition to clean energy. We’re big enough to be a respected industry leader but small enough for you to impact our company directly. Our commitment gives you opportunities to impact on and off the job positively. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner.
  
  
**Hours**

* 8:00 am – 5:00 pm (Mon-Fri) On Site Palatine, IL

**Compensation**
At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices.
**The estimated annual base salary range for this position is $154,968- $205,332.60.**
Individual pay within this salary range is determined by several compensable factors, including performance, knowledge, job-related skills and experience, and relevant education or training. This role is also eligible for S&C’s annual incentive plan (AIP), subject to eligibility criteria.
  
  
**Join Our Team as a Senior Manager – Productions Operations!**
The Senior Manager – Production Operations is responsible for planning, overseeing, and managing the operations and production processes for the department, leading a team of Managers, Assistant Managers, and Supervisors to achieve strategic Objectives and Key Results (OKRs), and Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) in safety, quality, delivery, and cost (SQDC). The Senior Manager – Production Operations focuses on strategic and tactical operations planning with a mid-term focus, contributing towards greater functional strategies, directing the smooth operations of multiple departments, driving strategic problem-solving and continuous improvement initiatives, reporting out to executive leadership on results, and making strategic adjustments and countermeasures when targets are missed.
  
  
**Key Responsibilities**

* Health & Safety Compliance: Drive a safety-first culture, ensuring leaders understand and enforce safety rules. Ensure that health & safety is considered in all departmental plans in order to maintain and promote a safety-conscious manufacturing environment and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements and industry standards related to production operations.
* Leadership & People Management: Lead, inspire, and develop a high-performing team. Role model appropriate and professional workplace behaviors, address/mediate conflicts to restore harmony, and support a positive, healthy, and inclusive workplace culture in accordance with S&C's mission, vision, values, and guiding principles. Manage departmental administrative team member processes, including but not limited to recruitment, induction, vacation management, performance reviews, performance improvement plans, and workforce/succession planning. Proactively establish, monitor, and hold team members accountable to clear responsibilities and accountabilities; provide ongoing performance feedback, both positive and developmental; address performance gaps in a timely manner; recognize and reward achievements and initiate decisions for corrective actions and terminations where required. Foster a culture that supports the growth and development of team members and proactively train, mentor, and coach team members.
* Strategy Implementation: Cascade strategies to develop mid-term tactical and operational plans for the function, in line with the company’s overall business objectives, including automation, insourcing, and unattended machining. Oversee a leadership team that directs the day-to-day operations of activities within the department and span of control, ensuring the timely and cost-effective delivery of outputs to KPIs. Work with senior leaders to recommend and implement strategic adjustments to operational plans in order to meet OKRs and KPIs.
* Production Planning & Operations: Lead strategic production planning initiatives, collaborating with cross-functional teams to develop a mid-term plan for the department and initiate strategies that contribute to long-term production planning. Work with leaders to optimize production schedules, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity plans and processing methods. Evaluate machine resources to ensure continued production and minimal downtime. Establish a balance between increased productivity and reduced costs of manufacturing operations. Set mid-term productivity goals and analyze report-outs from Managers.
* Lean Performance Systems: Recommend and implement goals for departmental performance improvement, supporting leaders as they identify and implement process improvements to enhance production efficiency, reduce costs, and increase overall operational effectiveness. Collaborate with other leaders to formulate high-level solutions and develop plans for how to implement improvements throughout multi-faceted functions. Serve as a change agent by influencing, communicating, and institutionalizing a culture of continuous improvement, simplification, standard work, process improvement, and lean principles.
* Quality Management: Oversee the implementation of broad quality control programs, ensuring leaders fully understand quality issues and their corresponding solutions.Discuss and understand high-level, multi-faceted quality issues and help leaders formulate resolutions. Monitor and guide leaders responsible for the department’s communication of corrective action plans, resolutions, and quality results.
* Reporting: Analyzes reports and reviews provided by first-line supervisors. Communicates regularly with upper management regarding problems impacting production. Reports issues regarding production, quality, maintenance, or personnel to senior and executive leadership.
* Budget Management: Develop and manage the function’s budget, ensuring accuracy and appropriate allocation of resources to maximize ROI and the achievement of larger functional strategies and objectives. Approve expenditures for the achievement of operational goals and work with senior leaders to identify investment opportunities for gains towards mid-term goals.
* Compliance: Understand and comply with all applicable Company policies and rules.
* Maintain regular and punctual attendance.
* Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
* Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
* Drive a car or other vehicle.
* Other responsibilities as assigned.

**Required**
**What you’ll need to succeed:**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical discipline such as Engineering, or a related field.
* Beliefs in, and alignment with, S&C Guiding Principles and Core Values
* 10+ years of manufacturing experience in an industrial metals fabrication environment, including advanced CNC machining, welding, laser cutting, forming, punching, stamping and related finishing operations.
* 5+ years of supervisory or management experience in a fabrication environment leading hourly and salaried employees.
* Leadership experience in workforce planning, scheduling, and staffing, employee development, coaching, and performance management.Experience managing multiple shifts is preferred.
* Knowledge of precision machining processes and practices within a high mix, low-to-medium volume environment.
* Demonstrated track record of lean manufacturing leadership, sustained improvements, and KPI attainment.
* Great leadership skills within a multi-level manufacturing environment, with an ability to lead, guide, motivate, and delegate to deliver results.
* Sound critical thinking, organizational, planning, and project management skills, and creative problem-solving when obstacles arise.
* Great interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, navigate and resolve conflict, moderate behaviors, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
* Excellent communication skills, (written, verbal, listening, and presentation) ability to liaise with internal and external stakeholders at all levels, from leadership to support staff, and present influentially to achieve buy-in from executives, managers, and team members.
* Sound analytical skills with the ability to use and analyze data to drive informed decisions, problem-solve difficult issues, and leverage data and learnings to drive continuous improvement.
* Proven success partnering across teams, creating effective partnerships at all levels, and collaborating at an operational level.
* Adapts to change and different ways of doing things quickly and positively and finds ways to get things accomplished, even when faced with challenges.
* Proficient computer skills, including Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, Word, Outlook) and preferably, Oracle.

**Preferred**

* Master’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or a related field.
* Six Sigma Certification(s).
* Certified Lean Six Sigma (CLSS).
* Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE).

S&C Electric is committed to equal-opportunity employment. All employees and applicants will be considered without regard to age, color, disability, gender, national origin, race, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity, protected veteran status, or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law. If you are an individual with a disability and need an accommodation to complete the application, please email us at TAsupport@sandc.com.
  
  
No fixed deadline
  
  
**About Us**
In 1909, S&C Electric Company transformed the delivery of safe, reliable electricity with the invention of the Liquid Power Fuse. Today, as the world faces extreme weather events and the demand for electricity grows, S&C continues to innovate and advance the electrical grid, ensuring reliable and resilient power for homes, communities, and critical infrastructure around the world.

**About The Role**
As a Senior Manager, LEU+ Manufacturing Process Engineering, you will lead process engineering. This role is part of the LEU+ Manufacturing Program, a capital expansion of Westinghouse's Columbia Fuel Fabrication Facility. The program aims to manufacture LEU+ (higher-enrichment low-enriched uranium) nuclear fuel. Accountable for the design, qualification and startup of the new manufacturing processes, including uranium conversion, pellet production, fuel rod and assembly manufacturing, uranium recovery and recycling, and the laboratory and maintenance areas. Plan and direct the methods, equipment and processes needed to deliver safe, high-quality, cost-effective fuel, and develops the engineers who deliver them.
  
  
You will report to the Project Director, LEU+ Manufacturing Program and be located at Columbia, SC. You will support this role 100% onsite.

* Lead the LEU+ Process Engineering organization with responsibility for safety, regulatory compliance, product quality, technical execution, cost, schedule, and operational readiness.
* Lead process engineering activities supporting nuclear safety, including Integrated Safety Analysis, hazard analysis, IROFS, criticality safety, NRC licensing activities, and regulatory change control.
* Oversee process engineering deliverables from initial design through equipment procurement, installation, commissioning, qualification, startup, and turnover to Operations.
* Ensure manufacturing equipment and processes meet product quality, nuclear safety, performance, and qualification requirements.

**About Komline**

As a pioneering leader in advanced separation technologies, Komline has established a global reputation for engineering excellence. Through our combination of innovative design, cutting-edge manufacturing capabilities, and decades of industry experience, we consistently deliver the highest quality equipment from our integrated manufacturing facilities. Serving our core markets of Water & Process, Agricultural & Renewables, and Industrials, we pride ourselves on providing comprehensive separation solutions precisely tailored to our clients' requirements. With a strong track record of strategic growth and acquisitions, Komline continues to expand its solution portfolio and technical capabilities while maintaining our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction.

**This Opportunity**

The Director, Operational Excellence is responsible for building, deploying, and sustaining the Komline Business System (KBS), a consistent operating excellence system across all Komline sites. This leader will partner with Business Unit General Managers, Plant Managers, and functional leaders to improve safety, quality, delivery, cost, working capital, productivity, and overall operating discipline while respecting the P&L accountability of each business. The role will lead Komline’s enterprise continuous improvement (CI) capability, develop CI talent, and ensure proven practices are shared and scaled across the network.

The successful candidate is a hands-on manufacturing leader who combines strong Lean expertise with business judgment, credibility on the shop floor, and the executive presence to influence decentralized business leaders. This leader will be equally comfortable coaching a plant team, challenging a site improvement plan, and communicating enterprise priorities to senior leadership.

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, this enterprise-wide role supports all Komline operating sites.

**Responsibilities:**

* Develop and lead implementation of the KBS Operational Excellence strategy, roadmap, standards, and multi-year improvement agenda across all sites
* Lead, coach, and develop the CI Manager team and other improvement resources; establish clear site coverage, priorities, and deployment expectations
* Partner with GMs and Plant Managers to identify the highest-impact opportunities and build robust, financially validated site-level improvement pipelines that deliver sustained results in safety, productivity, delivery, lead time, quality, inventory, cost, and working capital
* Establish and sustain common Lean / KBS operating practices, including daily management, visual management, standard work, problem solving, RCCM, value-stream improvement, kaizen, and leader standard work
* Create a practical maturity assessment for Operational Excellence and use it to prioritize coaching, capability building, and site support; track improvements in maturity and consistent adoption of core operating practices
* Drive measurable productivity and capacity improvements through flow, labor optimization, constraint removal, setup reduction, layout improvement, and waste elimination
* Partner with Industrial Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, EHS, Finance, Engineering, HR, and other enterprise functions to quantify benefits and ensure improvements are sustained
* Build CI capability within site leadership and frontline teams through training, coaching, kaizen leadership, and development of local change agents
* Establish common operational KPI definitions and review routines that enable benchmarking and the sharing and scaling of best practices across Komline
* Support acquisition integration by assessing operational maturity, identifying improvement opportunities, and integrating acquired sites into Komline’s operating system
* Provide regular enterprise-level reporting to the COO on CI pipeline, benefits realization, site maturity, risks, and resource priorities
* Promote a culture of accountability, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement while maintaining strong partnership with decentralized business leadership

**Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, Business, or a related field
* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, continuous improvement, operational excellence, industrial engineering, or related leadership roles
* Demonstrated success leading Lean / continuous improvement across multiple sites or business units
* Strong knowledge of Lean manufacturing, daily management, kaizen, standard work, value-stream mapping, structured problem solving, and performance management
* Proven ability to influence GMs, Plant Managers, and functional leaders without relying on direct authority
* Strong business and financial acumen with the ability to translate operational improvements into measurable financial impact
* Excellent leadership, coaching, facilitation, communication, and executive presentation skills
* Ability to travel approximately 50%+, depending on site and project needs

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Lean leadership certification or equivalent and/or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt
* Experience in multi-site industrial, engineered-product, capital-equipment, or process-equipment manufacturing
* Experience integrating acquired businesses or deploying a common operating system across decentralized businesses
* Experience with plant layout, flow optimization, capacity improvement, and working-capital initiatives
* MBA or advanced technical/operations degree

**Equal Opportunity Statement:**
Komline is an EEO employer – M/F/Vets/Disabled

existing_roles.description:
Global Director, Operational Excellence COE
  
  
At Nouryon, our global team takes positive action every day, to reach higher collectively and individually. We create innovative and sustainable solutions for our customers to answer society’s needs – today and in the future.
  
  
We are looking for team members who bring ideas forward, champion others and work together to do better. Does that sound like you?
  
  
**About the job**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence (OpEx) COE is a senior leadership role responsible for defining the strategic direction, standards, and governance of Nouryon’s global OpEx program. This role owns the organizational design, frameworks, methodologies, and capability pipelines that enable sustainable continuous improvement across 63 manufacturing sites in the Integrated Supply Chain (ISC) organization – spanning the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
This role is the architect of OpEx productivity engine. The COE Director owns the design of the systems, standards, and organizational capabilities that enable VMC and FMC delivery – including ownership of the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking (ANT) and performance reporting (PowerBI). Execution of productivity targets is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role ensures those teams are equipped, aligned, and operating within a governance structure capable of sustaining results.
  
  
This role leads a newly consolidated Center of Excellence that brings together CI methodology and Lean/Six Sigma certification, ISC Learning & Development, End-to-End Process Management, and Manufacturing Excellence under a single governance structure. The COE Director sets priorities, establishes the program architecture, and holds accountability for outcomes – operating through a team of direct reports who own execution across regions. Key relationships span the COO, regional OpEx Managers, Site Directors, and ISC functional leaders across three regions.
  
  
This is a permanent, full-time position reporting to the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing, based in a Nouryon regional hub (Amsterdam, Houston, or Shanghai) with global travel of 15–25%.
  
  
**In your future role as the Global Director, Operational Excellence COE, you will**
**CI Methodology, Standards & Governance**

* Own the global Operational Excellence methodology, ensuring a consistent, fit-for-purpose CI framework is deployed across all 63 Nouryon manufacturing sites.

* Define and govern the Lean/Six Sigma certification pathway from Yellow Belt through Master Black Belt, establishing quality standards for program content, assessment, and progression.
* Partner with regional OpEx Managers to translate global standards into site-level execution plans, maintaining strategic alignment while enabling regional adaptation.
* Establish and sustain a durable CI Governance model – defining the review cadence, accountability structure, and performance mechanisms that ensure CI maturity compounds over time across the Nouryon network.
* Own the enterprise systems of record for productivity tracking and performance reporting, including the ANT productivity platform and PowerBI reporting architecture, ensuring data integrity and leadership visibility across all sites.

**ISC Learning & Development**

* Lead the design and continuous improvement of the ISC Learning & Development program, spanning CI capability, technical skills, and leadership development for the ISC organization.
* Direct the L&D team to build and maintain a structured curriculum that supports onboarding, role progression, and organizational capability uplift.
* Connect L&D investment directly to VMC and FMC delivery targets, ensuring program outcomes are measurable and business-relevant.
* Own the design mandate for Digital Literacy and AI capability across the ISC organization – defining the people, process, and metrics framework required to build and sustain enterprise AI competency at scale. This includes establishing program objectives, identifying ownership, and proposing a deployment model aligned to Nouryon’s broader digital strategy.

**End-to-End Process Management**

* Own the ISC End-to-End process architecture, defining process standards, documentation requirements, and governance for core ISC value streams.
* Drive process modeling and SIPOC-level design across ISC, working through the Process Modeler and Global Process Owner to ensure clarity of accountability and performance standards.
* Identify and close process design gaps that create risk, inefficiency, or measurement inconsistency across the ISC organization.

**Manufacturing Excellence**

* Define the Manufacturing Excellence framework for Nouryon, including OEE, TPM, reliability, and asset performance standards applied across the manufacturing network.
* Direct the Manufacturing Excellence Manager to develop and deploy site-level improvement programs, closing the loop between plant performance data and structured intervention.
* Integrate manufacturing excellence priorities into the broader OpEx roadmap, ensuring alignment with Digital Manufacturing, Palantir-enabled analytics, and capital investment decisions.

**People Leadership & COE Development**

* Lead a geographically distributed team of nine direct reports
* Define team structure, role clarity, and succession priorities for the COE
* Build a high-performance COE culture grounded in Nouryon’s Leadership Capability Framework

This role requires approximately 15–25% global travel across the Americas, Europe, and Asia Pacific.
  
  
**Key Performance Indicators**
The Global Director, Operational Excellence COE is measured against the same Breakthrough KPIs as the VP, Global Operational Excellence & Digital Manufacturing. This alignment is intentional – the COE’s organizational design, capability systems, and governance structures exist to enable these outcomes. Execution is driven through the regional OpEx Manager network; this role is accountable for building and sustaining the organization capable of delivering them.
  

* People Safety
* Process Safety
* FMC — Fixed Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* VMC — Variable Manufacturing Cost Productivity
* OEE — Overall Equipment Effectiveness
* OTIF — On-Time In-Full
* Quality Sigma Level
* CI Activation Rate

**We believe you bring**

* A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
* A minimum of 15 years of progressive experience in Operational Excellence, Continuous Improvement, or manufacturing leadership roles in a global, multi-site environment.
* Certified Master Black Belt (MBB) or Black Belt in Lean/Six Sigma, with demonstrated capability to design, govern, and quality-assure a full belt certification program.
* Proven track record of leading change management initiatives in large, matrixed, multi-regional organizations – with the ability to align diverse stakeholders and shift organizational culture.
* Deep knowledge of Manufacturing Excellence frameworks including OEE, TPM, and reliability methodologies, with experience deploying these at scale across a manufacturing network.
* Demonstrated people leadership across multiple geographies and organizational grades, including experience developing high-performing teams in a distributed structure.

**Great if you have**

* Experience in specialty chemicals, process manufacturing, or a similarly regulated, capital-intensive industrial environment.
* Hands-on expertise in End-to-End process design and governance, including SIPOC-level architecture and process ownership models.
* Experience designing and leading corporate Learning & Development programs, including competency frameworks and structured curricula for technical disciplines.
* Prior experience building or structuring a Center of Excellence from the ground up, including team design, governance models, and stakeholder alignment.
* Working proficiency with PowerBI or equivalent reporting platforms for program performance tracking and executive communication.

**We believe you are**
...
  
  
A systems thinker who sees the whole before diving into the parts. You lead through frameworks, not firefighting – you understand that durable operational excellence is built on governance, capability, and culture, not individual heroics. You bring intellectual rigor to every conversation and are comfortable challenging assumptions at any level of the organization, including in rooms where the answer is already assumed.
  
  
You are energized by building – building teams, building programs, building the conditions for others to succeed. You know how to hold standards without being rigid, and how to drive urgency without creating chaos. The right candidate is someone who finds genuine satisfaction in watching a global organization improve because of the systems they put in place – and who brings the patience, persistence, and precision that transformation at scale demands.
  
  
**We offer you**
This is a rare opportunity to architect and lead a newly consolidated global COE with a clear mandate from senior leadership, a defined team, and direct line of sight to enterprise value delivery. You will operate with significant autonomy, build the structure you believe is right, and leave a measurable legacy across a global manufacturing organization at an inflection point in its CI and digital transformation journey.
  
  
At Nouryon, we provide a great job and friendly coworkers, plus benefits in addition to salary.
