existing_roles.description:
**DIRECTOR OF OPERATIONS**

*Ritchey Livestock ID* | Fort Collins, Colorado | Full-Time, Onsite

Run the Operation. Build the Team. Shape What's Next.

**This Role Is For Builders.**

**We're looking for someone who can run a great operation today—and help build the company we'll become tomorrow.**

At Ritchey Livestock ID, we believe farmers and ranchers are the unsung heroes of our world. They work long hours, in every kind of weather, doing the essential work of feeding the rest of us. They don't ask for much in return. The least we can do is get our little part right.

For more than 60 years, we've manufactured livestock identification tags that ranchers can count on. Our products may be small, but the responsibility we feel to our customers is anything but.

We're a profitable, growing American manufacturer with a loyal nationwide customer base. We've recently completed the largest facility investment in our company's history, opening a new manufacturing operation in Fort Collins, Colorado. Now we're building the people, systems, and culture to carry Ritchey into its next chapter.

**We're looking for a hands-on Director of Operations who can lead that effort—and potentially grow into a broader executive leadership role as the company evolves.**

This is not a position for someone who wants to lead from behind a desk. You'll spend meaningful time on the production floor, working alongside your managers, solving real problems, and helping people succeed.

You'll also be expected to think beyond today's production schedule: developing leaders, building systems, improving performance, and preparing Ritchey for its next stage of growth.

**The Opportunity**

You'll lead approximately 45 people across manufacturing, engraving, shipping, and related operations, working directly with our CEO.

Your mission is twofold: **Run an exceptional operation today. Build the people, processes, and accountability that make excellence repeatable tomorrow.**

You'll own performance across safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, cost, and team development.

You'll be responsible for developing department managers, improving operational systems, driving continuous improvement, and building a culture where people take pride in their work and ownership of their results.

**Your First Year: Real Challenges, Real Opportunity**

We've made a major investment in our future. Now comes the work of making that investment pay off.

Here are five challenges you'll help us tackle:

* **Strengthen our new manufacturing operation.** Continue ramping up our Fort Collins facility, improving production stability, quality, capacity, and efficiency.
* **Improve scheduling and throughput.** Build better production planning and workflows across manufacturing, engraving, and shipping to improve delivery performance and reduce bottlenecks.
* **Build systems that last.** Reduce dependence on individual employees by developing practical SOPs, standardized processes, clear performance measures, and repeatable operating routines.
* **Develop our next generation of leaders.** Coach newer managers, strengthen accountability, and build employee development practices that help great people grow.
* **Drive continuous improvement.** Use Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, and practical root-cause problem-solving to reduce waste, improve productivity, and create measurable, sustainable improvements.

You'll have meaningful ownership of these challenges, the support of our leadership team, and the freedom to make a lasting impact.

**Who We're Looking For**

We're looking for a rare combination of heart, head, and hands. Someone who can lead people, build systems, solve problems, and roll up their sleeves when the work demands it.

**What you must bring:**

* **Proven People Leadership:** Demonstrated success leading teams in a manufacturing or production environment, ideally 20 or more employees, with experience developing supervisors or managers and holding people accountable.
* **Demonstrated Systems Building:** A track record of improving processes, implementing operational improvements, and building systems that continue to work without your constant involvement.
* **High Agency & Ownership:** The judgment, initiative, work ethic, and follow-through to take responsibility for results, solve difficult problems, and lead confidently in a hands-on environment.

**What we'd love to see:**

* Experience in plastic injection molding, extrusion, or related manufacturing processes.
* Practical experience applying Lean manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other structured continuous improvement methods. Certifications are valued but not required.
* Familiarity with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, purchasing, and quality systems.
* Strong financial and analytical skills, with an understanding of how operational decisions affect profitability.
* Experience developing managers, building teams, and helping an organization prepare for growth.

We value experience, but we're far more interested in what you've accomplished than the number of years on your résumé.

**Seasoned plastics professionals and exceptional leaders from other manufacturing environments are equally encouraged to apply.** What matters most is demonstrated leadership, systems thinking, operational judgment, and a willingness to keep learning.

***The Ritchey Way***

Our culture is built around one simple commitment: **DO RIGHT BY THE RANCH.**

Four core principles guide how we show up every day:

**ASK WHY. ASK WHAT IF.** — Learn the work. Make it better.

**MAKE THE SMALL THINGS COUNT.** — Bring care to the details, seen or unseen.

**NO SIDELINES.** — See it. Say it. Help solve it.

**BE GOOD TO WORK WITH.** — Carry your share. Be good company.

These aren't just words on a wall. They're the standards we hold ourselves and each other to. As our Director of Operations, you'll help bring *The Ritchey Way* to life through your leadership, your example, and the team you build.

**Why Ritchey?**

We're small enough that your ideas matter, but established and ambitious enough that your work can make a lasting difference. You'll have direct access to ownership, real authority to drive improvement, and a genuine opportunity to help shape the company's future.

**We're intentionally looking for someone with the potential to grow beyond operations.**

For the right individual who demonstrates exceptional leadership, business judgment, and results, this role could become a pathway toward broader company leadership, potentially including a future President or General Manager position.

That opportunity isn't guaranteed or tied to a timetable. It will be earned through performance, trust, and demonstrated ability to lead an increasingly complex business.

Most importantly, you'll be part of a team that takes pride in showing up every day for the farmers and ranchers who feed us.

**If you're a builder at heart, believe great people deserve great leadership, and want to create something you can be genuinely proud of, we'd love to meet you.**

**Location:** Fort Collins, Colorado — Full-Time, Onsite

**Compensation:** $130,000–$160,000 base salary, depending on experience and qualifications, plus performance-based bonus..

existing_roles.description:
OPPORTUNITY

Mammoth Biosciences is seeking a Director, Manufacturing Science and Technology (MSAT) to lead the scale-up of our lipid nanoparticle (LNP) drug product process from Phase 1 into Phase 2 and toward late stage readiness. This leader will own the technical path from the current clinical process to a well-characterized, scalable process that is ready for process performance qualification (PPQ).

All manufacturing and analytical work is performed at external contract development and manufacturing organizations (CDMOs) and contract testing labs. The Director will be Mammoth's technical owner of the process at those partners, ensuring that development, technology transfer, process characterization and PPQ are executed in line with current regulatory guidance and industry best practice.

This is a build role. Initially the Director will deliver through external resources (CDMOs, consultants and contract staff), then grow an internal MSAT team in stages as program milestones are met. The role reports to the Head of CMC and works closely with Process Development, Analytical Development, Quality, Regulatory CMC, Supply Chain and Program Management.

### **KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

Process scale-up and technology transfer

* Lead scale-up of the Phase 1 LNP process (nucleic acid payload formulation, mixing, buffer exchange/TFF, sterile filtration and fill) to Phase 2 and late-stage clinical scale
* Define the scale-up strategy, including equipment selection, mixing platform scalability, scale-down model development and comparability between process versions
* Plan and execute technology transfers of processes and methods between Mammoth, development partners and GMP CDMOs, including transfer protocols, gap assessments and engineering runs
* Own the technical risk assessments (e.g., FMEA) that drive scale-up and characterization priorities

Process characterization and PPQ readiness

* Build the control strategy using a QbD approach: define CQAs and CPPs, link material attributes to product quality, and set proven acceptable ranges
* Design and oversee process characterization studies (DoE, qualified scale-down models, hold times, mixing and filtration studies) that support the control strategy and regulatory filings
* Lead PPQ planning and execution: validation master plan inputs, PPQ protocols and reports, acceptance criteria, sampling plans and the transition to continued process verification
* Partner with Analytical Development to make sure methods are phase-appropriate, validated on time and fit to support characterization and PPQ

External manufacturing and CDMO management

* Serve as Mammoth's technical lead and person-in-plant at CDMOs and contract labs for development, engineering and GMP campaigns
* Lead selection, qualification and oversight of CDMO partners for drug product manufacturing, fill-finish operations and drug product testing, including technical due diligence, capacity and capability assessment, and scale-up fit
* Provide technical oversight for engineering and GMP runs at external partners
* Develop scalable, phase-appropriate aseptic drug product processes at CDMOs, including fill-finish operations, cryogenic handling (as applicable) and cold-chain compatibility
* Assess and implement suitable container-closure systems (vials, syringes) that meet regulatory and operational requirements
* Accountable for review and approval of batch records in accordance with regulatory guidelines; review campaign plans, deviations, investigations, CAPAs and change controls in partnership with Quality
* Manage partner timelines, budgets, deliverables and quality in collaboration with internal stakeholders; drive technical decisions and escalate issues early
* Project manage external stakeholders and high-profile partner meetings (up to 10% of time)
* Contribute to technical sections of quality agreements, statements of work and budgets

Regulatory and cross-functional support

* Author and review CMC sections for IND/IMPD/CTA amendments, end-of-Phase 2 and later filings (Module 3 process description, process development history, process validation)
* Support regulatory interactions and inspections with process knowledge and data
* Provide manufacturing input to program plans, timelines and supply forecasts

Team and resource leadership

* In the early phase, deliver through external resources: CDMO technical teams, consultants and contract MSAT staff
* Build the internal MSAT function in stages tied to milestones, including hiring plans, roles and the balance of internal and outsourced work
* Set up MSAT systems and practices: tech transfer templates, process knowledge management, data trending and lifecycle documentation

### **REEQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* PhD in chemical engineering, pharmaceutical sciences, chemistry or a related field with 10+ years of industry experience, or MS with 14+ or BS with 16+ years of experience
* 6+ years in MSAT, process development or technical operations for parenteral drug products, including at least 3 years in a leadership role
* Hands-on experience scaling up LNP or comparable complex parenteral processes (liposomes, nanoparticles, nucleic acid formulations) from early clinical to late-stage scale
* Led at least one process characterization and PPQ campaign through completion, with working command of ICH Q8–Q12 and FDA/EMA process validation expectations
* Extensive experience managing CDMOs and contract labs as the sponsor's technical lead, including tech transfer, person-in-plant oversight, deviations and change control
* Experience with fill-finish operations, aseptic processing and external manufacturing oversight
* Strong working knowledge of cryogenic storage and cold-chain management for LNP drug products
* Track record of authoring CMC regulatory sections and supporting agency interactions
* Ability to influence and direct external partners without line authority, and to make sound technical calls under timeline pressure
* Ability for frequent domestic and international travel to CDMO and contract lab sites, estimated at up to [30–40]% and peaking during engineering, characterization and PPQ campaigns
* Must be able to travel internationally on short notice and hold, or be able to obtain, a valid passport and any visas needed for partner sites
* Ability to commit to extended on-site presence at CDMOs (person-in-plant) during critical campaigns, sometimes across time zones.
* Based in the San Francisco Bay Area preferred, with ability to work onsite at our Brisbane, CA location; hybrid or remote arrangements are available
* Ability to work Pacific Time Zone hours if not located on the West Coast
* Ability to travel to Mammoth’s Brisbane, CA HQ regularly if not local

### **PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Direct experience with mRNA/LNP or gene editing drug products
* Experience with impingement jet or microfluidic mixing scale-up, TFF and sterile filtration of LNPs
* Experience with commercial process validation and BLA/MAA preparation
* Experience building a function or team from the ground up in a small or mid-size biotech
* Working knowledge of statistical tools for DoE and process data analysis (e.g., JMP, Minitab)

### **BENEFITS**

* Company-paid health/vision/dental benefits
* Unlimited vacation and generous sick time
* Company-sponsored meals and snacks
* Wellness, caregiver and ergonomics benefits
* 401(k) with company matching

Actual base salary will be determined by relevant professional experience, applicable skills, and internal equity

**COMPANY**

Mammoth Biosciences is a biotechnology company focused on leveraging its proprietary ultracompact CRISPR systems to develop long-term curative therapies, as well as other applications such as decentralized precision diagnostics. Founded by CRISPR pioneer and Nobel laureate Jennifer Doudna and Trevor Martin, Janice Chen, and Lucas Harrington, the company’s ultracompact proteins are designed to enable *in vivo* gene editing in difficult to reach tissues utilizing both nuclease applications and new editing modalities beyond double stranded breaks, including base editing, gene writing, and epigenetic editing. The company is building out its pipeline of potential *in vivo* gene editing therapeutics and capabilities and has partnerships with leading pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies to broaden the reach of its innovative and proprietary technology. Mammoth’s deep science and industry experience, along with a robust and differentiated intellectual property portfolio, have enabled the company to further its mission to transform the lives of patients and deliver on the full promise of CRISPR technologies.

This policy covers all facets of employment including, but not limited to: recruitment, selection, placement, promotions, transfers, demotions, terminations, training, and compensation.

**Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality**

**Location:** Lakewood, Ohio  
**Company:** Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company  
**Employment Type:** Full Time  
**Reports To:** President

**About Ferry Cap**

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is a long-established American manufacturer of engineered fasteners and specialty metal components serving demanding industrial and power generation applications. As we invest in our people, equipment, and operating systems, we are seeking a senior quality leader who can help strengthen our processes and build a companywide culture of quality.

**Position Summary**

The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will lead Ferry Cap’s quality organization and serve as a key member of the company’s leadership team.

This is a hands on leadership position for someone with strong experience in metallurgy, metal transformation, manufacturing processes, and heat treatment. The successful candidate will work closely with operations, engineering, maintenance, supply chain, and customers to improve process control, solve technical problems, and ensure consistent product quality.

The right leader will view quality as an operating partnership, not simply an inspection function. This individual must be comfortable working on the production floor, engaging directly with employees, and helping build quality into every stage of the manufacturing process.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Lead all quality assurance, quality control, laboratory, inspection, and quality systems activities.
* Partner directly with operations to establish a culture in which safety, delivery, quality, and cost are shared responsibilities.
* Provide technical leadership related to metallurgy, raw materials, metal forming, metal transformation, machining, threading, and heat treatment.
* Oversee metallurgical testing and analysis, including hardness, microstructure, case depth, decarburization, mechanical properties, material certification, and failure analysis.
* Evaluate and improve heat treatment processes, including furnace controls, quenching, tempering, process consistency, and product conformance.
* Strengthen incoming, in process, and final inspection systems to ensure product requirements are consistently achieved.
* Lead root cause analysis and corrective action activities involving internal defects, customer complaints, supplier issues, and process failures.
* Use structured problem solving methods such as 8D, 5 Why, fishbone analysis, PFMEA, control plans, SPC, and MSA.
* Maintain and continuously improve the company’s quality management system, documentation, procedures, work instructions, and audit processes.
* Ensure compliance with customer requirements, industry standards, specifications, and applicable regulatory requirements.
* Lead customer audits, supplier audits, internal audits, and customer quality reviews.
* Build strong working relationships with customer quality and engineering teams.
* Develop meaningful quality metrics, including first pass yield, scrap, rework, cost of poor quality, customer complaints, corrective action effectiveness, and supplier performance.
* Improve material traceability and process control throughout the manufacturing operation.
* Lead supplier quality development and ensure purchased materials and outside processes meet Ferry Cap requirements.
* Develop, coach, and hold accountable the quality team while strengthening quality knowledge throughout the organization.
* Support new product introduction, process changes, capital projects, and continuous improvement initiatives.
* Establish clear containment, escalation, and corrective action processes when quality concerns arise.

**Required Qualifications**

* Significant quality leadership experience in a metal manufacturing environment.
* Strong practical knowledge of metallurgy, material properties, metal transformation, and heat treatment.
* Experience with manufacturing processes such as cold forming, forging, machining, threading, rolling, or similar metalworking operations.
* Demonstrated ability to diagnose metallurgical and manufacturing process failures.
* Experience leading quality systems, customer audits, corrective actions, and continuous improvement activities.
* Strong working knowledge of dimensional inspection, mechanical testing, metallurgical testing, calibration, and measurement systems.
* Experience using quality tools such as PFMEA, control plans, SPC, MSA, 8D, and root cause analysis.
* Proven ability to work collaboratively with operations and engineering teams.
* Strong leadership, communication, organization, and problem solving skills.
* Willingness to spend significant time on the manufacturing floor and become personally involved in resolving issues.
* Bachelor’s degree in metallurgy, materials science, engineering, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant manufacturing experience.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Ten or more years of progressive quality experience, including at least five years in a leadership role.
* Experience with engineered fasteners, high strength components, critical industrial products, or power generation applications.
* Experience with ISO based quality management systems and customer specific quality requirements.
* Experience working with commercial heat treat suppliers and internal heat treatment operations.
* ASQ certification, Six Sigma certification, or formal Lean manufacturing training.
* Experience working in a union manufacturing environment.

**Leadership Profile**

The successful candidate will be:

* Hands on and comfortable working directly with production employees.
* Collaborative and capable of building trust across departments.
* Technically strong, practical, and decisive.
* Focused on preventing defects instead of relying on inspection to find them.
* Comfortable challenging existing practices while respecting Ferry Cap’s people and history.
* Able to balance customer requirements with operational realities.
* Committed to accountability, continuous improvement, and developing others.

**Why Join Ferry Cap**

This position offers the opportunity to play a major role in the continued transformation and growth of a historic American manufacturing company. The Senior Quality Manager / Director of Quality will have direct access to company leadership, meaningful influence over operations, and the opportunity to build a quality culture that supports Ferry Cap’s customers, employees, and long term success.

Ferry Cap & Set Screw Company is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.

***Ready to lead a function, not just a shift? This is your next step.***

American Armor Gloves makes high-quality nitrile gloves here at home in South Carolina. Healthcare workers, first responders, and essential workers across the country rely on what we build. Our purpose is simple: **We strengthen America by building quality protection at home.**

We're a lean, growing manufacturer scaling toward 320–350 people, and we've spent the past year building the foundation for that growth: a redesigned organization, a clear vision with quarterly milestones, defined leadership roles, and a new leadership and compensation architecture. Manufacturing is the heart of that growth, and we need a leader ready to own it.

**THE OPPORTUNITY**

The Director of Manufacturing is one of the most essential roles in our company. You'll own the end-to-end performance of our Manufacturing department, turning business plans into consistent, safe, high-quality production results.

This role is built for an accomplished Manufacturing Manager who is ready to take the next step. You've proven you can run a strong operation. Now you're ready to **lead through systems and leaders rather than personal effort on the floor**, and to build a manufacturing function that performs at a high level no matter which team is on shift.

Reporting to our VP of Operations, you'll be the bridge between enterprise strategy and shift-by-shift execution. You'll set the systems, build the leaders, and own the results.

**WHAT YOU'LL DO**

* **Own manufacturing performance.** Deliver results across safety, quality, OEE, throughput, schedule attainment, labor productivity, scrap, and downtime through accountable leaders and strong systems.

* **Build repeatable production systems.** Design shift handoffs, accountability routines, labor deployment standards, and scheduling so performance never depends on heroics.

* **Lead and develop your Shift Manager team.** Coach your Shift Managers as leaders, not only as production operators, and build the next generation of manufacturing leadership.

* **Integrate compounding and batching.** Keep material availability, formulation compliance, and production demand aligned and well governed.

* **Drive continuous improvement.** Lead projects that reduce waste, improve workflow, raise OEE, and close performance gaps, in partnership with Process Engineering.

* **Partner across the business.** Work side by side with Quality, Process Engineering, Maintenance, Logistics, and People & Culture to remove barriers to production.

* **Build workforce capability.** Own training plans, manufacturing career pathways, and engagement so our workforce is ready to support growth.

**WHAT YOU'LL OWN**

You'll set daily and weekly production priorities, deploy labor across shifts, manage Shift Manager performance, and direct improvement projects within manufacturing. You'll shape manufacturing KPI targets, capacity planning, equipment needs, and staffing structure through your recommendations to the VP of Operations. You'll lead Shift Managers, Production Planning, and Batching/Compounding leadership, with a frontline team of Production Supervisors and Manufacturing Associates across multiple shifts.

**A REAL CAREER PATHWAY**

We grow leaders deliberately, and this role is designed as a launch point, not a ceiling. Our leadership framework defines exactly what it takes to grow from functional leadership into executive leadership, and we invest in getting high performers there.

* **Where you go next.** The Director of Manufacturing is a direct pathway to VP of Operations or other senior operations leadership, based on demonstrated enterprise judgment, cross-functional partnership, and the strength of the leadership bench you build.

* **How you get there.** Expect direct mentoring from the VP of Operations, exposure to enterprise planning and capital decisions, cross-functional visibility, and formal leadership development.

* **A clear standard.** Your growth is measured against the same competency framework used for job descriptions, performance reviews, and succession planning, so you always know where you stand and what comes next.

* **Visibility at the top.** Our annual bench-strength review puts strong leaders on the executive team’s radar early.

**WHY THIS ROLE, WHY NOW**

* **Essential to the mission.** Every glove we ship runs through the function you lead.

* **Build, not just run.** Our organization is lean and still forming, so you'll shape systems and standards that scale with the business.

* **A clear operating rhythm.** A shared vision, quarterly milestones, and a common scorecard keep leaders aligned and connect your work to company priorities.

* **Leave a legacy.** You'll develop Shift Managers into future Directors and Supervisors into future Shift Managers, building a team that carries the company forward.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Industrial Technology, Business, or a related field, or equivalent progressive leadership experience

* 8–10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership in a high-volume environment

* Proven success leading multiple shifts and developing frontline leaders

* A track record of owning department performance through KPIs, systems, and accountable leadership

* Strong cross-functional partnership with Quality, Engineering, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and HR

* Solid knowledge of OSHA safety requirements and manufacturing quality systems

* Proficiency with Microsoft Office, ERP/MRP systems (NetSuite preferred), KPI dashboards, production scheduling, and QMS

**Bonus points for:** experience in medical device, PPE, chemical processing, or FDA-regulated manufacturing; Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement practice; ERP implementation; and leading through growth and scale.

**HOW YOU LEAD**

You lead safely, every shift, not only when incidents happen. You hold leaders accountable through systems, not by stepping in for them. When something breaks, you fix the system, not just the shift. You raise problems early and directly. You treat Quality, Engineering, and Maintenance as partners, and you understand how manufacturing affects the entire business.

**READY FOR YOUR NEXT STEP?**

If you're a Manufacturing Manager ready to own a function, build leaders, and grow into enterprise leadership with a company that's scaling with purpose, we'd like to hear from you. Apply today.

*American Armor Gloves is an equal employment opportunity employer and does not discriminate against employees or job applicants on the basis of race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, age, national origin, mental or physical disability of a qualified individual, veteran or military status, pregnancy, marital status, familial status, genetic information, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state or local law.*

At El Pollo Loco, we are on a mission to be the nation’s leading fire-grilled chicken restaurant. When it comes to our people, we are all about growth. In fact, we see you as our secret ingredient. While our chicken is fire, it’s our people who set us ablaze.
  
  
Our restaurants are only the tip of the flame! If you’re looking for an innovative, winning, and welcoming workplace, then a flamin’ good career in our Restaurant Support Center is right for you.
  
  
At our Support Center, we believe our best work is done Together, when departments collaborate and everyone is confident in contributing their ideas. This is why we are in the office 3 days per week.
  
  
Let’s Get Loco!
  
  
What’s in it for you!
  
  

* STRONG office culture recognized as a Great Place to Work® and driven by our core values: Simple. Together. Relentless. Ownership. Nimble. Growth
* Career growth opportunities
* Competitive pay and bonus potential
* Be an Owner: Equity Compensation
* Medical + Dental + Vision Insurance + HSA Savings Account
* 401(K) Retirement Plan with company match and immediate vesting
* Paid Vacation + Sick Pay + 12 Paid Holidays
* Employee Assistance Program
* Free El Pollo Loco food + restaurant discounts
* PerkSpot discounts program

**POSITION PURPOSE:**  
The Regional Director of Operations is responsible for driving El Pollo Loco’s success in the Los Angeles, CA region. They are responsible for providing operational expertise, strategic leadership and coaching. Directs, leads, manages and analyzes all aspects of the restaurant operations for the Areas under their direction to ensure achievement and maintenance of the regional sales, budgetary targets, controllable profit, performance metrics (e.g., service, quality, cleanliness, etc.), brand integrity, and compliance standards (e.g., food and restaurant safety, federal/state/local labor laws, etc.). Implements and executes strategic and tactical operational initiatives that support future business growth strategies. Oversees and manages adequate resource availability for existing and new restaurant openings including the attraction, retention, training, development and coaching of a high performing management team.
  
  
**ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**  

* Oversees all aspects of the region’s restaurant business, operations, and facilities. Directs and aligns company strategies with restaurant management activities.
* Utilizes reporting systems to determine trends in sales, cost of goods and guest services. Reviews, monitors and manages the financial progress of the individual restaurants and region, including food and labor costs, ensuring budgeted targets are achieved.
* Meets regularly with Area Leaders to coach, develop, train and review performance, share best practices and disseminate information on any areas where there is an opportunity for improvement (e.g., P&L, RCP, FSA, QSC, Mystery Shops, etc.). Develops action plans with Area Leaders to improve revenue, profitability and quality/service standards.
* Directs, manages and ensures the region’s successful and timely implementation of all marketing strategies and LTOs. Supports and inspects marketing strategies in building guest counts and sales.
* Provides effective and timely resolution to all guest and employee complaints, conflicts and employee relations that cannot be resolved at the Area Leader level.
* Ensures the region’s restaurants are in compliance with all local, regional, and national laws and have all the required documentation and paperwork.
* Leverages two-way communication with Field and Support Center employees. Represents the Operations perspective on prioritization, planning and promotions to inspire operational excellence, effective implementation and facilitate insights. Provides specific operational input and feedback into the development of new products and programs to ensure successful execution.
* Collaborates with Development, Human Resources, and Operations in the coordination and execution of new restaurant openings. Directs team selection, monitors the training and ensures the teams perform to El Pollo Loco’s standards. Participates in the local public relations support in all locations. Approves employee relocation within region ensuring moves are conducted in the most economical and efficient manner.
* Develops regional succession plans: evaluates open opportunities, assesses internal talent, oversees management training programs, and drives recruiting efforts to ensure adequate number of managers are available to sustain growth of the organization.
* Champions effective vertical and horizontal communications within the regional area including Company-wide news of interest, upcoming events, new facilities, promotions, product developments, “Best Practices” among peers, etc. Prepares thoroughly and delivers well-organized, dynamic and informative presentations to senior management as needed. Holds meetings with their respective teams on a regular basis to ensure fluid and consistent messaging.
* Creates and fosters a positive team environment through recognizing and reinforcing behaviors and results that are aligned with El Pollo Loco’s core values and culture. Ensures open channels for employee suggestions.
* Interacts professionally and ethically, constructively participating as a collaborative team leader in pursuit of common goals, including active attendance to meetings. Initiates cost-effective suggestions to improve operational procedures.
* Other activities, duties or responsibilities that are assigned by your supervisor.

QUALIFICATIONS – EDUCATION, EXPERIENCE, LICENSE/CERTIFICATIONS:
  
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to satisfactorily perform the essential functions of the job. Reasonable accommodation will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the job. The requirements listed below are representative of the education and/or experience required.
  
  
**Education/Work Experience:**  
High school diploma or equivalent (GED) required, BA/BS degree in Business Administration preferred. 8+ years QSR/multi-site restaurant experience as an Area Leader or District Manager required; 5+ years regional QSR management experience preferred; 3+ years El Pollo Loco experience preferred; and a track record of success in leading, managing, coaching and developing high performance teams.
  
  
**License/Certifications:**  
Current valid driver’s license required as frequent weekly travel is involved. Current ServSafe certification preferred.
  
  
**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**  

* Experience with successfully recruiting, building, and developing a team (based on current and future needs).
* Confidence in execution of strategic initiatives.
* Must be decisive and able to make fact-based decisions.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving mindset and skills; meticulous attention to detail
* Ability to effectively communicate with internal and external business partners.
* Ability to prioritize and plan work assignments and work under pressure of frequent and tight deadlines.
* Ability to read, write, and interpret complex reports, documents, and correspondence.
* Adept at managing and prioritizing competing time sensitive requests while working well in a team atmosphere that may be under pressure.
* Ability to exercise independent judgment on matters of significance to the company.
* Ability to work weekends and extended work schedules as needed.
* Must be willing and able to travel locally within Southern California and to out-of-state restaurant locations, as needed by car or airplane.

Our Company
  
  
In 1980 the first American El Pollo Loco opened on Alvarado Street in Los Angeles, quickly becoming a destination for the best citrus-marinated, fire-grilled pollo in town. Over the past four decades, El Pollo Loco has grown into more than 500 restaurants across 9 states, becoming an L.A. mainstay and cultural benchmark along the way. And today, we continue to work just as hard to always provide customers with fresh and innovative L.A. Mex from our famous family dinners to Mexican entrees.
  
  
The pay range identified is the hourly or salary rate El Pollo Loco expects to pay for the posted position. This range does not include any benefits or bonus opportunities that might be available for the position based on position and eligibility criteria. Individual pay will vary based on a variety of factors including years of experience, industry experience, education, geography, etc.

protected_roles.description:
**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

**Position Summary**
The Director, Quality is responsible for leading multiple manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality resources in the execution of the overall STERIS Quality System. This position is principally responsible for manufacturing/service site or functional quality system execution to drive product/service quality improvement and ensure compliance with, as appropriate, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, MDSAP, FDA QMSR CFR Part 820/211, EU MDR, and other applicable standards. Supporting the GI Reprocessing business, this role provides quality leadership for products, processes, and services that help healthcare providers safely clean, disinfect, and reprocess gastrointestinal endoscopes and related equipment. The Director will champion a culture of quality, compliance, and continuous improvement, helping ensure the delivery of safe, effective, and reliable solutions that support infection prevention, patient safety, and customer confidence. The Quality Director will lead teams of quality managers and engineers responsible for product and service quality, supplier quality, new product/service support, continuous improvement initiatives, and quality system execution. This leader will partner closely with Operations, Engineering, Regulatory Affairs, and Commercial teams to drive operational excellence, mitigate risk, support innovation, and enhance quality performance across the GI Reprocessing portfolio.
  
  
Preferred onsite location: Mentor, OH, with consideration for candidates based in Plymouth, MN or Conroe, TX.
  
  
**What You’ll Do As a Director Quality**

* The Director, Quality will have responsibility for the following: Leads manufacturing/service sites and/or corporate quality staff in the execution and continuous improvement of the STERIS Quality System. Operates with a focus on the following objectives:

+ Ensures site level compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
+ Drives strategies and methods to continuously improve capital, consumable and service product quality performance.
+ Establishes clear and consistent quality measurement systems in order to monitor and drive results.
+ Leads quality planning and the execution of assigned New Product/Service Development (NPD) projects to achieve targeted quality deliverable adherence.
+ Drives targeted supplier quality improvement efforts and oversees supplier evaluation, approval, and control for assigned manufacturing sites.
+ Assists in the continuous improvement and standardization of quality system procedures and monitor effectiveness.
+ Supports the reliability function by integrating design for reliability tools and techniques within the local projects.
+ Leads quality planning efforts through cross-functional teaming at a site level.

* Supports the New Product/Service Development process and projects to ensure projects attain cost, quality, and delivery objectives.
* Directs local staff on planning sequential and concurrent quality activities. Establish planning and monitoring tools and techniques.
* Provides Quality viewpoints and opinions in planning and specifying existing and future products.
* Assists in the development of the Quality budget. Helps to ensures resources are adequate to fully support the Quality System.
* Takes ownership of all local quality issues, projects, and development activities. Works closely with the site’s Senior Management Teams to provide strategic direction and development of the manufacturing sites product quality strategies and tactics.
* Manages and provide direction to a teams of quality professionals both at corporate and manufacturing sites, with responsibility for hiring, performance management, appropriate staffing, and deployment of resources.
* Assures that local sites maintain and improve operational and quality systems to remain in a state of compliance to appropriate ISO, FDA, and other applicable regulatory standards.
* Works closely with the regulatory function to ensure compliance to appropriate ISO and FDA standards; plans for and assists in the management of external audits.
* Leads manufacturing and service site quality teams to ensure alignment to operations, support of Lean efforts and drive quality improvement performance for products, services, and processes across the sites.
* This individual has autonomy to perform the duties of Person Responsible for Regulatory Compliance (PRRC) on behalf of STERIS legal manufacturing entities under the EU MDR. This individual shall suffer no disadvantage within the organization in relation to proper fulfilment of his or her duties in lieu of article 15 of the EU MDR.

**Required**
**The Experience, Skills, and Abilities Needed**

* Bachelor’s Degree (Engineering or related technical field)
* Minimum 10 years of experience with increased responsibility leading quality system and product quality improvement efforts. Exceptional leadership manifested through organizing and motivating teams toward their respective goals by employing hands-on management.
* Must fulfil the experience requirements listed in Article 15 of the EUMDR (PRRC).
* A solid quality foundation indicated by a demonstrated understanding of Lean/Six Sigma, quality system, and product/process improvement methodologies.
* Solid business acumen and proven ability to build and lead process and product improvement strategies and results.
* Strong expertise in analytical methods, quality systems, and continuous improvement methods.
* Excellent interpersonal, as well as verbal and written communication skills in order to develop and maintain rapport and effective internal and external relationships to support business success.
* The ability to work hard and deliver results under pressure, as well as the willingness to address and shift priorities in rapidly changing markets.

**Preferred**

* Advanced degree.
* Experience with statistical analysis software and Visio.
* Experience in medical device industry.

**Other**

* Excellent problem-solving skills.
* Focus on identification of potential issues and continuous improvement.
* Experience working on cross-functional teams and on own initiative.
* Demonstrated excellent organizational, oral, and written communications skills.
* Must have PC experience, as well as working familiarity of desktop applications including Excel, Word, and PowerPoint.

**What STERIS Offers**
We value our employees and are committed to providing a comprehensive benefits package that supports your health, well-being, and financial future.
  
  
**Here Is a Brief Overview Of What We Offer**

* Market competitive pay
* Extensive paid time off and (9) added holidays
* Excellent healthcare, dental, and vision benefits
* Long/short term disability coverage
* 401(K) with company match
* Maternity and parental leave
* Additional add on benefits/discounts for programs such as pet insurance
* Tuition reimbursement and continued educational programs
* Excellent opportunities for advancement in a stable long-term career

Pay range for this opportunity is $144,500.00 - $187,000.00. This position is eligible for bonus participation.
  
  
Minimum pay rates offered will comply with county/city minimums, if higher than range listed. Pay rates are based on a number of factors, including but not limited to local labor market costs, years of relevant experience, education, professional certifications, foreign language fluency, etc.

WE HELP OUR CUSTOMERS CREATE A HEALTHIER AND SAFER WORLD by providing innovative healthcare and life sciences products and services around the globe. For more information, visit www.steris.com.

Saluda Medical is a commercial‑stage medical device company focused on developing treatments for chronic neurological conditions using its novel closed‑loop neuromodulation platform. The company’s proprietary technology senses and measures neural responses to stimulation and automatically adjusts therapy based on real‑time neurophysiological feedback.
  
  
Saluda Medical’s first product, the Evoke® System, is designed to deliver known, consistent, and personalized spinal cord stimulation therapy by objectively measuring neural responses and maintaining therapy within a prescribed therapeutic window. Saluda Medical is headquartered in Minneapolis, Minnesota.
  
  
At Saluda, we challenge boundaries. We innovate and think beyond the conventional. Our focus is to revolutionize the standard of care in neuromodulation to positively impact patient’s lives.
  
  
The Quality Director reports to the VP QA and is responsible for managing the company’s quality activities at the Bloomington, Minnesota site.
  
  
What You’ll Do:
  
  

* Manage all quality control (QC) activities, to include receiving inspection and product release from the site.
* Manage all quality assurance activities in the distribution facility, to include non-conformance reports (NCR) and supplier quality for our contract manufactured and OEM acquired products.
* Ensure activities performed in the facility are compliant to global regulatory requirements for which we claim compliance, as well as Saluda business expectations.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, be a vocal advocate for a strong culture of quality and compliance at the site.
* Build strong working relationships with other cross-functional leadership at the site to include Supply Chain, Distribution & Customer Service, Clinical, Sustaining Engineering, and Regulatory Affairs.
* In partnership with the head of US Distribution and Customer Service, ensure products distributed from the facility are handled appropriately and distributed to customers accurately and in a timely manner.
* Provide direct leadership to inspectors, technicians, quality specialists and engineers utilizing an inclusive and empowering leadership approach.
* Manage distribution, contract manufacturing and OEM-related quality challenges as they arise.
* Develop and ensure the implementation of a site inspection readiness plan.
* Participate internal and external audits to ensure the site’s quality system is effective.
* Manage and lead quality improvement projects in all areas of responsibility.
* Organize Supplier Change Assessment Board meetings and ensure submitted change request has the required information for the Change Assessment Board.

What You’ll Bring:
  
  

* Bachelor of Science degree or higher in a life sciences or engineering discipline
* At least 5+ years of experience in medical device quality with 2+ years of leadership experience.
* Proven ability to execute and maintain quality systems, with direct experience in post-market quality, distribution quality, or supplier quality.
* Strong relationship builder and communicator with diverse work teams
* Experience building strong relationships with global colleagues.
* Ability to work on-site 4+ days a week.
* Prior experience with returned product analysis and oversight of U.S.
* FDA 21 CFR Part 806 reporting obligations.

Our Core Values:
  
  

* People – Our first responsibility is to the patients we serve.
* Integrity – Do the right thing
* Pioneering – Lead Boldly, Change Lives, Disrupt the Status-Quo
* Performance – Win together – Deliver with Excellence.

*Saluda Medical embraces diversity and equal opportunity. We are committed to building a team representative of a variety of backgrounds, perspectives and skills. We believe people are the source of our inspiration and innovation.*

protected_roles.description:
General Summary
  
  
The Global Director of Quality is responsible for oversight of Quality Management and Continuous Improvement Programs for Team Industrial Services globally. The position is ultimately responsible for all corporate and Divisional Quality and Continuous support personnel. The successful candidate provides the necessary management and oversight to ensure the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of TEAM’s Quality Management System (QMS) as well as the supplemental Quality Control and Technical programs. Position is responsible for managing and coordinating all Quality support activities relating to the execution of the Quality Management System (QMS) for Team Corporate, Product and Service Line, Engineering and Manufacturing, and Operations. Global Director of Quality is responsible for operating on a cost-effective basis within the framework of company approved policies, objectives, and budgets.
  
  
**Essential Job Functions**

* Maintains a safe, secure and healthy environment by adhering to Company/Customer safety and quality standards and practices and to legal regulations, alerting others regarding potential hazards or concern
* Adheres to and is a champion of TEAM’s Core Values
* Establish a continuous improvement culture across the enterprise utilizing known methods and concepts such as Lean, Six Sigma, FMEA, Kaizen, Poka-yoke, CAPA, 8D, etc.
* Maintains contact with district, division and corporate levels to promote and instill a “Quality Culture” throughout the organization.
* Ensure TEAMs QMS is globally consistent and regionally precise based on local requirements.
* When necessary, provide training to affected personnel, including customers, to obtain maximum process efficiency, productivity, cooperation, and morale.
* Leads the Enterprise management review to evaluate quality objectives, assess the adequacy and effectiveness and continuing suitability of the existing QMS and identify opportunities for improvement.
* Manage the Supplier Quality Management program and supports third-party and Customer assessments.
* Ensures company-wide targets and objectives are established and action plans are developed and tracked to achieve them.
* Development and implementation of performance monitoring and measurement system of leading and lagging KPIs to evaluate performance across the entire supply chain – Supplier – Order Intake - Engineering – Manufacturing – Installation – Service – Warranty.
* Development and implementation of system of associating and tracking non-conformances with costs for supplier claims, internal issues and customer escapes. This includes understanding the company’s Cost of Poor Quality and Non-Conformance Costs.
* Stay up-to-date on industry trends, including Quality-related initiatives.
* Develops medium to long-term operating strategies and recommendations for plans and programs for increasing TEAM’s Quality performance.
* Prepare capital expense and operating budgets and ensure cost-effective departmental operations.
* Support sales efforts when necessary, including the completion of pre-qualification surveys and submission of controlled quality documents to customer representatives.
* Have a general understanding of all company products and services that are available to our customers, and how TEAM’s Quality program applies to these areas.
* Ensures the Enterprise external certifications (ISO-9001, Nuclear, Aerospace, etc.) are maintained.
* Other duties as assigned

**Job Qualifications**

* Requires a bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field. Master’s degree preferred. Continuous Improvement Methodology certifications such as Six Sigma is preferred.
* Experience in Oil and Gas, Lean Manufacturing, Petrochemical, or a Field Service Industry is a must.
* 15 years’ experience in Quality or Operational Excellence related function.
* Experience with problem solving methods such as A3, FMEA, etc. preferred.
* Experience in introducing/implementing a solid warranty tracking system that captures accurate Customer and or Field related issues.

As
**Quality Director**
, you will lead the Global & NA Institutional Quality Pillar within Ecolab's future-state Global Quality organization, setting and sustaining the standards that govern product quality across the manufacturing, warehousing and distribution network. You will be responsible for building a best-in-class quality function focused on product safety, regulatory compliance, continuous improvement and a superior customer experience. Reporting to the Vice President, Global Quality, you will have primary responsibility for the North America quality management system, supplier and contract manufacturer quality, and customer complaint resolution. You will partner closely with Central Quality, Global Supplier Quality, business-aligned Quality pillars, Supply Chain, Commercial, RD&E, manufacturing, suppliers, third-party manufacturers and regulatory bodies to establish clear accountability, consistent standards, timely escalation and shared learning across the enterprise. Innovation and data-driven decision-making will be essential to activating the future-state operating model, strengthening local execution and continually increasing the value Quality delivers to the business and customers.
  
  
**What You Will Do**

* Own the North America quality strategy and roadmap, aligning regional priorities with the global quality agenda and future-state Global Quality operating model while driving synergies across the function
* Provide leadership and vision to the NA quality team across manufacturing plants, warehouses, and contract manufacturing partners, developing both people and technology to elevate overall performance
* Own and continuously improve the quality management system, ensuring readiness for internal, customer, regulatory and third-party audits
* Ensure compliance with FDA, EPA, ISO 9001 and other applicable regulatory and customer requirements across all North America sites
* Own the NA quality budget and cost of poor quality, including target setting for divisions
* Drive reduction in customer complaints, non-conformances and rework through structured root cause analysis and disciplined corrective and preventive action
* Establish quality metrics and reporting, using data and analytics to identify trends and direct resources to the highest-impact issues
* Partner with RD&E and the divisions on new product introductions, formula changes and specification management so that quality is designed in from the start
* Partner with the supplier and contract manufacturing teams to establish strong quality programs, including qualification, performance monitoring, audits and corrective action
* Direct the investigation and resolution of significant quality events, including product holds, recalls and customer escalations
* Build strong, trust-based relationships with commercial leaders to constantly drive improvements and efficiencies across the supply chain
* Drive standardization of quality processes across the network while implementing operational excellence and continuous improvement initiatives
* Protect Ecolab's brand by ensuring compliance with legal and regulatory requirements, and promoting environmental responsibility
* Activate the future-state Global Quality operating model across North America by clarifying decision rights, governance, interfaces, support channels and escalation paths while keeping Quality closely connected to sites, businesses and customers
* Build a connected One Quality culture by applying common standards and metrics, sharing expertise and learning across Quality pillars, and strengthening early risk visibility and consistent execution across the network

protected_roles.description:
Elevate is committed to providing the highest quality commercial roofing, wall and lining systems to solve our customers’ challenges, grounded by a 45-year legacy of proven experience. Our mission is to deliver solutions that save time, perform reliably and protect our communities. We are devoted to building partnerships rooted in trust in reflection of our Elevate promise that Nobody Covers You Better™.
  
  
Elevate is part of the Amrize family of brands. Visit ElevateCommercialBP.com to learn more.
  
  
We’re seeking a Director of Quality Assurance who’s ready to be part of a people-first company offering best-in-class products, exceptional training, and deep industry pride—all built to help our partners and team succeed.
  
  
**About The Role**
The Quality Assurance Director strategically leads the development, implementation, and maintenance of comprehensive quality evaluation and control systems across the organization. This includes overseeing the design and analysis of inspection and testing processes, ensuring the precision and accuracy of products and equipment, driving root cause analysis for incidents, and establishing compliance with reliability standards and documentation requirements to uphold the highest levels of product quality and operational excellence
  
  
**What You'll Accomplish**

* Strategic Oversight - Overseeing and directing the overall operations of quality assurance within a company to ensure continuous improvement and compliance. This involves defining and promoting a quality mindset across the entire company.
* Quality Management System - Developing and implementing quality management systems to ensure product and service quality, and maintaining and improving quality standards, policies, and procedures.
* Compliance & Regulatory Oversight - Ensuring compliance with industry standards, regulations, and company policies, and coordinating with regulatory bodies and external auditors.
* Quality Control, Claim Mgmt, Supplier Quality - Overseeing quality control processes to ensure products meet quality standards, and conducting regular quality audits and inspections to identify and address quality issues.This also includes establishing and enforcing quality standards, testing materials and products, and developing raw material and in-process product inspection standards.
* Continuous Improvement - Leading continuous improvement initiatives to enhance product quality and operational efficiency, and implementing best practices to reduce defects and improve processes. This can involve applying tools such as CAPA, SPC charts, Root Cause Analysis, and FMEA, and leading Six Sigma or Lean initiatives.
* Leadership & Team Development - Leading and mentoring the quality assurance team, fostering a culture of high performance and professional development, and ensuring the team has the necessary skills and resources. Responsible for generating a culture of collaboration across the organization.
* Budget & Financial Management - Achieving financial objectives by preparing the quality assurance budget, scheduling expenditures, analyzing variances, and initiating corrective actions.
* Customer Experience - Gathering customer feedback through gemba and data collection on quality andperformance, ensuring products meet or exceed customer expectations, and implementing changes based on feedback
* Demonstrate a commitment to communicating, improving and adhering to health, safety and environmental policies in all work environments and areas.
* Promote a culture of safety and exhibit these behaviors.

**What We're Looking For**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Mgmt, or related discipline from an accredited university or college.
* At least 8 y+ years of relevant quality, continuous improvement, manufacturing experience including at least 5 years management or direct/indirect leadership experience.
* 3+ years of QMS / ISO9001 or similar experience required.
* CMQ/QE, CQE, CQA are all preferred.
* Six Sigma certification preferred.

**Additional Requirements**

* Successful candidates must adhere to all safety protocols and proper use of Amrize approved Personal Protection Equipment ("PPE"), including but not limited to respirators.
* Employees that are required to wear respirators must be clean shaven where the respirator seal meets the face in order to pass the qualitative and quantitative fit tests.

**What We Offer**

* Competitive salary
* Retirement Savings: Choose from 401(k) pre-tax and/or Roth after-tax savings
* Employee Stock Purchase Plan
* Medical, Dental, Disability and Life Insurance
* Holistic Health & Well-being programs
* Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) & Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) for health and dependent care
* Vision and other Voluntary benefits and discounts
* Paid time off & paid holidays
* Paid Parental Leave (maternity & paternity)
* Educational Assistance Program

**Description**

**Company & Job Overview:**

Diality is a medical device company focused on developing solutions to improve lives impacted by kidney disease. Diality offers the Moda-flx Hemodialysis System, a user-friendly, mobile, and connected hemodialysis system designed to maximize clinical flexibility and ease-of-use for both clinical and non-clinical users. The Moda-flx Hemodialysis system combines flow rate capabilities of conventional in-center dialysis devices with a fully integrated reverse osmosis (RO) water filtration system to provide a broad range of prescriptions and meet the needs of any professional dialysis care setting.

The Vice President of Manufacturing is a strategic executive responsible for leading the end-to-end operational strategy, including manufacturing, supply chain, procurement, and logistics. The ideal candidate will scale our production capabilities, optimize global supply chain resilience, and ensure uncompromising compliance with FDA, ISO 13485, and GMP regulations. This leader will bridge the gap between R&D, product development, and commercialization to deliver high-quality, cost-effective medical devices to the market

The ideal candidate will have a proven track record in Operations leadership, particularly in a medical device, medical technology or biotechnology organization. They will possess deep expertise in talent management, organizational development, and workforce planning.

This position is an office-based position at the company’s Irvine, CA headquarters.

**Responsibilities**

**Strategic Leadership & Execution**

* Translate corporate vision into actionable operational strategies, setting short- and long-term objectives for scaling manufacturing and supply chain.
* Oversee Profit & Loss (P&L) for the operations division, managing budgets, and identifying areas for continuous cost optimization.
* Serve as a core member of the executive leadership team, collaborating cross-functionally with R&D, Quality, Regulatory, and Commercial teams.

**Manufacturing & Supply Chain Management**

* Direct all manufacturing operations (internal facilities and/or outsourced/CMO partnerships), ensuring production schedules are met with the highest standards of safety and quality.
* Oversee global supply chain, procurement, and logistics, mitigating risks related to material shortages and distribution delays.
* Implement Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies to eliminate waste, reduce lead times, and improve manufacturing efficiency.

**Quality Assurance & Regulatory Compliance**

* Partner closely with Quality/Regulatory to uphold and enforce compliance with FDA 21 CFR Part 820, ISO 13485, and other global regulatory requirements.
* Maintain a culture of compliance and continuous improvement, proactively addressing audits, CAPAs (Corrective and Preventive Actions), and non-conformances.
* Guarantee that all products are manufactured, tested, and released according to defined specifications.

**New Product Introduction (NPI) & Scaling**

* Partner closely with R&D during the design transfer phase to ensure new products are manufacturable, cost-effective, and ready for commercial scale.
* Manage capacity planning, facility expansions, and capital expenditure (CapEx) projects to support product pipeline growth.
* Build, mentor, and develop a high-performing operations team, fostering a culture of accountability, innovation, and operational excellence.

**Requirements**

**Required Skills & Abilities**

* Exceptional interpersonal and communication skills, with the ability to build trust across all levels of the organization.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities, with a focus on data-driven decision-making.
* Ability to navigate complexity and lead in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
* Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach to operational excellence.

**Education & Experience**

* Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management, Engineering (Biomedical, Mechanical, or Industrial), Business Administration, or a related technical field. Master’s degree or MBA strongly preferred.
* Minimum of 15-20 years of progressive operations leadership experience in the medical device, life sciences, or heavily regulated manufacturing industry.
* Lifecycle Track Record: At least 5 years of experience in a startup or rapid-growth environment actively guiding a complex medical device through the transition from R&D to commercial launch.
* Product Complexity: Proven technical expertise managing Class II or Class III active (electromechanical) medical devices involving fluidics, software, or sterile disposables.
* Exceptional writing, editing, and verbal communication skills.
* Demonstrated expertise in talent management, organizational development, and Operations strategy.
* Proven success in managing change and leading cross-functional teams in a global setting.

**Preferred Attributes**

* Deep expertise in Quality Management Systems (QMS), FDA regulations (cGMP), and ISO 13485.
* Strong track record of managing global or complex supply chains and contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs).
* Exceptional P&L management skills with proven ability to drive CapEx planning and cost-reduction initiatives.
* Proven capability to lead transformational change, manage risk, and foster cross-functional teamwork.

**Travel**

* Ability to occasionally travel domestically

**Physical Requirements**

* The employee may occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds.

**Working Environment**

This position primarily works in an office environment. It requires frequent sitting, standing and walking. Daily use of a computer and other computing and digital devices is required. May stand for extended periods when facilitating meetings or walking in the facilities.

This role provides leadership across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, Quality Control, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety. The Director is accountable for delivering strong performance in safety, quality, customer service, cost, productivity, and inventory while building manufacturing capabilities to support future business growth.
  
  
The successful candidate will bring strong manufacturing and technical leadership, business judgment, and experience leading complex operations in a regulated environment. This position partners closely with Quality, EH&S, R&D, Supply Chain, Finance, Legal, and business leadership to ensure reliable operations, successful new product introductions, and a resilient manufacturing network.
  
  
**How You’ll Make An Impact**

* Lead chemical manufacturing operations with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, inventory, and customer service.
* Develop and execute manufacturing strategies aligned with business requirements, capacity needs, gross margin objectives, and long-term growth.
* Lead and develop a multidisciplinary organization across Production, Materials, Chemical Development, Engineering, QC, Plant Maintenance, Regulatory, and Safety.
* Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, structured problem solving, and continuous improvement.

* Develop and execute equipment, infrastructure, automation, and capital investment strategies to improve reliability, capacity, and efficiency.
* Drive cost and productivity improvements across labor, yield, scrap, waste, material usage, manufacturing variances, and inventory.

**Richmond, CA**

For 70 years, Bio-Rad has focused on advancing the discovery process and transforming the fields of science and healthcare. As one of the top five life science companies, we are a global leader in developing, manufacturing, and marketing a broad range of high-quality research and clinical diagnostic products.
